items.title: [Feature] Container snapshot lifecycle support (Model Runner V2)
items.body:
## Overview

Consolidated replacement for #54942, #54943 and #54946, following RFC #54940. Bring the container snapshot lifecycle from `snapshot_0.30.0` to current main, targeting Model Runner V2 only.

**Draft: migration review, test fixes and hardware acceptance are not complete. Please do not merge yet.**

## Claims

- Add opt-in `--snapshot-config` and suspend/unlock/resume/status lifecycle plumbing from the serving API through EngineCore and workers.
- Reconnect frontend/EngineCore transports after container restore and coordinate scheduler KV connector teardown/reconstruction.
- Keep platform-specific device and model restoration in the companion vLLM-Ascend PR. This is external container restoration, not a replacement for main's existing startup checkpoint implementation.

## Validation

Published commit: `37af3ca801`. This exact commit has **not** passed a full regression run.

During migration, the CPU snapshot suite was run with:
```
TORCH_DEVICE_BACKEND_AUTOLOAD=0 PYTHONPATH=$PWD python -m pytest --confcutdir=tests/snapshot tests/snapshot -q --tb=short
```
Latest result on the pre-commit working tree: **1 failed, 30 passed in 11.33s**. The remaining failure is the elastic-EP router-handover test constructing EPLB configuration on a CPU platform. This is unresolved, not a passing test claim. Local ZMQ tests required running outside the filesystem/network sandbox.

No NPU end-to-end, numerical accuracy or performance results are claimed for main. The submitter will supply cold-start, original-process continuation after capture, container restore and first-request acceptance results later. Heavy local checks were stopped following WSL instability.

## Details

The original 0.30.0 branch is preserved. The new branch rebases a consolidated feature change onto main `d51a5147112a31dfbed08cfa4b774c27c34ce90d`; removed Model Runner V1 paths are not reintroduced. Existing main transport, elastic-EP and startup-checkpoint functionality is retained, but compatibility review is ongoing.

Remaining work includes completing the current V2 dependency/state audit, resolving test and style failures, checking serving API security boundaries and documenting supported deployment combinations. Snapshot lifecycle operations are privileged administrative actions and must not be exposed to untrusted callers. This draft does not claim support for every main configuration or reuse of old-release validation results.

AI assistance: OpenAI Codex assisted with migration, code changes, tests and this description; submitter review and hardware acceptance remain pending.

items.title: [Bugfix] Reject --video-pruning-rate for models without video pruning support
items.body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

`--video-pruning-rate` is silently ignored by every model that does not implement video pruning. If the model lists at least one method, vLLM rejects an unsupported `--video-pruning-method`. If it lists none, vLLM accepts any method. For example, `NemotronShortcutForConditionalGeneration`, `Qwen2VLForConditionalGeneration` and `Glm4vForConditionalGeneration` start normally with `--video-pruning-rate 0.5`, and every video keeps all of its tokens. With this PR, vLLM rejects the flag at startup for those models, as [docs/features/multimodal_inputs.md](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/docs/features/multimodal_inputs.md#video-token-pruning) already says ("Unsupported combinations are rejected at startup").

## Claims

- A multimodal model with no supported pruning methods now fails at startup with `Video pruning method 'evs' is not supported by <arch> (supported methods: none).`
- A text-only model with `--video-pruning-rate` now fails with `Video pruning is not supported by text-only model <arch>.`
- Models that implement pruning are unchanged. Every architecture that runs EVS or VidCom2 code inherits `supported_video_pruning_methods` from `SupportsMultiModalPruning` or from Qwen3-VL: Qwen2.5-VL, OpenCUA, Exaone4.5, Qwen3-VL and Qwen3-VL-MoE, InternS1Pro, Qwen3.5 and its variants, Qwen4Exp, InternS2, Cohere Compass, and Nemotron Nano VL.

## Validation

New test `test_video_pruning_requires_model_support` in `tests/config/test_multimodal_config.py`. It uses models this file already loads, and it covers both rejections, the existing unsupported-method rejection (previously untested), and a supported model.

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/config/test_multimodal_config.py -k video_pruning -q
```

Results, on this change applied to vLLM `eff4de9be` (the two hunks are identical on `main`):

```text
PR:   1 passed in 9.54s
main: E       Failed: DID NOT RAISE ValueError
      1 failed in 7.83s
```

End to end, on the same build: with `--video-pruning-rate 0.5`, `vllm serve` of a Nemotron Shortcut VL checkpoint now stops with this error:

```text
Video pruning method 'evs' is not supported by NemotronShortcutForConditionalGeneration (supported methods: none).
```

On `main`, it serves 48,875 prompt tokens per 128-frame request, the same count as without the flag.

## Details

- **Root cause:** in `ModelConfig.__post_init__`, the check `pruning_spec is not None and supported_pruning and ...` skips models whose `supported_video_pruning_methods` is empty. The flag is also never examined for text-only models, because the check sits inside `if self._model_info.supports_multimodal`.
- **Behavior change:** commands that passed `--video-pruning-rate` to a model without pruning support used to start and do nothing. Now they fail with an explicit error. For GLM-4V and Glm5Next, the flag's only previous effect was to disable encoder CUDA graphs.
- **Duplicate search:** I found no open PR or issue for this check (searched `video pruning`, `video_pruning_rate`, `EVS` across open and closed PRs). Related: vllm-project/vllm#69772 adds EVS support to Nemotron Shortcut.

items.body:
## Overview

Adds official support for OmniASR (`hf-audio/omniasr-llm-300m-v2`) through the Transformers modeling backend, as suggested by @hmellor. Related: #69320,  closes #28509.

## Claims

- `OmniASRForConditionalGeneration` is registered in `_TRANSFORMERS_SUPPORTED_MODELS` with `TransformersMultiModalForTranscription`, so the model loads without `--model-impl transformers`.
- The test registry has an example checkpoint with `min_transformers_version="5.24.1"`, the first release that contains huggingface/transformers#51100.
- The model is listed in the Transcription table of the supported models page.

## Validation

Tested on a T4 with vLLM nightly `0.34.1rc1.dev34+gd9586ca91` plus the registry change of this PR, and Transformers `main` (`5.24.0.dev0`, which includes huggingface/transformers#51100):

```bash
vllm serve hf-audio/omniasr-llm-300m-v2 --dtype half --max-model-len 4096 \
  --limit-mm-per-prompt '{"audio": 2}' \
  --attention-backend FLEX_ATTENTION \
  --attention-config.flex_attn_block_m 8 --attention-config.flex_attn_block_n 16
```

The dtype and FlexAttention options are only needed on the T4, see #69320.

```text
INFO [model.py:774] Resolved architecture: OmniASRForConditionalGeneration
INFO [base.py:148] Using Transformers modeling backend.
```

```bash
curl -s http://localhost:8000/v1/audio/transcriptions -F file=@mr_quilter.wav -F model=hf-audio/omniasr-llm-300m-v2
```

```text
{"text":"mister quilter is the apostle of the middle classes and we are glad to welcome his gospel","usage":{"type":"duration","seconds":6}}
```

I did not run the test suite locally. In CI, the new test registry entry is skipped until vLLM uses Transformers 5.24.1 (#69129).

## Details

Chat completions with audio also work (tested with one and two clips in a request). I left the model out of the Text Generation table since it only transcribes. I can add it there if you prefer.

There are no open PRs for OmniASR.

items.title: [Model][MoE] Support sequence-parallel MoE in Step3p5 and Step3p5MTP
items.body:
## Overview Wire `ParallelConfig.use_sequence_parallel_moe` through `Step3p5DecoderLayer`, `Step3p5MLP`, `Step3p5Attention`, `Step3p5Model`, and `Step3p5AMultiTokenPredictorLayer` so Step-3.5-Flash and its MTP drafter support native sequence-parallel MoE execution without model-layer monkey-patching. ## Claims - When `parallel_config.use_sequence_parallel_moe` is `False`, `Step3p5` and `Step3p5MTP` retain their existing tensor-parallel execution path unchanged. - On MoE layers with `use_sequence_parallel_moe=True`, `Step3p5Attention.o_proj` skips its internal TP `all_reduce`, `Step3p5DecoderLayer` `reduce_scatter`s post-attention states and residual shards across TP ranks, `Step3p5MLP` (`share_expert`) runs replicated (`disable_tp=True`) on each rank's token shard, and `FusedMoEBlock` executes with `is_sequence_parallel=True` and `already_sequence_parallel=True`. - Full-sequence hidden states and residuals are restored via `tensor_model_parallel_all_gather` + slice (`[:num_tokens]`) before dense decoder layers, pipeline-parallel stage handoffs, final `Step3p5Model` output, and `Step3p5AMultiTokenPredictorLayer` residual/norm output. ## Validation Tested on commit `2dc8798aaad4dcb6c10ebb031baa851b79d7f628` (branched from `main` at `2aae0e21f8ea109066080bd724fbdd27ce33a9df`) on macOS CPU (`Python 3.12.13`): ```bash VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu VLLM_PLUGINS='' HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 \ pytest tests/models/test_step3p5_sequence_parallel.py -v ``` ```text ========================= 4 passed, 1 warning in 1.78s ========================= ```
Reproducer failure on main (2aae0e21f8) before this change ```text FAILED tests/models/test_step3p5_sequence_parallel.py::test_step3p5_mlp_runs_locally_on_sequence_parallel_shard E TypeError: Step3p5MLP.__init__() got an unexpected keyword argument 'is_sequence_parallel' FAILED tests/models/test_step3p5_sequence_parallel.py::test_step3p5_decoder_layer_constructor_wires_sequence_parallel_moe[False] E AttributeError: 'Step3p5DecoderLayer' object has no attribute 'use_sequence_parallel_moe' FAILED tests/models/test_step3p5_sequence_parallel.py::test_step3p5_decoder_layer_constructor_wires_sequence_parallel_moe[True] E AttributeError: 'Step3p5DecoderLayer' object has no attribute 'use_sequence_parallel_moe' FAILED tests/models/test_step3p5_sequence_parallel.py::test_step3p5_model_and_mtp_sequence_parallel_forward_equivalence E AssertionError: assert [5, 5, 5] == [3, 5, 3] ========================= 4 failed, 1 warning in 0.44s ========================= ```
The unit suite exercises: 1. `Step3p5MLP(is_sequence_parallel=True)` numerical equivalence on sharded inputs vs. full-batch `Step3p5MLP` without TP `all_reduce`. 2. `Step3p5DecoderLayer` constructor wiring across dense and MoE layers (`o_proj.reduce_results`, `share_expert` replication, `FusedMoE.is_sequence_parallel`). 3. 2-rank (`TP=2`) lockstep numerical equivalence against `use_sequence_parallel_moe=False` across `[MoE, Dense, MoE]` transitions, odd token counts requiring padding (`num_tokens=5`), intermediate PP `IntermediateTensors` handoff (`is_last_rank=False`), final `Step3p5Model` output, and `Step3p5AMultiTokenPredictorLayer`. `tests/models/test_step3p5_sequence_parallel.py` is wired into `.buildkite/test_areas/models_basic.yaml` (`basic-models-test-other-cpu`), and staged-file `pre-commit run` (`ruff`, `mypy`, `check-test-tethering`, `check-forbidden-strings`) passed. **Pending before ready-for-review:** multi-GPU/NPU serving and `lm_eval` accuracy check on a real Step-3.5-Flash (+ MTP) checkpoint with `use_sequence_parallel_moe=True` (including `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error` on GPU). ## Details `Step3p5` mixes dense MLP layers and MoE layers (`is_moe_layer`) and pairs with `Step3p5MTP` (`Step3p5AMultiTokenPredictorLayer`). We follow the sequence-parallel transition pattern established in `kimi_k25.py`, `qwen3_next.py`, and `deepseek_mtp.py`: - **Shared experts (`Step3p5MLP`):** When `FusedMoE` runs with `is_sequence_parallel=True`, `DefaultMoERunner` / `SharedExperts` invokes `shared_experts` on each rank's token shard without a TP `all_reduce`. Passing `disable_tp=is_sequence_parallel` into `Step3p5MLP`'s `MergedColumnParallelLinear` and `RowParallelLinear` replicates the shared-expert weights (matching `DeepseekV2MLP`) so each rank computes complete hidden-dim outputs for its shard, while also remaining compatible with out-of-tree shared-expert wrappers. - **Mixed MoE/Dense transitions & MTP:** `is_sequence_parallelized` tracks whether `hidden_states` and `residual` are currently sharded across TP; transitions into dense layers, PP boundaries, final norm, and `Step3p5AMultiTokenPredictorLayer` (`self.mtp_block.use_sequence_parallel_moe`) `all_gather` and slice back to `num_tokens`. Zero-token batches (`num_tokens == 0`) keep `should_Pad_or_Shard` disabled by only entering the SP path when `num_tokens > 0`. No host-device syncs are introduced. Duplicate-work check: open Step-3.5/3.7 PRs (#38494, #48506, #49490, #49642) cover attention/model variants and bug fixes; open MoE SP PRs (#51656, #50691, #53191, #60653) target other architectures (`NemotronH`, `MiniMax-M2`, `Llama4`, `GPT-OSS`). None add sequence-parallel MoE to `Step3p5` / `Step3p5MTP`. AI assistance was used to implement and validate this draft. ---

items.title: [Model] Add MiniCPM5-15B-A2.5B support
items.body:
## Overview

Add native MiniCPM5-15B-A2.5B inference. This replaces #68748 and includes its CI and test registry fixes. AI assistance was used.

## Claims

- Implement gated GQA and FP32 sigmoid MoE routing for `minicpm5_moe`.
- Support BF16 and compressed-tensors INT4 W4A16 using vLLM's existing kernels.
- Export target hidden states for the existing DSpark proposer.

## Validation

CPU job `1791803` tested commit `9ea15f001142d5e2e7ea38f35d076886e59881fc` with the PR's Python changes over the official CUDA nightly for `9c1d45c2`. Run the command from the repository root in the test environment.

```bash
cd tests
python -m pytest -v -s -rs --junitxml=/tmp/minicpm5-after.xml \
  models/test_registry.py::test_hf_registry_coverage \
  'models/test_registry.py::test_registry_imports[MiniCPM5MoEForCausalLM]' \
  'models/test_initialization.py::test_can_initialize_large_subset[MiniCPM5MoEForCausalLM]' \
  models/test_minicpm5_moe.py
```

```text
=========================== short test summary info ============================
SKIPPED [1] models/test_initialization.py:307: Model is not available online
========================= 8 passed, 1 skipped in 4.47s =========================
```

GPU smoke tests ran at `6db175bb0b27d8300af929c69982950fbc1c5846` on one H800 (TP=1), using local checkpoints. BF16 and INT4 each completed four 48-token greedy requests with DSpark off and again with it on, using temperature 0 and seed 17. BF16 without DSpark matched the Hugging Face SDPA first token on all four prompts. Full sequences matched across DSpark modes on 4/4 BF16 prompts and 1/4 INT4 prompts.

<details>
<summary>Launch command and INT4 diagnostics</summary>

Set `MODEL_DIR` to the BF16 or INT4 checkpoint, `TOKENIZER_DIR` to the target's fast tokenizer directory, and `DSPARK_DIR` to the draft checkpoint when using DSpark.

```bash
extra=()
# For the INT4 checkpoint:
# extra+=(--quantization compressed-tensors --linear-backend marlin --moe-backend marlin)
# To enable DSpark:
# extra+=(--speculative-config "{\"method\":\"dspark\",\"model\":\"$DSPARK_DIR\",\"num_speculative_tokens\":7}")

vllm serve "$MODEL_DIR" --tokenizer "$TOKENIZER_DIR" \
  --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8000 --served-model-name MiniCPM5-15B-A2.5B \
  --dtype bfloat16 --tensor-parallel-size 1 --max-model-len 4096 \
  --max-num-seqs 8 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.80 --generation-config vllm \
  "${extra[@]}"
```

The INT4 trace showed Marlin linear and MoE kernels. With `max_model_len=512` and prefix caching disabled, INT4 greedy parity was 4/4 in eager mode and 1/4 with `torch.compile`, with CUDA Graphs either on or off. A fixed-input diagnostic found batch-dependent Marlin MoE results in 19/27 comparisons (maximum absolute difference 0.0009765625). See the [related Marlin MoE issue](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/52525).

</details>

## Details

The model reuses vLLM attention, parallel linear layers, and fused MoE. The gate computes logits in FP32, matching the [SGLang implementation](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/5be555298f396ef748f3339773881db154b11c69/python/sglang/srt/models/minicpm5.py#L250). Model tests run in Models - Basic. The unpublished checkpoint's test registry entry uses an empty HF ID and `is_available_online=False`.

items.title: [Bugfix][NIXL][HiSparse] Support mixed-device KV registration for hybrid MLA+Mamba models

labels.name: nixl
labels.description: NIXL KV connector / multi-tiered KV offloading (KVCR)

items.body:
## Overview

Fix NIXL KV cache registration failures for hybrid MLA+Mamba models when using mixed-device (`DRAM` + `VRAM`, e.g., HiSparse host pool) memory layouts.

## Claims

- Support mixed-device (`DRAM` + `VRAM`) KV cache registration and local transfer descriptor generation when `_has_mamba` is enabled alongside `_mixed_mem_types`.
- Preserve region-specific block counts (`region_num_blocks`) for Mamba layers across host/device pools with differing capacities.
- Ensure `_desc_is_dram_by_block_size` accurately covers both FlashAttention/MLA and Mamba GPU descriptors.

## Validation

- Added unit test `test_mixed_memory_hybrid_mla_mamba_local_descriptors` in `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_connector.py` verifying mixed `DRAM`/`VRAM` descriptor splitting and per-descriptor memory-type mapping on commit `217ae8fefe`.
- Validated code formatting, linting, and type checks via `pre-commit` (`ruff check`, `ruff format`, `mypy`, `check-test-tethering` passed).
- Full pytest execution deferred to Buildkite CI (`tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_connector.py`).

## Details

- **Root Cause**: In `NixlConnectorWorker` (`vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/nixl/base_worker.py`), Mamba registration assumed uniform block counts across regions, explicitly disallowed `_mixed_mem_types` when `_has_mamba` was true, and omitted Mamba GPU descriptor entries when building `_desc_is_dram_by_block_size`, causing length mismatches and assertion failures in hybrid MLA+Mamba setups with host-resident KV pools.
- **Implementation**: Adjusted `region_num_blocks` indexing for Mamba regions, removed the restrictive `_mixed_mem_types` assertion in `register_local_xfer_handler`, and appended Mamba GPU descriptor flags (`False`) to `_desc_is_dram_by_block_size`.

## Overview

Add support for `fastino/GLiDE-27B`, a Qwen3.5-based structured decision
model with an answer-code readout and recurrent depth. The implementation
supports checkpoint detection, GLiDE-specific prompts, recurrent execution,
and image processing.

A search of open vLLM PRs found no other GLiDE-27B model-support PR.
The Valkey GLIDE PR found by the keyword search concerns a separate project.

- Automatically detect GLiDE checkpoints through `decision_config.json`
  and register `GlideForSequenceClassification`.
- Support GLiDE's answer-code prompts and classification readout.
- Implement parameter-free damped Euler recurrence in a dedicated
  `GlideModel`, reusing existing D3 and Qwen3.5 components.
- Keep Qwen3Next identical to the upstream baseline and preserve all
  shared Qwen3.5 forward methods. The shared constructor changes retain
  their existing default classes.
- Apply GLiDE-specific image limits without modifying cached processors.
- Add checkpoint-selection, prompt, configuration, and recurrent-logit

items.title: [Model] Add MiniCPM5-15B-A2.5B support
items.body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Add native vLLM support for MiniCPM5-15B-A2.5B with BF16 serving, compressed-tensors INT4 W4A16 inference, and DSpark speculative decoding.

AI assistance was used. The open-PR search for MiniCPM5-15B-A2.5B model integration found this PR.

## Claims

- Register the Hugging Face model type `minicpm5_moe` and implement `MiniCPM5Model` and `MiniCPM5MoEForCausalLM`, including gated GQA and FP32 sigmoid MoE routing matching the Hugging Face and SGLang implementations.
- Pass quantization settings to vLLM's parallel Linear and FusedMoE layers. Run the INT4 checkpoint through the existing Marlin backend. Export target hidden states for the existing DSpark proposer.

## Validation

The CPU tests and GPU serving runs below used commit `6db175bb0b27d8300af929c69982950fbc1c5846`, including the FP32 router change. The environment used the official CUDA nightly for base `9c1d45c21836370104d4eb51d3b46eda20719c47` with the PR's Python changes overlaid, PyTorch 2.14.0, and Transformers 5.23.0.

```bash
.venv/bin/python tests/models/test_minicpm5_moe.py -v
```

```text
Ran 6 tests in 0.009s

OK
```

The CI placement was subsequently updated at `d6dbda2c42455c22d0aa663115dea31f5266e596`: the unit tests now run in the existing Models - Basic initialization step. YAML and CI-routing checks passed; model and test Python files are unchanged.

At `45511c9b26f557e50756c479ad818d109e561105`, one test-registry entry was added with an empty HF ID and `is_available_online=False` because the checkpoint is not public yet. CPU job 1738372 used the same official image. Ruff check and format passed. Registry coverage and model-class import remain active; checkpoint initialization is explicitly skipped. Reproduce the test selection from the repository root:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -v -s -rs \
  tests/models/test_registry.py::test_hf_registry_coverage \
  'tests/models/test_registry.py::test_registry_imports[MiniCPM5MoEForCausalLM]' \
  'tests/models/test_initialization.py::test_can_initialize_large_subset[MiniCPM5MoEForCausalLM]' \
  tests/models/test_minicpm5_moe.py
```

The same coverage test with the parent registry failed as expected; the candidate result follows:

```text
AssertionError: Please add the following architectures to `tests/models/registry.py`: {'MiniCPM5MoEForCausalLM'}
1 failed in 2.33s

SKIPPED [1] models/test_initialization.py:307: Model is not available online
8 passed, 1 skipped in 4.20s
```

On 1× NVIDIA H800 with TP=1, the four combinations of BF16 and INT4 with DSpark off/on each completed four 48-token greedy requests. Earlier-revision token comparisons were recorded diagnostically because the router computation intentionally changes. For BF16 without DSpark, the first generated token matched the Hugging Face BF16 SDPA reference on all four prompts, with top-5 overlap of 5, 5, 4, and 5. The INT4 CUDA trace contained both `marlin::Marlin` and `marlin_moe_wna16::Marlin`.

<details>
<summary>MiniCPM5-15B-A2.5B launch and generation results</summary>

Set `MODEL_DIR` to the MiniCPM5-15B-A2.5B BF16 or compressed-tensors INT4 checkpoint. Set `TOKENIZER_DIR` to the target's fast tokenizer directory and `DSPARK_DIR` to the corresponding draft checkpoint when enabling DSpark.

```bash
extra=()
# For the INT4 checkpoint:
# extra+=(--quantization compressed-tensors --linear-backend marlin --moe-backend marlin)
# To enable DSpark:
# extra+=(--speculative-config "{\"method\":\"dspark\",\"model\":\"$DSPARK_DIR\",\"num_speculative_tokens\":7}")

vllm serve "$MODEL_DIR" --tokenizer "$TOKENIZER_DIR" \
  --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8000 --served-model-name MiniCPM5-15B-A2.5B \
  --dtype bfloat16 --tensor-parallel-size 1 --max-model-len 4096 \
  --max-num-seqs 8 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.80 --generation-config vllm \
  "${extra[@]}"
```

Use `MiniCPM5-15B-A2.5B` as the API request's `model` value with the launch command above.

The generation check encoded each prompt with `add_special_tokens=False` and sent the resulting IDs to `/v1/completions` with `temperature=0`, `seed=17`, `max_tokens=48`, `ignore_eos=true`, `logprobs=5`, and `return_tokens_as_token_ids=true`. For the BF16 reference, the same IDs were fed to the checkpoint's Transformers model in BF16 with SDPA. The comparison used log-softmax of the last input token's logits.

```text
Prompt                                  HF top-1  vLLM top-1  Top-5 overlap
The capital of France is                    8181        8181              5
计算 17 + 25，结果是                          242         242              5
def add(a, b):\n    return                   280         280              4
请用一句话介绍北京。                       130073      130073              5

DSpark target  Proposed tokens  Accepted tokens  Exact token matches vs. draft off
BF16                     1008               48                                4/4
INT4                      658               98                                1/4
```

Exact greedy parity for INT4 across draft modes remains open.

Separate 1× H800 diagnostics at the same commit reproduced batch-dependent numerics in the existing Marlin MoE path. With checkpoint weights, hidden states, expert IDs, and routing weights fixed, 19 of 27 comparisons between M=1 and M=8/16/64 differed, with maximum absolute difference 0.0009765625. Repeated M=1 calls were identical. These calls bypassed both the MiniCPM5 gate and DSpark. Ordinary decoding without a draft also produced different sequences between one request and eight identical requests.

For the four prompts above, with `max_model_len=512` and prefix caching disabled, eager ordinary/DSpark runs matched 4/4 full sequences. Enabling `torch.compile` gave 1/4 matches with CUDA Graphs either enabled or disabled; the two compiled settings produced identical sequences. This confirms numerical sensitivity in existing execution paths, while not isolating every final-token difference to a single operation. No shared-kernel changes are included. See the [related upstream Marlin MoE report](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/52525).

</details>

## Details

The model classes implement attention and expert routing for MiniCPM5-15B-A2.5B using vLLM's parallel layers and fused MoE. The gate computes `F.linear(hidden_states.float(), weight.float())`, matching the [SGLang gate](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/5be555298f396ef748f3339773881db154b11c69/python/sglang/srt/models/minicpm5.py#L250). It retains the original weight and FP32 correction-bias parameters for the existing loader and MoE router. CPU tests cover FP32 computation before BF16 rounding and parameter reloads. DSpark consumes target hidden states at layers 1, 7, 13, 19, and 25 for the tested draft checkpoint. The change adds model implementation and configuration registration, a supported-model entry, and CPU configuration/router tests wired into CI.

The end-to-end serving runs used local checkpoints. The accuracy evidence covers the four generation prompts above. Full task-level accuracy, throughput, and multi-GPU execution are outside the current validation scope.

items.body:
## Overview

Serve `google/shieldgemma-2-4b-it` natively through `/classify`. The response is one score, P(Yes) that the image violates the policy in the prompt. The model is `as_seq_cls_model(Gemma3ForConditionalGeneration)` plus a `MODELS_CONFIG_MAP` entry that selects `from_2_way_softmax` over the `No`/`Yes` tokens, following `d3.py`.

Not a duplicate: no open or merged PR adds ShieldGemma 2. #7084 and #15147 are about ShieldGemma 1 (text) and are closed.

## Claims

- `vllm serve google/shieldgemma-2-4b-it --runner pooling` loads the original checkpoint and answers `POST /classify` with `probs: [P(Yes)]`. No conversion script, no `hf_overrides`, no `--chat-template`.
- Scores match the Transformers `ShieldGemma2ForImageClassification` reference on public images: prompt lengths equal on 2100/2100 image/policy pairs, agreement at 0.5 of 100% on COCO (300 pairs) and 99.33% on the C4Censor sample (1800 pairs, 489 positive).
- ~70 lines of Python plus a 33-line chat template, reusing `as_seq_cls_model` and `load_weights_using_from_2_way_softmax`.

## Validation

Tests run on this branch (H100; vLLM nightly 7c3a9302f with this branch's Python files on top, base cbb38c458):

```
pytest tests/models/multimodal/pooling/test_shieldgemma2.py      # 7 passed
pytest tests/models/test_initialization.py -k ShieldGemma2        # 1 passed
pytest tests/models/test_registry.py                              # 459 passed, 2 skipped (not ShieldGemma2)
```

Parity setup. Reference: `ShieldGemma2ForImageClassification` + `ShieldGemma2Processor`, bf16, separate process, same GPU. vLLM: this PR's files on top of upstream main 7c3a9302f, transformers 5.23.0, torch 2.14.0+cu130, NVIDIA H100 NVL, `--runner pooling --max-model-len 8192`, original JPEG sent as a data URL. Policies: the 3 defaults of `ShieldGemma2Processor` (`dangerous`, `sexual`, `violence`).

| set | pairs | ref. positives | agreement @0.5 | mean \|ΔP(Yes)\| | max \|ΔP(Yes)\| | prompt length equal |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| COCO val2017, 100 random images | 300 | 3 | 100% | 4.1e-4 | 0.037 | 300/300 |
| C4Censor sample, 600 images | 1800 | 489 | 99.33% | 6.1e-3 | 0.549 | 1800/1800 |

- COCO: 100 images drawn with `random.Random(1)` over the sorted val2017 ids. COCO is benign, so agreement says little there; the |ΔP| and length columns are the informative ones.
- C4Censor: the public preview sample (4 categories × 3 subcategories × 50 images), Dutta et al., J. Comput. Soc. Sci. 9:34 (2026), <https://doi.org/10.6084/m9.figshare.30946031> (figshare license field: CC BY 4.0). Files checked by SHA-256 against the public archive (600/600 match). Not redistributed.
- Prompt lengths equal the reference's `attention_mask` length on every pair (409 / 414 / 419 per policy), i.e. vLLM sees the same two `<bos>`.
- Max |ΔP| on C4Censor: one image carries EXIF orientation 8. vLLM applies `exif_transpose` on load; the reference's `Image.open().convert("RGB")` does not. With the reference on the rotated image the total becomes 99.39%, mean 5.8e-3, max 0.46. Details below.
- Run-to-run: two server starts with default batching differ by up to 1.3e-2 (mean 1.8e-4) over the 2100 pairs, and 1 decision flips at 0.5 (batch-dependent kernels). At `--max-num-seqs 1` two starts agree to 7.3e-9, and the hand-written classifier from alternative 3 below matches this PR to 4.5e-7, with 0 differing decisions.

### How to reproduce

The model is gated: accept the license on the Hub and set `HF_TOKEN`.

```shell
vllm serve google/shieldgemma-2-4b-it --runner pooling --max-model-len 8192
```

```shell
curl -s http://localhost:8000/classify -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{
    "model": "google/shieldgemma-2-4b-it",
    "messages": [
        {
            "role": "user",
            "content": [
                {"type": "image_url", "image_url": {"url": "https://example.com/image.jpg"}},
                {"type": "text", "text": "No Violence/Gore content: the image shall not contain content that depicts shocking, sensational, or gratuitous violence."}
            ]
        }
    ]
}'
```

Image before the policy text, one policy per request. `data[0].probs[0]` is P(Yes).

Parity script: `parity_public.py`, in the first comment of this PR. It downloads the COCO images itself; for C4Censor pass the extracted figshare archive with `--c4censor-dir`.

```shell
python parity_public.py select    ./data
python parity_public.py reference ./data
vllm serve google/shieldgemma-2-4b-it --runner pooling --max-model-len 8192 &
python parity_public.py vllm      ./data http://localhost:8000
python parity_public.py compare   ./data http://localhost:8000
```

## Details

<details>
<summary>Design and alternatives</summary>

### The two-way softmax is exact

The reference computes `softmax(logits[:, -1, [yes, no]])`. Without a final logit softcap, `softmax([a, b])[0] = sigmoid(a - b) = sigmoid((e_Yes - e_No) · h)`, with `e` the `lm_head` rows. `from_2_way_softmax` builds that one-row head from `lm_head[Yes] - lm_head[No]` in fp32 (`vllm/model_executor/models/adapters.py:592-594`). With a softcap the identity breaks (`tanh` is not linear), so `ShieldGemma2ForImageClassificationConfig` raises `ValueError` if `final_logit_softcapping` is set; the checkpoint loads, so it is not.

The head has one output row, so the classify pooler applies a sigmoid (`vllm/model_executor/layers/pooler/seqwise/poolers.py:133`). The `No`/`Yes` ids come from the tokenizer (3771 / 10784, the reference's defaults). The config entry is needed because with `convert none` `SequenceClassificationConfig` does not run (`vllm/config/vllm.py:2981-2985`).

### Alternatives considered

1. `--convert classify` on the original checkpoint:
   - (a) The name does not resolve: `_normalize_arch` tries `ShieldGemma2ForCausalLM` / `ForConditionalGeneration`, which are not registered (`vllm/model_executor/models/registry.py:1430-1454`).
   - (b) Overriding `architectures` to Gemma 3 fails: `Gemma3ProcessingInfo.get_hf_config` type-checks the config class (`vllm/multimodal/processing/context.py:262`), and `hf_overrides` changes attributes, not the class.
   - (c) Gemma 3's mapper (`gemma3_mm.py:516-523`) maps `model.language_model.` to `language_model.model.`; this checkpoint nests one level deeper and ends up as `language_model.model.model.*`.
2. Aliasing the architecture to Gemma 3 in the registry: hits (b) and (c) and changes Gemma 3 for everyone.
3. A hand-written classifier with its own head and pooler. I wrote that first. At `--max-num-seqs 1` it gives the same decisions as this adapter form and a bit-identical `score.weight`, with more code, so the adapter form won.

### Processor

`ShieldGemma2Processor` ignores `text`, builds one prompt per (image, policy) from its own template and calls `Gemma3Processor`. Here the client sends one policy per request, so vLLM uses `Gemma3Processor` (`gemma3_mm.py:85-86`); `ShieldGemma2ProcessingInfo` only changes the expected config class. Prompt lengths match on all 2100 pairs.

### Prefix-LM mask

Gemma 3 sets `is_mm_prefix_lm` on `text_config` (`gemma3_mm.py:566`), but the arch-config convertor reads `hf_config` and otherwise falls back to a model-type list (`vllm/transformers_utils/model_arch_config_convertor.py:357-370`). `"shieldgemma2"` is added to that list. On an internal set, removing the entry dropped agreement from 0.985 to 0.945.

### Chat template and `<bos>`

The reference prompt starts with two `<bos>`: the Hub template writes one and Transformers' tokenizer adds another (`add_special_tokens=True`). vLLM's chat path does not add BOS by default, so this PR adds `shieldgemma2` to `_MODEL_TYPES_OVERRIDING_TOKENIZER_CHAT_TEMPLATE` (`vllm/transformers_utils/chat_templates/registry.py:50`) with `template_shieldgemma2.jinja` (Hub template plus one leading `<bos>`), and widens that function's docstring to cover this case. A test asserts the rendered `ours == "<bos>" + hub`.

Alternative: no override, and clients send `add_special_tokens: true` (`vllm/entrypoints/pooling/base/protocol.py:297-298`). That gives the reference tokens too, but the default (`false`) then drops one `<bos>` and the score changes without any error. Measured on one COCO image: without the override the prompt is one token shorter on each policy (413 / 408 / 418) and P(Yes) changes by 1.5–2× (all scores near 0 for that image, so no decision changes). The two do not combine: override plus `add_special_tokens: true` gives three `<bos>`.

### Other changes

- `"shieldgemma2"` in `_FLOAT16_NOT_SUPPORTED_MODELS` (`vllm/config/model.py:2536`), like `gemma3`.
- Docs: `classify.md` (supported models).
- `tests/models/registry.py`: in `_SEQUENCE_CLASSIFICATION_EXAMPLE_MODELS`, next to D3 and LlamaNemotronVL. `test_common.py` only iterates `_MULTIMODAL_EXAMPLE_MODELS`, so those two are not covered there either. Happy to add a processing test for sequence-classification VLMs in a follow-up.
- The `/classify` smoke test needs a 24 GB GPU and `HF_TOKEN` with license access, like other gated examples.

### Limitations

- Tensor parallel untested. The loader indexes the local shard of the embedding, as for the existing `from_2_way_softmax` models.
- Float16 rejected; use bf16 or fp32.
- One policy per request.

</details>

<details>
<summary>C4Censor tail</summary>

The 30 pairs with the largest |ΔP| (28 images) were rerun: vLLM at `--max-num-seqs 1` twice, the reference twice in separate processes.

| comparison (30 pairs) | mean \|ΔP\| | max \|ΔP\| |
|---|---|---|
| vLLM batch 1, run 1 vs run 2 | 2.5e-4 | 7.5e-3 |
| vLLM batch 1, `--no-enable-prefix-caching`, run 1 vs run 2 | 0 | 0 |
| reference, run 1 vs run 2 | 0.049 | 0.258 |
| vLLM batch 1 vs reference | 0.137 | 0.549 |

- vLLM's own run-to-run difference at batch 1 comes from prefix caching: the three policies of an image share the image prefix, and whether a request hits the cache depends on arrival order. With prefix caching off, two runs are bit-identical; vLLM vs reference does not change (mean 0.137, max 0.549). The effect is intermittent: the 2100-pair run above gave 7.3e-9.
- `pixel_values` as computed by the reference and by vLLM are identical for 27 of the 28 images and for 28 control images with |ΔP| < 0.01. The exception is the EXIF image, which is the 0.549 pair; the reference on vLLM's pixels moves it from 0.44 to 0.98 (vLLM: 0.99).
- On these near-boundary pairs the reference disagrees with itself by mean 0.049; vLLM at batch 1 differs from it by mean 0.137. About a third of the gap is reference nondeterminism; the rest is consistent with different bf16 kernels near the boundary. Computing the reference head in fp32 instead of bf16 moves it by at most 0.056. We did not isolate it further. On the control pairs all of these are below 0.01.

</details>

---

items.title: [Model] Support EAGLE-3 aux hidden states for EXAONE 4 and DeciLM
items.body:
Exaone4ForCausalLM and DeciLMForCausalLM (Llama-Nemotron Super/Ultra) did not implement SupportsEagle3, so set_aux_hidden_state_layers() was missing and an EAGLE-3 draft (or anything else that reads auxiliary hidden states) could not be attached to these targets.

- Exaone4Model / DeciModel now use EagleModelMixin and return (hidden_states, aux_hidden_states) when aux layers are set.
- EXAONE 4 is post-LN: each decoder layer already returns the full residual stream in hidden_states, so the aux states are taken from hidden_states alone instead of hidden_states + residual.
- DeciLM is pre-norm with fused residual add; hidden_states + residual stays the residual stream across no-op attention/FFN blocks.
- Aux hidden states over pipeline parallelism are not enabled for these models (supports_aux_hidden_states_over_pp stays False).



## Overview

`Exaone4ForCausalLM` and `DeciLMForCausalLM` (Llama-Nemotron Super/Ultra, `nemotron_nas.py`) do not implement `SupportsEagle3`. Every feature that reads auxiliary hidden states from the target therefore stops at engine init in `set_eagle3_aux_hidden_state_layers` (`RuntimeError: Model does not support EAGLE3 interface`): EAGLE-3 speculative decoding and the `extract_hidden_states` speculator. This PR adds the interface to both models.

## Claims

- EXAONE 4 and DeciLM targets can be used with `method: "eagle3"` and `method: "extract_hidden_states"`.
- The aux hidden state of layer `l` is the residual stream after decoder layer `l` (`l = 0`: embeddings), the same tensor as HF transformers' `output_hidden_states[l]`, including for EXAONE 4's post-LN layers.
- Nothing changes when no aux layers are set (the default path returns `hidden_states` as before).

## Validation

Hidden states dumped by `extract_hidden_states` + `ExampleHiddenStatesConnector` are compared with HF transformers `output_hidden_states` for the same token ids (2 prompts, all prompt tokens, layers `0, 1, L/2, L-1`; layer `L` is skipped because HF applies the final norm there).

Expected (measured numbers will replace this):

| Model | TP | cos mean (min) | rel. error | norm ratio |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| LGAI-EXAONE/EXAONE-4.0-32B | 1 | ≈ 1.0 (> 0.99) | bf16 noise | ≈ 1.0 |
| nvidia/Llama-3_3-Nemotron-Super-49B-v1 | 2 | ≈ 1.0 (> 0.99) | bf16 noise | ≈ 1.0 |

- On `main` without this change, both runs are expected to fail at engine init with `Model does not support EAGLE3 interface`.
- For EXAONE 4, taking `hidden_states + residual` (the pre-norm convention) would give a norm ratio clearly above 1 against HF; the ratio check guards against that.

<details>
<summary>Reproduce</summary>

```bash
python check_aux_hidden_states.py LGAI-EXAONE/EXAONE-4.0-32B --tp 1
python check_aux_hidden_states.py nvidia/Llama-3_3-Nemotron-Super-49B-v1 --tp 2 --trust-remote-code
```

</details>

## Details

- EXAONE 4 is post-LN: `Exaone4DecoderLayer` returns the full residual stream as `hidden_states` and the pre-MLP stream as `residual`. The aux states are therefore taken from `hidden_states` alone (`residual=None` in `_maybe_add_hidden_state`). Using `hidden_states + residual`, as for pre-norm models, would add the pre-MLP stream a second time.
- DeciLM is pre-norm with a fused residual add, like Llama. `hidden_states + residual` remains the residual stream across no-op attention / FFN blocks (`HasNoOps`), so the default `_maybe_add_hidden_state` is used.
- `supports_aux_hidden_states_over_pp` stays `False` for both models, so the runner keeps rejecting these methods with pipeline parallelism; enabling it is left for a follow-up.
- Motivation: reading intermediate-layer hidden states during serving (e.g. linear probes on the residual stream) with EXAONE 4 and Llama-Nemotron targets, besides EAGLE-3 drafts.

items.body:
## Overview
Adds `LaraMiniForCausalLM` for [Lara Mini Base](https://huggingface.co/translated/Lara-4-Mini-Base), a 7.2B-total /
0.6B-active multilingual hybrid MoE base model. I'm with Translated, the developer of Lara Mini; it is the first of a
series of models we are going to develop and release (downloads are still low, as access to the checkpoint is gated).
Technical report: https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.16956.
Native Transformers support: huggingface/transformers#50819 (merged).

## Claims
- Native implementation reusing vLLM's Gated DeltaNet layer (`QwenGatedDeltaNetAttention`), `FusedMoE` with
  `GateLinear` fp32 router logits, and the hybrid KV cache. The Transformers modeling backend cannot run the GDN
  layers (`ValueError: Layer 0 (linear_attention) does not dispatch through the Transformers attention interface`;
  linear attention in the backend starts with #59224, for Mamba2).
- TP (up to 8), PP, EP, EPLB without redundant experts, chunked prefill, prefix caching (`align`) and CUDA graphs.
- LoRA (`SupportsLoRA`) on the attention, GDN and shared-expert projections, the routed experts (3D) and the
  embeddings.
- Matches the HF reference: |ΔNLL| ≤ 0.001 nats on long documents (16k tokens, and 2 × 32k tokens); GSM8K on par
  with the technical report and our earlier vLLM integration.

## Validation
H200, CUDA 13.2, torch 2.14.0, transformers 5.23.0 (as in CI), branch merged with main `5d83998e92`:
```

pre-commit run --files $(git diff --name-only main...HEAD)
  18 hooks passed, none failed
```

Usage (the repo is gated: request access on the model page and set `HF_TOKEN`):
`vllm serve translated/Lara-4-Mini-Base --trust-remote-code`

Agreement with the HF reference (Hub remote code, fp32) on the released weights, teacher-forced logprobs on 16,380
long-document tokens (4 × 4096, crossing the 512-token window); the last digit moves between runs:
| vLLM config | ΔNLL | top-1 agreement |
|---|---|---|
| HF bf16 (reference spread) | −0.0005 | 98.1 % |
| default (torch.compile + CUDA graphs) | −0.0005 | 98.4 % |
| eager | −0.0007 | 98.3 % |
| chunked prefill (256-token budget) | −0.0008 | 98.4 % |
| TP2 / TP4 / TP8 | −0.0005 / −0.0006 / +0.0004 | 98.2 / 98.1 / 98.3 % |
| TP2 + EP | −0.0004 | 98.3 % |
| TP2 + EP + EPLB (no redundant experts, rebalancing every 16 steps) | −0.0003 | 98.3 % |
| PP2 | −0.0001 | 98.3 % |

GSM8K: lm-eval 0.4.14.dev0 (`69c005f265e7`), task `gsm8k` unchanged, 5-shot, greedy, `max_gen_toks=512`, no chat
template:
| | accuracy (strict-match) |
|---|---|
| this PR | 67.3 % |
| our earlier vLLM 0.28 integration | 66.5 % |
| [technical report](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.16956), Table 7 | 67.2 % |

vLLM's own `tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py` (5-shot, 256 tokens): 63.3 %, 0 invalid.

<details>
<summary>GSM8K commands and raw output</summary>

```
vllm serve translated/Lara-4-Mini-Base --trust-remote-code --served-model-name lara --max-model-len 4096 \
  --generation-config vllm --port 8433

num_concurrent=64,tokenized_requests=False,tokenizer_backend=None,max_gen_toks=512 \

```

</details>

<details>
<summary>More validation</summary>

- Greedy (64 tokens, 14 prompts): 13 or 14 of 14 "close" (identical, or each pick in the other's top 5 at the first
  differing token) in every configuration above; the exceptions are one prompt at a token where the top 5 are within
  0.41 nats. Two 32,768-token documents: ΔNLL within +0.0008, with no drift along the sequence.
- LoRA against PEFT 0.21.2 on the native Transformers implementation (released weights): the adapter's effect on the
  logprobs agrees with a relative error of 0.14–0.21 and a correlation ≥ 0.977, the bf16 noise floor. Checked at TP1
  for 2D, routed-expert, combined, embedding and converted adapters, also with chunked prefill + prefix caching, and
  at TP2 with and without `fully_sharded_loras`; mixed-adapter batches at TP1 and TP2. Happy to add a LoRA test if
  you'd like one.
- Prefix caching: on the second pass, 1920 of 2000 prompt tokens come from the cache; outputs agree with the first
  pass up to bf16 near-ties.
- GSM8K, paired on the same 1,319 questions: 56 solved only by this PR, 45 only by the 0.28 integration (exact
  McNemar p = 0.32).
- Router: all 34 gates return fp32 logits; max relative error ≤ 1.8e-6 against an fp32 reference (batch 1–4096).
- `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error`, default and eager (mixed batch with prompts past the 512-token window, chunked prefill
  and a prefix-cache pass): no synchronization raised.

</details>

## Details
- The config comes from the Hub remote code, hence `--trust-remote-code`; a follow-up drops it once a Transformers
  release with `lara_mini` is in vLLM's supported range.
- The checkpoint fuses the GDN input projection (`in_proj`, rows `[q|k|v|z|b|a]`); `load_weights` splits it into
  `in_proj_qkvz` and `in_proj_ba`. No shared-code changes; the Qwen GDN Triton warmup does not run for this model
  (as for InternS2-Mobius).
- LoRA adapters use the split GDN names (`in_proj_qkv/z/b/a`), as in the native Transformers implementation.
  Adapters trained with the Hub remote code target the fused `in_proj` and are rejected with an error that lists the
  expected modules; the Transformers model doc in the PR above describes the conversion. Two generic limits also
  apply: an `lm_head` LoRA is not applied to `prompt_logprobs`, and a router LoRA has no effect (also for Qwen3.5 and
  Qwen3-Next).
- EPLB with `num_redundant_experts > 0` hits #67054, a generic stacked-checkpoint loader bug (fix proposed in #62918).
- Not validated: quantized checkpoints, LoRA with EP or PP. Not supported yet: sequence-parallel MoE.
- CI: the Hub repo is gated (manual approval by Translated; weights CC BY-NC-SA 4.0). No test downloads the weights,

- Validated on NVIDIA H200 only; the AMD mirror of the hybrid step (MI355) also runs the hybrid test.
- Not a duplicate: no open or closed PR or issue covers this model (searched "lara", "lara_mini", "LaraMini",

items.body:
## Overview

Hopper (SM90) support for Inkling 2 Small, for both the original (NVFP4 + MXFP8) and the MXFP8 checkpoints. Inkling 2 Small itself landed in #67325; this PR now only adds Hopper on top of main, with the Hopper code under `vllm/models/inkling2/nvidia/` like the rest of the model.

## Claims

- Inkling 2 Small runs on H100/H200 with the same accuracy as the reference: GSM8K 0.976 for both checkpoints. Image input works too.
- Blackwell is unchanged: every Hopper path is gated on `use_sm100_kernels()`.
- The PR's tile-invariance contract holds on Hopper: MoE outputs are bitwise identical across token tiles (`test_moe`).

## Validation

H200, CUDA 13.0, FlashInfer 0.7.3. These results predate the update onto main (#67325 landed). That update moves the Hopper code into the `nvidia/` layout but leaves the Hopper kernels and dispatch unchanged; it has not been re-run on H200 yet.

| Checkpoint | Setup | GSM8K (1319 questions, 0-shot, chat) | Invalid | Output throughput |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Original (NVFP4 + MXFP8) | TP4 | 0.976 | 0 | 116.7 tok/s single stream, 1471 tok/s at concurrency 128 |
| MXFP8 | TP8 | 0.976 | 0 | 2553 tok/s at concurrency 128 |

```bash
vllm serve thinkingmachines/Inkling-2-Small --tokenizer-mode inkling -tp 4 --max-model-len 16384
python tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --use-chat-completions --max-tokens 4096 \
    --temperature 0 --num-questions 1319 --max-concurrency 128
```

Tests (`tests/models/inkling2`, H200):

| Suite | Result |
|---|---|
| `test_moe.py` | 49 passed |
| `test_attention.py` | 62 passed, 24 skipped (split-KV variants of the SM100 prefill kernel) |
| `test_core_ops.py` | 30 passed |
| `test_allreduce.py` | 4 passed |
| `test_model.py` | 6 passed |
| `test_vision.py`, `test_processing.py` | 6 passed |
| `test_dspark.py` | 10 passed; the 2 multi-GPU all-reduce cases hang under pytest during Gloo process-group setup on this cluster (before any Inkling2 code runs) and pass when run directly with `GLOO_SOCKET_IFNAME=lo` at TP2 and TP4 |

## Details

Blackwell-only pieces and their Hopper replacements:

- **Attention.** `ops/attention_sm90.py` is a Triton paged attention kernel that replaces both tml_fa4 prefill and the tcgen05 decode/verify kernel (including DSpark drafts). It reads the same sheared relative logits from `attention_prologue` and applies causal and sliding-window masks itself. Each program packs GQA rows (tokens × group) for one request and KV head. KV splits are interleaved (split `s` takes blocks `s, s + S, …`), so the split count depends only on the batch and holds across CUDA graph replays. Prefill writes fp32 output and LSE where tml_fa4 did; decode writes the gated output directly or split partials for the existing combine kernel.
- **MoE.** `ops/moe_sm90.py` has the same interface as `trtllm_bmm.bmm` and reads row-major (unshuffled) expert weights plus the same tile-padded activations and block scales. Both operands are dequantized exactly (NVFP4 to fp16, MXFP8 to bf16: a value times its block scale fits in 8 significant bits), so the products match the block-scaled MMA. Weights are the MMA's M side (swap-AB), so small token tiles still fill the MMA. The per-row and per-expert fp32 scales apply to the accumulator.
- **NVFP4 activation quantization.** Hopper has no `cvt.rn.satfinite.e2m1x2`, so `ops/nvfp4.py` rounds to e2m1 in software (round to nearest even, saturating), with identical results.
- **`csrc/inkling2/conv_mix.cu`.** Scalar round-to-nearest fallbacks for `__fadd2_rn`/`__fmul2_rn`/`__ffma2_rn` and `fma.rn.f32.bf16`. The Inkling2 kernels now also build for `9.0a`, which adds one arch to these small translation units.
- **Other.** Vision attention uses FA3, small linears use cuBLAS, and the fused multicast all-reduce is enabled on SM90.

Limitations:

- MoE prefill GEMMs reach roughly 180 TFLOPS at large batches; a WGMMA-based kernel would close more of the gap. Decode is bandwidth-bound and benefits less.
- I validated with a precompiled wheel plus a separately built SM90 copy of `csrc/inkling2`, because the build host's GCC is older than 13. The `CMakeLists.txt` arch change has not been through a full source build.
- No Inkling 2 tests run in Buildkite yet (#67325 adds none). An H100 step for `tests/models/inkling2` could follow.

---

items.title: [Model] Support LoRA for Nemotron Labs Diffusion
items.body:
Stacked on #58387 (Nemotron Labs Diffusion). Isolated delta: https://github.com/pst2154/vllm/commit/03f1cc3da9

## Purpose
Serve PEFT LoRA adapters with `--enable-lora` on Nemotron Labs Diffusion, on both the masked-diffusion path and the AR path (`ar_mode` / `NemotronLabsDiffusionForCausalLM`).

- `NemotronLabsDiffusionForBlockDiffusion` implements `SupportsLoRA`; it reuses the existing `packed_modules_mapping` (`qkv_proj`, `gate_up_proj`).
- Adapters apply to the decoder linear layers (q/k/v/o, gate/up/down). The untied `diffusion_head` and the input embeddings take no adapter.
- PEFT names under the checkpoint's `encoder.` prefix are mapped by the existing `hf_to_vllm_mapper`.
- `supported_models.md`: LoRA column ✅.

## Test Plan
- CPU: `test_lora_support`: LoRA interface on both registered architectures, and PEFT `encoder.` names mapping to vLLM module names.
- GPU (`test_lora_matches_merged_weights`): a synthetic PEFT adapter (rank 8 and 16, all 7 decoder projections) served with `--enable-lora` vs. the same adapter merged into the weights, on the diffusion and AR paths; also a request without an adapter on an `--enable-lora` engine vs. a plain engine. Runs with `enforce_eager=True` and with CUDA graphs.

## Test Result
H200, BF16, nvidia/Nemotron-Labs-Diffusion-3B; `test_nemotron_dllm.py` and `tests/test_sampling_params.py` 98/98 passed (the LoRA test in eager and CUDA-graph modes). The table is from the eager runs. The whole file also passes in one pytest process (34/34, twice). With `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error`, the masked-diffusion tests stop at a host sync in the #58387 sampler (the same tests fail on #58387 alone); stacked on #60287, which removes it, all LoRA tests pass under the check.

| adapter | path | max abs logit diff, adapter vs merged | max abs diff, merged vs base | greedy tokens adapter == merged | no-adapter request on `--enable-lora` engine vs plain |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| r8  | diffusion | 0.375 | 8.70 | yes | 0.0 (identical tokens) |
| r8  | AR        | 1.406 | 9.16 | yes | 0.0 (identical tokens) |
| r16 | diffusion | 0.406 | 5.72 | yes | 0.0 (identical tokens) |
| r16 | AR        | 0.688 | 9.27 | yes | 0.0 (identical tokens) |

Without the model change the same tests fail with "LoRA is not supported for NemotronLabsDiffusionModel". pre-commit (incl. mypy) and the strict docs build pass.

items.title: [ROCm][Model] Add Inkling 2 Small support on ROCm
items.body:
## Overview ROCm support for Thinking Machines' [Inkling 2 Small](https://huggingface.co/thinkingmachines/Inkling-2-Small) and its DSpark speculator, which #67325 added for NVIDIA. This PR runs both on AMD Instinct MI355X (gfx950) with the all-MXFP8 checkpoint [`thinkingmachines/Inkling-2-Small-MXFP8`](https://huggingface.co/thinkingmachines/Inkling-2-Small-MXFP8). The ROCm implementation lives under `vllm/models/inkling2/amd/`, and package dispatch selects it on ROCm. NVIDIA's model and kernel files are unchanged. **Reviewing:** one commit, 29 files, +6,535/−161. Most of that is `vllm/models/inkling2/amd/` (6,052 lines), and 80% of its lines are unchanged copies of the NVIDIA module each file mirrors. The ROCm-specific code is about 1,150 new or changed lines, 690 of them in the Triton attention (`amd/ops/attention.py`) and the MXFP8 grouped GEMM (`amd/ops/triton_bmm.py`). The rest of the commit is tests (+412/−147) and +71/−14 in shared files and docs. ## Claims - Inkling 2 Small serves on 4x MI355X (TP4) with DSpark (7 draft tokens), full decode CUDA graphs, image input, and the reasoning and tool-call parsers. The KV cache holds 1.9M tokens, so a 1M-token request fits. - The MXFP8 experts run on a Triton `tl.dot_scaled` grouped GEMM. Attention is a Triton relative-bias kernel whose decode and verify path splits the keys across idle compute units (split-KV). - Accuracy: GSM8K is 94.8% strict with DSpark and 95.2% without. MMMU-Pro is within one standard error of #67325's numbers, and NIAH passes all 550 cases from 4K to 1M tokens. - Decode step time stays flat with context: 10.3 ms at 1K and 10.7 ms at 100K tokens without speculation, 13.7 and 14.2 ms with DSpark. - No HIP/C++ kernels, and no changes to the scheduler, KV-cache manager, model runner, attention backends or NVIDIA's Inkling 2 files. **UPDATE**: Pushed fixes for four issues an additional review found in the ROCm attention and MoE code, plus a mixed-batch latency fix:
Fixes in 2a53fd71f

1. **Weight reloads left full decode graphs on the old relative projection.** `process_weights_after_loading` rebound `rel_proj_shifted` to a new tensor, but full decode CUDA graphs keep reading the address they captured. The tensor is now allocated once and refilled in place with `copy_()` on reload. `test_inkling2_reload_refills_rel_proj` checks that the address stays the same and the values follow the new weights. End to end on 4x MI355X with full decode graphs, after adding per-layer noise to `rel_logits_proj` and reloading, graph decodes and prefills of the same text agree on 98.0% of greedy tokens (mean logprob gap 0.031); before the fix, 75.4% (gap 0.71). 2. **An expired KV-cache value could turn live attention outputs into NaN.** With a sliding window, the kernel rounded its first key down to a block boundary and masked the expired scores, but still loaded their keys and values, so a NaN in a freed page reached the output through 0 × NaN. The loop still starts on a block boundary; the page and K/V load masks now use the exact window start. `test_inkling2_window_skips_expired_pages` fills the expired slots with NaN. 3. **Prefill and mixed-batch padding could come out NaN.** `gated_rel_attention` zeroed the padded rows of its intermediate output, then ran `gate_sink` over every row, so NaN gates on padding produced NaN. `gate_sink` now takes `cu_seqlens_q` and writes zeros after its last entry without reading the inputs, the same guard as the split-decode merge. `test_inkling2_gated_rel_attention_zeroes_padding` puts NaN in the padded gates. 4. **The MXFP8 grouped GEMM accepted strided activations.** `bmm` validated only the weights, but it addresses the activations and their scales as packed rows. It now asserts the activation dtype, shape and contiguity, and contiguous `uint8` scales of shape `[rows, K // 32]`. Both MoE callers already pass packed tensors, so outputs don't change. **Mixed batches:** at the 6:1 GQA ratio, one prefill in a batch disabled split-KV for every decode request in it. The metadata builder now records the decode/prefill split, and the leading decode and verify requests run on `rel_decode_attention`, as on the NVIDIA path, with the rest on `gated_rel_attention`. With four 100K-context streams decoding while short prompts arrive, the p90 decode step during prefills drops from 167 ms to 81 ms without speculation and from 174 ms to 83 ms with DSpark; short-prompt latency (p50) drops from 191 ms to 105 ms and from 215 ms to 120 ms. `test_inkling2_mixed_batch_splits_leading_decodes` checks a mixed batch against the reference. Validation on 4x MI355X (TP4, EP4): | Check | Before | After | |---|---|---| | `tests/models/inkling2` (skips: CUDA-only and Inkling 2 Mini cases) | 204 passed, 103 skipped | 232 passed, 103 skipped | | The new tests | 7 failed, as expected | passed | | Repeated runs of `tests/models/inkling2` | 3 of 3 passed | 32 of 32 passed | | The new tests under 64 shifted seeds | | all passed | | GSM8K 5-shot, strict / flexible, DSpark | 94.84 / 97.27 | 95.15 / 97.27 | | GSM8K 5-shot, strict / flexible, no speculation | 95.15 / 97.12 | 94.54 / 97.42 | | NIAH | | 440/440 from 4K to 256K; 10/10 at 1M, depth 50 | | Decode ITL at 1K / 100K, no speculation | 10.31 / 10.71 ms | 10.32 / 10.75 ms | | Decode ITL at 1K / 100K, DSpark | 13.66 / 14.24 ms | 13.82 / 14.37 ms | | p90 decode step during prefills, no speculation / DSpark | 167.1 / 173.8 ms | 80.6 / 83.2 ms | The GSM8K differences are within noise (the standard error is about 0.6 points per run). Findings 1 and 3 have the same pattern in `nvidia/` (the shifted projection is rebound on reload, and the prefill epilogue gates padded rows unguarded), and the NVIDIA window loop also loads the expired keys of its first block.

### Serving command ```bash vllm serve thinkingmachines/Inkling-2-Small-MXFP8 \ --served-model-name inkling2 \ --tensor-parallel-size 4 \ --max-model-len 1048576 \ --max-num-seqs 256 \ --reasoning-parser inkling \ --tool-call-parser inkling \ --enable-auto-tool-choice \ --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":7,"draft_sample_method":"probabilistic"}' ``` ## Validation **Setup:** 4x AMD Instinct MI355X (gfx950), TP4 with DSpark unless noted. Nothing was run on NVIDIA hardware. | Check | Result | |---|---| | `pytest tests/models/inkling2` on one GPU | 204 passed, 103 skipped (CUDA-only and Inkling 2 Mini cases), in 3 of 3 runs | | `test_model.py` with `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error` | 9 passed, 12 skipped | | `pre-commit` on the changed files: Ruff, mypy, typos, markdownlint and the `tools/pre_commit` checks | Pass | | Serving smoke test: text with reasoning, image, tool call, tool result, streamed tool call | 5/5, with and without DSpark | | Eval | This PR (MI355X, TP4) | #67325 (NVIDIA) | |---|---:|---:| | GSM8K, 1,319 questions, strict / flexible | 94.84% / 97.27% (± 0.61 / 0.45) | not reported | | GSM8K without speculation | 95.15% / 97.12% (± 0.59 / 0.46) | not reported | | MMMU-Pro standard-10, first 150 | 86.0% | 86.0% | | MMMU-Pro vision, first 150 | 85.3% | 84.7% | | NIAH 4K to 256K, 440 cases | 440/440 | 440/440 (TP8) | | NIAH 1M, 110 cases | 110/110 | 110/110 (TP8) | GSM8K is 5-shot chat, greedy, reasoning effort none. Before the rebase it was 95.00% / 97.19% with DSpark, and 95.22% / 97.42% and 94.92% / 97.19% in two runs without. DSpark's mean acceptance length during GSM8K is 4.4 of 7. MMMU-Pro (T=1, effort max) and NIAH (T=0) use [inkling-verify](https://github.com/thinking-machines-lab/inkling-verify), as in #67325. #67325's MMMU-Pro numbers are on the main checkpoint rather than MXFP8; at n=150 the standard error is about 3 points. ### Performance Decode step time (median gap between streamed chunks, one chunk per step) for one request with a random prompt and 512 output tokens. "Without split-KV" is the same build with one attention program per request and KV head. | Context | No speculation | DSpark | No speculation, without split-KV | DSpark, without split-KV | |---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | 1K | 10.3 ms | 13.7 ms | 13.6 ms | 18.1 ms | | 8K | 10.4 ms | 13.7 ms | 17.1 ms | 23.0 ms | | 32K | 10.5 ms | 13.9 ms | 29.2 ms | 39.3 ms | | 100K | 10.7 ms | 14.2 ms | 63.5 ms | 85.4 ms | For reference, #67325 reports 4.8 ms at 100K on GB200. Time to first token for a fresh prompt is 83 / 300 / 1,264 / 5,064 ms at 1K / 8K / 32K / 100K without speculation, and 93 / 313 / 1,287 / 5,096 ms with DSpark. SPEED-Bench v1.1 `throughput_1k` without the gated `cais/hle` rows (1,282 prompts), 1,024 output tokens: | Concurrency | No speculation (tok/s) | DSpark (tok/s) | Acceptance length | |---:|---:|---:|---:| | 1 | 96.9 | 241 | 3.41 | | 4 | 345 | 616 | 3.49 | | 16 | 880 | 1,512 | 3.50 | | 64 | 2,210 | 3,377 | 3.31 | These are single runs after a warm-up on the same prompts, so they measure decode, not prefill.
Benchmark commands ```bash # Decode step vs context, LEN in 1024 8192 32768 102400 vllm bench serve --backend openai-chat --endpoint /v1/chat/completions --base-url http://127.0.0.1:8000 \ --model inkling2 --tokenizer thinkingmachines/Inkling-2-Small-MXFP8 --tokenizer-mode inkling \ --dataset-name random --random-input-len $LEN --random-output-len 512 --ignore-eos \ --max-concurrency 1 --num-prompts 3 --seed 0 # TTFT: the same with --seed $LEN on a fresh server, after one prompt with --seed $((LEN + 1)). Random # prompts with the same seed share leading tokens, so --seed 0 at every length hits the prefix cache. # SPEED-Bench, C in 1 4 16 64; N is 16 below concurrency 4, else 4 * C. throughput_1k.jsonl is # Model-Optimizer's examples/specdec_bench preparation of v1.1 without cais/hle, as {"messages": [...]} rows. vllm bench serve --backend openai-chat --endpoint /v1/chat/completions --base-url http://127.0.0.1:8000 \ --model inkling2 --tokenizer thinkingmachines/Inkling-2-Small-MXFP8 --tokenizer-mode inkling \ --dataset-name speed_bench --dataset-path /path/to/speed-bench --speed-bench-dataset-subset throughput_1k \ --speed-bench-output-len 1024 --max-concurrency $C --num-prompts $N --seed 0 ```
## Details - **Vendor ownership:** ROCm code is under `vllm/models/inkling2/amd/` and imports nothing from NVIDIA's modules. `configs.py`, `processing.py`, `quant_config.py` and the speculator modules stay shared. - **Platform dispatch:** `vllm.models.inkling2` resolves its exports by platform, lazily, since `transformers_utils` imports `inkling2.configs` early. `rocm.py` lists `inkling2` as a supported quantization, and the shared `Inkling2QuantConfig` maps the checkpoint's `quant_method: fp8` to it on both platforms. - **MoE:** MXFP8 experts only, in the checkpoint layout, on a `tl.dot_scaled` grouped GEMM (`amd/ops/triton_bmm.py`). Other expert formats raise at model construction. - **Attention:** Triton relative-bias attention (`amd/ops/attention.py`) behind NVIDIA's entry points, with `main`'s KV-cache layer configs. Decode and verify batches split the keys and merge fp32 partials, with a split count that depends only on the batch shape, so it is safe under CUDA graphs. Prefill and mixed batches use query tiles. - **Other ROCm paths:** vision attention uses CK flash-attention through `fa_utils`. DSpark's argmax (all-gathered logits, then `greedy_argmax`) and its `refresh_derived_weights` are the same code as on CUDA. - **Not on ROCm:** NVFP4, PDL, inline PTX, FlashInfer, FA4, the NVLink multicast paths (fused all-reduce, sequence parallelism, `conv_mix`), LoRA, routed-experts capture, and Inkling 2 Mini (`Inkling2LoopForConditionalGeneration`). Mini and gfx942 are rejected at model construction. - **Duplication:** 80% of the 6,052 lines in `amd/` match the NVIDIA file they mirror, as in Beam and Inkling v1, because every NVIDIA module has CUDA-only code. About 1,150 lines are new or changed, 690 of them in `ops/attention.py` and `ops/triton_bmm.py`. Moving the shared parts into `inkling2/common/` is left to a follow-up once #63510 settles that pattern for Beam. The closest copies are `vision.py`, `ops/vision.py`, `ops/sconv.py`, `ops/attn_res.py`, `ops/norm.py`, `ops/mxfp8.py`, `ops/dspark.py` and `dspark.py`: about 2,900 lines, with at most 35 ROCm-specific lines each. - **Tests:** NVIDIA's test files import ops from the package and skip CUDA-only cases on ROCm. These changes reach CUDA and were not run there: `test_moe.py` loads its modules through `import_module` (same cases, same order); `test_inkling2_rel_attention` takes the ROCm kernel first and keeps `main`'s SM100 and Hopper branches; `test_vision.py` gates on `is_device_capability` instead of the major version (the same CUDA GPUs); and `test_core_ops.py`'s `_dense_conv` reference sums taps in the kernel's order, since the old order misses the tolerance in 3 of 800 seeded cases on gfx950. The last needs an ack from #67325's authors. - **Known gaps:** new prefill sizes keep compiling `_route_tokens_kernel` variants (0.7 to 1.2 s each until cached; the constexpr is inherited from CUDA). The Rust frontend was not built. - **Footprint:** 6,535 additions and 161 deletions across 29 files: 6,052 lines in `amd/`, +412/−147 in tests and +71/−14 elsewhere. AI assistance was used.

items.title: [Model][ROCm][Inkling]: Add support for Lamport P2P(hip kernels) collective on ROCm/AMD
items.body:
## Overview Add Lamport P2P Collective support back on ROCm with hip kernels and ipc buffers. ## Claims Previous Lamport P2P code used triton kernels and pytorch symmetric memory. However, that stack didn't have proper support for memory semantics required by Lamport P2P and caused deadlocks. The PR adds support back using hip kernels and ipc buffers without any deadlocks while preserving the accuracy. ## Details Enabling lamport P2P is a critical optimization for Inkling model. It reduces decode time. Note: this is already enabled by default on Nvidia side, but the original implementation didn't work on AMD/RoCm If Lamport P2P collective isn't used, then RCCL library kernels are used. Inkling model involves collective communication post attention and moe op. The pipeline is this ReduceScatter -> sconv(short convolution) on shards -> AllGather -> fused add(+rmsnorm). With RCCL calls, this results in two collective ops Reduce Scatter and AllGather. By using Lamport P2P collective mechanism the overall time of this pipeline is reduced. It still involves 4 kernels, but relies on spin-wait mechanism between GPU peers and uses a sentinel value as part of data payload for synchronization. The following traces from a decode step show the perf. improvement. **Lamport-OFF** **Lamport-ON** **1. items.title: [CPU] Support prompt embeds in the standalone CPU model runner
items.body:
## Overview

`--enable-prompt-embeds` no longer starts on CPUs that use the standalone CPU model runner (no Triton: Arm, s390x, POWER, macOS arm64). The runner from #61995 lists prompt embeddings as unsupported, and since #63373 removed MRv1 that is a startup error instead of a fallback:

```
Value error, The CPU model runner without Triton does not yet support: prompt embeddings
```

This ports prompt embeds to `vllm/v1/worker/cpu/`, following the GPU MRv2 implementation.

## Claims

- `enable_prompt_embeds` works on the standalone CPU model runner, for pure `prompt_embeds` prompts and for chat prompts that mix text with `prompt_embeds` parts.
- Chunked prefill, requests past their embeddings (decode), and the `prompt_is_token_ids` mask behave as on GPU.
- `prompt_embeds` content parts sent together with image/audio parts are passed through the CPU encoder runner, as on GPU.
- No change for runs without `--enable-prompt-embeds`.

## Validation

MacBook Air M2 (8 GB), macOS arm64, CPU build, `StandaloneCPUModelRunner`. Base `75be5c391`.

**Existing end-to-end test, before and after** (`facebook/opt-125m`; the token-id run is checked against HF, and the run from HF input embeddings against the token-id run, both with `check_logprobs_close`):

```
pytest -x -v -s 'tests/models/language/generation/test_common.py::test_models[True-False-5-32-facebook/opt-125m]'
```

| | Result |
|---|---|
| main | `1 failed in 10.71s`: `Value error, The CPU model runner without Triton does not yet support: prompt embeddings` |
| this PR | `1 passed in 37.18s` |

This PR adds that test ID to the Arm CPU job (`run-cpu-test-arm.sh`), which already downloads `opt-125m`. No job ran prompt embeds on a non-Triton CPU before.

**Hybrid model, mixed prompts, and the multimodal path** (`Qwen/Qwen3.5-0.8B`, bf16, `MambaHybridModelState`; needs #65320 applied locally, because Qwen3.5 does not load on macOS CPU on main). Embeddings come from the model's own `embed_input_ids`, so the output must equal the token-id run. "Text-only" is `language_model_only=True`; "multimodal" is the default, where the overlay lands on the encoder runner's buffer. Each cell holds for both the default `max_num_batched_tokens` and 16, where the embedding span crosses a chunk boundary:

| Prompt | Text-only | Multimodal |
|---|---|---|
| 3 pure `prompt_embeds` prompts (5, 4, 294 tokens) | identical tokens, max \|Δ logprob\| 0.0 | identical tokens, max \|Δ logprob\| 0.0 |
| chat: text + 17-token `prompt_embeds` part + text (46 tokens) | identical tokens, max \|Δ logprob\| 0.0 | identical tokens, max \|Δ logprob\| 0.0 |

Δ logprob is over the sampled token at each generated step (up to 24).

<details>
<summary>Script and commands for the Qwen3.5 runs</summary>

```
VLLM_CPU_KVCACHE_SPACE=1 VLLM_ENABLE_V1_MULTIPROCESSING=0 python check_prompt_embeds.py Qwen/Qwen3.5-0.8B
VLLM_CPU_KVCACHE_SPACE=1 VLLM_ENABLE_V1_MULTIPROCESSING=0 python check_prompt_embeds.py Qwen/Qwen3.5-0.8B 16
VLLM_CPU_KVCACHE_SPACE=1 VLLM_ENABLE_V1_MULTIPROCESSING=0 python check_prompt_embeds.py Qwen/Qwen3.5-0.8B --multimodal
VLLM_CPU_KVCACHE_SPACE=1 VLLM_ENABLE_V1_MULTIPROCESSING=0 python check_prompt_embeds.py Qwen/Qwen3.5-0.8B 16 --multimodal
```

Each run prints, for example:

```
StandaloneCPUModelRunner MambaHybridModelState supports_mm_inputs=True
pure: prompt_tokens=5 same_tokens=True max_dlogprob=0.00000
pure: prompt_tokens=4 same_tokens=True max_dlogprob=0.00000
pure: prompt_tokens=294 same_tokens=True max_dlogprob=0.00000
mixed, embeds at [7, 24): prompt_tokens=46 same_tokens=True max_dlogprob=0.00000
```

```python
import base64
import io
import sys

import torch

from vllm import LLM, SamplingParams

PROMPTS = [
    "The capital of France is",
    "def fibonacci(n):",
    "Summarize: "
    + " ".join(f"Paragraph {i}: the river carried silt past the old mill." for i in range(20)),
]
PHRASE = " The Eiffel Tower is in Paris, and the Colosseum is in Rome."
PARAMS = SamplingParams(max_tokens=24, temperature=0, logprobs=3)


def compare(name, out, ref):
    tokens = list(out.outputs[0].token_ids)
    delta = max(
        abs(a[t].logprob - b[t].logprob)
        for a, b, t in zip(out.outputs[0].logprobs, ref.outputs[0].logprobs, tokens)
        if t in b
    )
    print(
        f"{name}: prompt_tokens={len(ref.prompt_token_ids)} "
        f"same_tokens={tokens == list(ref.outputs[0].token_ids)} max_dlogprob={delta:.5f}"
    )


if __name__ == "__main__":
    # usage: check_prompt_embeds.py MODEL [MAX_NUM_BATCHED_TOKENS] [--multimodal]
    args = [arg for arg in sys.argv[2:] if arg != "--multimodal"]
    kwargs = {"max_num_batched_tokens": int(args[0])} if args else {}
    llm = LLM(
        sys.argv[1],
        language_model_only="--multimodal" not in sys.argv,
        dtype="bfloat16",
        max_model_len=1024,
        max_num_seqs=4,
        enforce_eager=True,
        enable_prompt_embeds=True,
        **kwargs,
    )
    tokenizer = llm.get_tokenizer()
    core = llm.llm_engine.engine_core.engine_core
    runner = core.model_executor.driver_worker.worker.model_runner
    print(
        type(runner).__name__,
        type(runner.model_state).__name__,
        f"supports_mm_inputs={runner.supports_mm_inputs}",
    )

    def embed(ids):
        with torch.inference_mode():
            return runner.model.embed_input_ids(torch.tensor(ids)).clone()

    # Pure prompt_embeds: the model's own embeddings must reproduce the token-id run.
    ids = [tokenizer.encode(p) for p in PROMPTS]
    refs = llm.generate([{"prompt_token_ids": i} for i in ids], PARAMS, use_tqdm=False)
    outs = llm.generate([{"prompt_embeds": embed(i)} for i in ids], PARAMS, use_tqdm=False)
    for out, ref in zip(outs, refs):
        compare("pure", out, ref)

    # Mixed chat prompt: text, a prompt_embeds part, then text.
    phrase_ids = tokenizer.encode(PHRASE, add_special_tokens=False)
    buffer = io.BytesIO()
    torch.save(embed(phrase_ids), buffer)
    content = [
        {"type": "text", "text": "Read this sentence:"},
        {"type": "prompt_embeds", "data": base64.b64encode(buffer.getvalue()).decode()},
        {"type": "text", "text": "Which city has the Colosseum? Answer in one word."},
    ]
    out = llm.chat(
        [{"role": "user", "content": content}],
        PARAMS,
        use_tqdm=False,
        chat_template_kwargs={"enable_thinking": False},
    )[0]
    # The rendered prompt has one placeholder id per embedding row. Put the
    # phrase's token ids back to get the token-id reference.
    prompt_ids, n = list(out.prompt_token_ids), len(phrase_ids)
    start = next(
        i for i in range(len(prompt_ids) - n + 1) if len(set(prompt_ids[i : i + n])) == 1
    )
    ref_ids = prompt_ids[:start] + phrase_ids + prompt_ids[start + n :]
    ref = llm.generate([{"prompt_token_ids": ref_ids}], PARAMS, use_tqdm=False)[0]
    compare(f"mixed, embeds at [{start}, {start + n})", out, ref)
```

</details>

**Unit tests:**

```
pytest tests/v1/worker/cpu/test_cpu_prompt_embeds.py tests/v1/worker/cpu/test_cpu_encoder_runner.py
```

| | Result |
|---|---|
| this PR | `15 passed` |
| new tests against main's `vllm/` | `1 failed, 8 passed, 6 errors`: the 6 errors are the same `does not yet support: prompt embeddings` error when building the config, and the failure is `assert ['embeds', 'image'] == ['image']` in the encoder runner |

The new state tests run against both a text-only and a multimodal `DefaultModelState`.

`pre-commit run --files <changed files>` passes.

Not run: Linux Arm, s390x and POWER (no hardware), and a `prompt_embeds` part together with an image or audio part end to end (unit-tested only).

## Details

**What is ported.** The CPU files mirror the GPU ones, as in #61995:

- `cpu/model_states/prompt_embeds.py`: `PromptEmbedsState`. The GPU version overlays rows with a Triton kernel through a pointer table. Here the overlay is a torch copy (`torch.where` for the `prompt_is_token_ids` mask). When no live request has prompt embeds it returns immediately; otherwise it visits only the requests that still have embedding rows in this step. It reads `input_batch.num_computed_tokens_np`, which the CPU batch already carries.
- `DefaultModelState`, the `supports_prompt_embeds` flag, the check in `init_model_state`, `EncoderOnlyModelState`, and `uses_inputs_embeds` in the runner follow the GPU code.
- `EncoderRunner.prepare_mm_inputs`: the `prompt_embeds` passthrough branch from the GPU encoder runner. Without it, a `prompt_embeds` part next to an image would be sent to the multimodal encoder.
- `"prompt embeddings"` is removed from `_get_standalone_cpu_model_runner_unsupported_features`.

**Docs.** The Feature x Hardware table in `docs/features/README.md` already lists prompt-embeds as supported on CPU, so there is nothing to update.

**Not a duplicate.** I searched open PRs and issues for `prompt embeds CPU`, `prompt_embeds standalone`, `enable-prompt-embeds Triton` and `PromptEmbedsState`, and checked open PRs touching `vllm/v1/worker/cpu/model_states/`. None adds prompt embeds to the CPU runner.

cc @fadara01 @bigPYJ1151 @njhill

AI assistance was used to investigate and write this change. I reviewed every changed line and ran the validation above on my M2.
