items.title: [Model] Support sequence parallelism with pipeline parallelism for Qwen3-Next, Qwen3.5 and DeepSeek-V2/V3

labels.name: ready
labels.description: ONLY add when PR is ready to merge/full CI is needed

items.body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Enable sequence-parallel MoE (SP) with pipeline parallelism (PP) for Qwen3-Next, Qwen3.5, and models using `DeepseekV2DecoderLayer`: DeepSeek-V3/R1, Kimi-K2, DeepSeek-V2, Mistral Large 3, and the DeepSeek MTP drafter.

With DP > 1, TP > 1, and EP, these models keep token shards on each TP rank between layers. They currently disable this optimization under PP because the next stage expects full-token tensors replicated across TP ranks. This PR restores that layout with an all-gather at each non-last stage's exit, then re-shards where needed in the next stage, following DeepSeek-V4 (#65766) and MiniMax-M3 (#65537).

Credit to @AceCoder0 for first enabling this combination in #53191 (last updated 2026-08-21). This PR also covers `vllm/models/qwen3_5/nvidia/model.py` and keeps SP enabled for small batches. #53191 added a small-batch all-reduce fallback for Qwen3-Next after observing NaNs on Ascend; on CUDA, Qwen3-Next and Qwen3.5 match the SP-off baseline in concurrency-1 GSM8K without that fallback.

## Claims

- Enable SP under PP for Qwen3-Next, Qwen3.5, and DeepSeek-V2/V3 with DP > 1, TP > 1, and EP.
- GSM8K scores are within run-to-run noise of PP1 with SP. Prompt-logprob differences from PP1 are no larger than those of PP2 on main.
- Qwen3.5 throughput is comparable to main. DeepSeek-V2-Lite and Qwen3-Next decode throughput is about 4% lower than main; DeepSeek-V2-Lite shows a similar SP decode cost at PP1, so PP now has the same trade-off as PP1.
- Qwen3.5 MTP under PP with SP achieves comparable GSM8K accuracy and acceptance length to PP1 with SP.
- PP1 behavior is unchanged.

## Validation

B300, TP2 × DP2 + EP with `allgather_reducescatter`, which enables SP wherever the model allows it. PP1 uses 4 GPUs; PP2 uses 8. Models: `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1`, `Qwen/Qwen3.5-35B-A3B` (`--language-model-only`), `Qwen/Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B-Instruct-FP8`, `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat`.

**GSM8K.** Each cell reports concurrency 64 / concurrency 1: all 1319 questions at concurrency 64, and the first 100 at concurrency 1.

| Model | PP1, SP on | PP2, main (SP off) | PP2, this PR (SP on) |
|---|---|---|---|
| DeepSeek-R1 | 0.951 / – | 0.955 / – | 0.953 / – |
| Qwen3.5-35B-A3B | 0.860 / 0.900 | 0.845 / 0.890 | 0.851 / 0.890 |
| Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B | 0.859 / 0.870 | 0.856 / 0.880 | 0.860 / 0.880 |
| DeepSeek-V2-Lite | 0.635 / 0.630 | 0.649 / 0.690 | 0.635 / 0.630 |

DeepSeek-R1 was tested only at concurrency 64. A DeepSeek-V2-Lite rerun on the first 200 questions at concurrency 1 scored 0.645 at PP1 with SP and 0.660 at PP2 on main, a difference of less than one standard error (about 0.034).

**Prompt logprobs.** Six fixed prompts, scored twice per server through `/v1/completions` with `prompt_logprobs: 0`. Values are mean |Δ logprob| relative to the first PP1 run:

| Model (positions) | PP1, SP on, second run | PP2, main (SP off) | PP2, this PR (SP on) |
|---|---|---|---|
| DeepSeek-R1 (412) | 0.0349 | 0.0894, 0.0743 | 0.0643, 0.0541 |
| Qwen3.5-35B-A3B (438) | 0.0098 | 0.0233, 0.0184 | 0.0035, 0.0233 |
| Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B (432) | 0.0436 | 0.0503, 0.0513 | 0.0388, 0.0499 |
| DeepSeek-V2-Lite (460) | 0.0011 | 0.0405, 0.0419 | 0.0287, 0.0262 |

For Qwen3.5, the second PP2 run with this PR is byte-identical to the first PP2 run on main.

**Throughput.** Output tok/s at PP2 × TP2 × DP2, with runs interleaved as main → this PR → main → this PR:

| Model | Workload (in/out, concurrency) | main (SP off) | This PR (SP on) |
|---|---|---|---|
| DeepSeek-V2-Lite | decode 512/512, c64 | 6979, 7381 | 6728, 7088 |
| | mixed 2048/256, c64 | 6906, 7100 | 7141, 6407 |
| | prefill 8192/16, c8 | 347.3, 340.2 | 339.3, 340.1 |
| Qwen3.5-35B-A3B | decode 512/512, c64 | 5517 | 5650, 5608 |
| | mixed 2048/256, c64 | 6129 | 6335, 6132 |
| | prefill 8192/16, c8 | 271.4 | 277.6, 286.1 |
| Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B | decode 512/512, c64 | 5081, 5051 | 4830, 4870 |
| | mixed 2048/256, c64 | 5519, 5382 | 5319, 5424 |
| | prefill 8192/16, c8 | 190.7, 194.9 | 199.2, 210.4 |

The second Qwen3.5 main run failed to start because the DP coordinator timed out; it was not repeated.

**SP at PP1.** DeepSeek-V2-Lite output tok/s at PP1 × TP2 × DP2, with SP-off and SP-on runs interleaved. SP was disabled through a local edit to the decoder-layer gate:

| Workload | SP off | SP on |
|---|---|---|
| decode 512/512, c64 | 10520, 10612 | 10131, 10087 |
| mixed 2048/256, c64 | 8355, 8217 | 8015, 7952 |

**MTP speculative decoding.** `{"method": "mtp", "num_speculative_tokens": 2}`, tested on all 1319 GSM8K questions at concurrency 64. Acceptance metrics come from the spec-decode counters over each GSM8K run:

| Model | Config | GSM8K | Acceptance rate | Mean acceptance length |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen3.5-35B-A3B | PP1, SP on | 0.851 | 0.888 | 2.777 |
| | PP2, this PR (SP on) | 0.853 | 0.890 | 2.779 |
| Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B | PP1, SP on | 0.859 | 0.877 | 2.755 |

Qwen3-Next MTP fails to start under PP on both main and this PR: the drafter branches on PP rank and fails `assert intermediate_tensors is not None` on the last stage. #66063 fixes this.

<details>
<summary>Commands</summary>

```bash
vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat --trust-remote-code \
  --max-model-len 16384 --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 --max-num-seqs 64 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 --no-enable-prefix-caching \
  --distributed-executor-backend mp --enable-expert-parallel \
  --tensor-parallel-size 2 --data-parallel-size 2 --pipeline-parallel-size 2
# The other models use the same flags; Qwen3.5 adds --language-model-only.
# PP1 rows drop --pipeline-parallel-size.
# MTP rows add --speculative-config '{"method": "mtp", "num_speculative_tokens": 2}'.

python tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --port 8000 --max-concurrency 64
python tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --port 8000 --max-concurrency 1 --num-questions 100

vllm bench serve --model deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat --trust-remote-code \
  --dataset-name random --random-input-len 512 --random-output-len 512 \
  --num-prompts 512 --max-concurrency 64 --ignore-eos --seed 1

curl http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/completions -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model": "...", "prompt": "...", "max_tokens": 1, "temperature": 0, "prompt_logprobs": 0}'
```
</details>

## Details

PP transport sends a 1/TP slice of each `IntermediateTensors` entry from each TP rank and reconstructs it with an all-gather on the receiving stage. Stage outputs therefore need to cover all tokens and be identical across TP ranks.

- Remove `pipeline_parallel_size == 1` from the SP gates in Qwen3-Next's `_should_use_sequence_parallel`, both Qwen3.5 decoder implementations, and `DeepseekV2DecoderLayer`.
- At each non-last stage's exit, concatenate `hidden_states` and `residual`, all-gather once, trim token padding, and split them back.
- On non-first stages, Qwen3-Next and Qwen3.5 shard the received `residual` alongside `hidden_states`. DeepSeek-V2's first SP layer already shards a full `residual`.
- DeepSeek-V2 uses the last local layer's SP flag to decide whether to gather at the stage exit. Row counts are ambiguous for a one-token batch, whose shard also has one row. #50691 replaces the existing intra-stage shape checks with explicit layout tracking.
- Qwen3.5 and Qwen3-Next MTP reuse these decoder layers and inherit SP enablement under PP.

AI assistance (Claude) was used to investigate, implement and validate this change. The submitter reviewed every changed line and the validation results.

items.title: [Model][Spec Decode] Support DFlash with pipeline parallelism for MiMo-V2
items.body:
## Overview

Enable MiMo-V2 DFlash with pipeline parallelism by reusing Model Runner V2's auxiliary-hidden-state relay. This extends the MiMo DFlash implementation in #46104; the current model implementation still rejects DFlash when PP > 1.

## Claims

- Relay requested target states across pipeline stages using their global layer indices, and make the target embedding available on the final stage when the existing drafter contract requires it.
- Cover PP=1 versus PP=2 at fixed TP=1 and TP=2 with a local, seeded target checkpoint and real generation and the existing token/top-k comparison.
- This is feature enablement. It does not claim a pretrained-model throughput improvement.

## Validation

| Candidate regression | Hardware | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| TP=1, PP=1 versus PP=2 | 2 x RTX 3080 | Passed in 63.09 s |
| TP=2, PP=1 versus PP=2 | 4 x RTX 3080 | Passed in 68.51 s |

Both cases use the final seeded four-layer, 32-token-vocabulary target, 16 fixed prompts, and at most 16 generated tokens per prompt. They use the existing token/top-k comparison and require nonzero draft acceptance; this helper does not assert numerical equality of logprobs. The compact vocabulary leaves one TP=2 vocabulary shard padded; the larger vocabulary-128 hybrid/MoE control separately exercises both vocabulary shards. No verification bypass, zeroed target weights, or relaxed comparison tolerance is used.

The same final TP=2 test fails without the model adaptation at PP=2 with `MiMoV2FlashForCausalLM does not support dflash with pipeline parallelism`. The imported baseline model blob was verified as `edd50109e386`, matching the PR parent and the inspected current-main file; the candidate blob is `97c26e821aff`.

A separate vocabulary-128, eight-layer hybrid-attention/MoE fixture ran at TP=2 with FULL CUDA graphs (32 prompts, 16 output tokens each):

| Configuration | Generated tokens | Accepted / drafted tokens |
| --- | --- | --- |
| PP=1 DFlash | 512 | 11 / 942 |
| PP=2 DFlash | 512 | 11 / 942 |
| PP=2 target-only | 512 | Not applicable |

With `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1`, all three matched every generated token and selected-token logprob exactly. Under default numerics, PP=1 versus PP=2 DFlash differed at 12/512 token positions, and PP=2 DFlash versus target-only differed at 22/512 positions. These are reported as separate controls; default-setting bitwise equivalence and pretrained throughput are not claimed.

Runtime: official vLLM `0.34.0rc1.dev139+gd9f94a98b`, PyTorch `2.14.0+cu130`, Transformers `5.22.2`; the exact PR MiMo implementation and final test file were overlaid on that runtime. This is not a full build of current main. Ruff check, Ruff format check and `git diff --check` passed.

The regression creates its target weights and draft configuration locally; no pretrained model or tokenizer download is required:

```bash
export CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1,2,3
export VLLM_WORKER_MULTIPROC_METHOD=spawn OMP_NUM_THREADS=2 HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1
python -m pytest -q tests/distributed/test_pipeline_parallel.py::test_pp_mimo_v2_dflash
```

The TP=1 parameter requires two GPUs; TP=2 requires four. Both compare PP=1 with PP=2 at the same TP size and require actual accepted draft tokens. The existing NVIDIA four-GPU optional/nightly pipeline job selects this file; it also has an AMD mirror, which was not locally validated.

Earlier eight-layer hybrid-attention/MoE checks compared all five drafter-input tensors at TP=1, PP=1/2/3, including a pipeline-boundary tap. With `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1`, three configurations (PP=1 DFlash, PP=2 DFlash and PP=2 target-only) matched all 512 generated tokens in each of three passes. Default-setting differences were separately traced to batch-dependent target numerics; exact cross-topology token equality is not claimed under default settings.

The existing Read the Docs failure is an authorization-gate failure, not an observed documentation compilation error: [build 35781015](https://app.readthedocs.org/projects/vllm/builds/35781015/) exited in `docs/pre_run_check.sh` because the [upstream pre-run check](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/actions/runs/42797551234/job/129766478555) had not passed. MkDocs did not run. Upstream GPU CI and the documentation build still need authorization.

## Details

The production change is confined to the MiMo model adapter: advertise the existing auxiliary-state PP contract, use global layer indices, pack local auxiliary states, and use `spec_decode_needs_target_embed`. It does not add another relay, scheduler behavior, or model-runner special case. The supported-model documentation is updated in the same PR. On November 16, main at `9986df412141` still had the pre-fix MiMo model file; searches for MiMo/DFlash/PP found no replacement implementation.

Tradeoffs and limits:

- Each upstream stage must forward the requested auxiliary states. The earlier width-256 fixture carried 1,536 additional BF16 bytes per transmitted row at the rank-0 boundary. This is tensor payload, not an end-to-end latency estimate.
- An untied target embedding can require an additional final-stage copy: about 1.16 GiB before TP sharding for 152,576 rows of width 4,096 in BF16.
- The test uses an untrained drafter. Its acceptance and timings do not estimate trained DFlash performance. Full pretrained MiMo checkpoints, quantized weights, multimodal inputs, task quality, and representative serving throughput remain unvalidated.

items.title: [Model] Support Decision 3.0 prefix_bidir attention (vllm-sr/d3-turbo)
items.body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

This carries over #62584 by @Xunzhuo, which @noooop approved on Oct 27. It has had `needs-rebase` since then, and my [offer to carry it over](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/62584#issuecomment-6702743184) got no reply. It serves [`vllm-sr/d3-turbo`](https://huggingface.co/vllm-sr/d3-turbo) on `/v1/systemone`; on main the model fails at start-up with `unsupported decision_config.json attention_mode 'prefix_bidir'`. Xunzhuo's commit is kept as is. A second commit adapts it to #65996 and #63373.

## Claims

- `prefix_bidir` checkpoints get their own mask. Each request's state block and question block become PrefixLM ranges of the full attention layers. This part is unchanged from #62584.
- Validated on NVIDIA. On an A100, `/v1/systemone` gives the same decision as `model.system_one()` on all 8 questions tried, with a max probability difference of 0.0073. #62584 was measured on an MI325X only.
- No model-runner file changes. #65996 builds per-request PrefixLM ranges in `DefaultModelState.add_request`, so the D3 model state writes its blocks there, and the `default.py` hook from #62584 is dropped.

## Validation

**Setup.** A100-SXM4-80GB, image `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-cf5cea2da3`, with this PR's 5 `vllm/` files and #65996 copied over the installed package. Checkpoint `vllm-sr/d3-turbo` @ `689b3af1`. vLLM selects `TRITON_ATTN`. The reference is the checkpoint's runtime (`trust_remote_code`) in the same image: transformers 5.22.2, with PyTorch fallbacks for its linear-attention kernels.

**`/v1/systemone` vs `model.system_one()`.** The server ran `vllm serve vllm-sr/d3-turbo --max-model-len 8192` with `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error`, and no sync error was raised. dp is the max option-probability difference; for `noul` it is the difference in the yes probability.

| request | question | vLLM | runtime | dp |
|---|---|---|---|---:|
| text | route (choice, 3) | returns | returns | <1e-4 |
| text | receipt (noul) | 0.99991 | 0.99990 | <1e-4 |
| text | urgency (score, 3) | 1.528 | 1.535 | 0.0073 |
| text | department (choice, 40) | department 2 | department 2 | 0.0012 |
| image | photo (noul) | 0.99975 | 0.99972 | <1e-4 |
| JSON state | team (choice, 3) | billing | billing | <1e-4 |
| JSON state | urgent (noul) | 0.640 | 0.637 | 0.0037 |
| JSON state | tone (score, 3) | 0.561 | 0.558 | 0.0049 |

**Code logits with and without the blocks.** `LLM.classify` ran on the runtime's own prompt tokens, as in the new test. With each prompt's state block size the result is closer to the runtime; without it, the whole prompt is read as one block. Max dp per question:

| | route | receipt | urgency | department | photo |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| state blocks | <1e-4 | <1e-4 | 0.024 | 0.0022 | <1e-4 |
| one block | <1e-4 | <1e-4 | 0.087 | 0.020 | 0.0002 |

**Tests**, on the same image without and with this PR:

| test | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `tests/models/multimodal/pooling/test_d3.py` | `prefix_bidir` test fails | 3 passed |
| `tests/entrypoints/generate/structured_decisions/test_strategies.py -k d3` | `prefix_bidir` test fails | 4 passed |
| `tests/config/test_model_arch_config.py -k decision_config_selects_d3` | 1 of 8 fails | 8 passed |

<details>
<summary>Test output</summary>

Without this PR:
```
$ pytest -v -s tests/models/multimodal/pooling/test_d3.py -k prefix_bidir
E         Value error, unsupported decision_config.json attention_mode 'prefix_bidir' [type=value_error, ...]
FAILED tests/models/multimodal/pooling/test_d3.py::test_d3_prefix_bidir_matches_the_checkpoint_runtime
======================= 1 failed, 2 deselected in 42.30s =======================

$ pytest -v tests/entrypoints/generate/structured_decisions/test_strategies.py -k prefix_bidir
E           TypeError: 'NoneType' object is not subscriptable
FAILED tests/entrypoints/generate/structured_decisions/test_strategies.py::test_d3_prefix_bidir_sends_each_prompts_state_block[prefix_bidir]
================ 1 failed, 93 deselected, 2 warnings in 15.26s =================

$ pytest -v tests/config/test_model_arch_config.py -k decision_config_selects_d3
E           AssertionError: assert False == ('prefix_bidir' == 'prefix_bidir'
FAILED tests/config/test_model_arch_config.py::test_qwen35_decision_config_selects_d3[Qwen3_5Model-True-prefix_bidir]
================== 1 failed, 7 passed, 55 deselected in 2.47s ==================
```

With this PR:
```
$ pytest -v -s tests/models/multimodal/pooling/test_d3.py
======================== 3 passed in 454.46s (0:07:34) =========================
$ pytest -v tests/entrypoints/generate/structured_decisions/test_strategies.py -k d3
================ 4 passed, 90 deselected, 2 warnings in 11.92s =================
$ pytest -v tests/config/test_model_arch_config.py -k decision_config_selects_d3
======================= 8 passed, 55 deselected in 2.06s =======================
```
</details>

The new GPU test runs in the "Multimodal Models (Extended Pooling)" step. `pre-commit` passes.

## Details

**Changes from #62584.**
- `D3PrefixBidirModelState` now overrides only `add_request`, and replaces the request's entry in `mm_prefix_ranges` (from #65996) with its two blocks.
- The `use_v2_model_runner` check is dropped. #63373 removed that attribute.
- Docstring backticks follow #65158.

**Why `DefaultModelState`.** `MambaHybridModelState.prepare_attn` does not pass PrefixLM ranges to the attention. #63114 subclasses it and builds the full-attention metadata itself, and keeps prefix caching. D3 runs as a pooling model without chunked prefill, prefix caching or speculative decoding, so it does not need the hybrid state, and `add_request` is the only override. RFC #67334 would move both onto request-level spans.

**Limits.** These are as in #62584: the state is re-read for each question, `/classify` and `/pooling` cannot carry the state block size, and TP and LoRA are not covered. The A100 run above is a spot check, not an accuracy sweep. #62584 has a 260-question sweep on the MI325X, done before the rebase.

**Related PRs.** #60375 bundles #62584's commit with StartLux support. It has been validated on Ascend only, has had conflicts since Oct 20, and has no review. #63114 (merged) serves Base Labs mammoth-1/elephant-1 with a similar two-block mask.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used for the rebase, validation scripts and this description; I reviewed every changed line and the results.

items.title: [Model] Kimi K3.1: NVIDIA specialized decode and AMD model updates, ROCm TP8 support (Kimi K3.1 split 4/6)

items.body:
## Overview

**Kimi K3.1 split 4/6: model file updates (NVIDIA and ROCm)**, split out of #65685 to shrink it. This PR takes the Kimi K3.1 model files under `vllm/models/kimi_k3` from #65685 as they are, plus the smallest set of changes outside `vllm/models` that the AMD files need to serve at TP8 (MI355X, gfx950). Splits 1/6 to 3/6 are merged, so the diff against `main` is only this PR.

| Split | PR | Contents | Base |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1/6 | #66030 (merged) | Model files and NVIDIA specialized decode | main |
| 2/6 | #66028 (merged) | Rust renderer | main |
| 3/6 | #66037 (merged) | KV cache and attention changes to serve K3.1 at TP8 | main |
| 4/6 | this PR | Model file updates (NVIDIA specialized decode, AMD), ROCm TP8 support | main |
| 5/6 | #65685 | ROCm DCP, P/D, indexer top-k | #66532 |
| 6/6 | #66027 | DCP optimizations (opt-in), merged last | #65685 |


Not a duplicate: the content comes from #65685, which drops it once this PR merges. #66172 (AMD specialized decode at DCP1 without M1) is a separate change; both touch `tests/models/kimi_k3/amd_specialized_decode/test_runtime.py` and the AMD specialized decode README, so whichever merges second needs a small rebase.

## Claims

- **NVIDIA specialized decode** (`vllm/models/kimi_k3/nvidia/**` and tests, +5.8k): the faster one-request decode at TP16 + DCP16, the DSpark Markov drafter and logits gather, the wide MoE grid sized by the SM count, and the fused indexer on non-power-of-two MLA pages (the packed hybrid cache's 9216-token pages at TP1, 1152 at TP8). These files need nothing outside `vllm/models` beyond `main`; their DCP paths run only with DCP > 1.
- **AMD model files** (`vllm/models/kimi_k3/amd/**`, the ROCm part of `common/dsa_cache.py`, +3.0k): the K3.1 DSA layers (FP8 indexer, MXFP4 indexer pending AITER page strides, FlyDSL sparse MLA kernel), the packed hybrid block size, and the AMD linear, latent MoE and KDA updates. `KimiK3IndexerBackend` declares 64-token kernel blocks for every indexer dtype: with the FP8 indexer on ROCm it inherited `[1, MultipleOf(16)]`, so the packed block came out at 992 tokens, and the block-flat paged MQA logits fell back from the Triton kernel (which tiles by 64) to the eager torch reference, whose `.item()` breaks CUDA graph capture. They also carry ROCm DCP code; it runs only with DCP > 1, whose ROCm support stays in #65685.
- **Outside `vllm/models`** (+135 −13), only what TP8 needs:
  - ROCm sparse MLA backend: the `fp8_ds_mla` cache, read by aiter's Triton `sparse_mla_fwd` (gfx950 only).
  - ROCm indexer ops and `SparseAttnIndexer`: an optional `cache_layout`, so the indexer section of the packed hybrid cache is read block-flat (`"NORMAL"`). `None` keeps today's auto-selection. The ROCm indexer op rejects `dcp_world_size > 1`.
  - The indexer decode metadata carries `query_start_loc`. `indexer_kv_dtype='mxfp4'` on ROCm still rejects Kimi K3.1: its decode scorer reads the merged index cache in place, and AITER's row-group FP4 MQA logits kernel asserts contiguous pages (TODO in `dsa_indexer_uses_fp4`). The K3.1 ROCm path runs with the default FP8 indexer.
  - `MultiHeadLatentAttentionWrapper.forward(skip_o_proj=...)`, for the AMD specialized decode.
  - `rocm_aiter_ops.indexer_top_k_decode` passes aiter's `stable` and `values` through.

## Validation

ROCm TP8 at `fba512debb` on one 8x gfx950 (288 GB) node, Kimi-K3.1-Pro (MXFP4), default `max_model_len` (1M):

```bash
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 vllm serve Kimi-K3.1-Pro -tp 8 --trust-remote-code \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.95 --max-num-seqs 64
```

Startup: 1024-token blocks, CUDA graph capture done, 5.33 GiB kept for transients,
3,839,026 KV cache tokens (3.66x concurrency at 1M tokens).

`VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1` is required: without it the prefill indexer logits take the torch
reference (`fp8_mqa_logits_torch`, an `[H, M, N]` FP32 score), the extensible KV cache's sizing
warmup measures a 51.7 GiB transient, and no KV cache block fits.

GSM8K (full 1319, 5-shot, greedy, chat template, 64 concurrent):

```bash
lm_eval --model local-chat-completions \
  --model_args model=kimi-k31,base_url=http://<host>:8000/v1/chat/completions,num_concurrent=64,tokenized_requests=False \
  --tasks gsm8k --apply_chat_template --gen_kwargs max_gen_toks=8192
```

| Filter | exact_match |
|---|---|
| flexible-extract | 0.9727 ± 0.0045 |
| strict-match | 0.9719 ± 0.0045 |

NVIDIA: B300 runs of `tests/models/kimi_k3` and a two-node TP8 serve with `decode_backend=latency_specialized` on this branch: TODO (running).

Local (no ROCm GPU; the ROCm kernel tests skip here):

```bash
pre-commit run --files <changed files>     # passed, including mypy
pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_rocm_aiter_mla_sparse_metadata_sync.py \
  tests/kernels/attention/test_kimi_mxfp4_indexer.py \
  tests/kernels/attention/test_rocm_triton_attn_dsv4.py \
  tests/models/kimi_k3/test_amd_dsa_indexer_weights.py \
  tests/models/kimi_k3/test_amd_kda_loading.py \
  tests/models/kimi_k3/amd_specialized_decode/test_runtime.py
# 97 passed, 179 skipped; test_runtime.py's 13 errors (no device type on a
# GPU-less node) are the same on #65685's branch.
```

CI: `test_kimi_mxfp4_indexer.py` is added to the MI355 attention kernels step, and the Kimi K3 model files now trigger the MI355 Kimi K3 model step.

## Details

- **Left in #65685**: ROCm DCP (`dcp_indexer_rocm`, the AITER DCP all-gather, `VLLM_ROCM_DSA_DCP_*`, the DCP sparse MLA paths), the opt-in `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FLYDSL_SPARSE_MLA` dispatch (the FlyDSL kernel file is here but not called yet), AITER MLA on packed caches for dense drafts, P/D and the indexer top-k backends.
- **Shared code**: `sparse_attn_indexer.py` (+10), `backends/mla/indexer.py` (+19) and `layers/mla.py` (+3) only add optional parameters or fields; their defaults keep the DeepSeek V3.2/V4 and NVIDIA paths unchanged.

items.title: [Model][Frontend] Support /v1/audio/transcriptions for LFM3-Audio
items.body:
## Overview

Adds `/v1/audio/transcriptions` support for LFM3-Audio by implementing `SupportsTranscription`. This is the follow-up I mentioned on #65826, now that #65828 has landed.

## Claims

- `LiquidAI/LFM3-Audio-2B` can be served through the OpenAI transcription endpoint. Before this, ASR only worked through chat completions with a system prompt.
- The prompt matches the model card: `Perform ASR.`, or `Perform ASR in <Language>.` when `language` is set.
- Audio up to `MAX_AUDIO_SECONDS` (the same cap as chat) is transcribed in a single pass, with no chunking. Translation requests are rejected.

## Validation

A100 80GB, wheel `0.33.0rc1.dev1045+gf905e7007` with this branch on top, bf16.

`pytest tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_lfm3_audio.py`: 15 passed (existing tests + new ones). The new tests cover:
- the prompt with and without a language;
- translation being rejected;
- the audio token estimate matching the placeholders the processor actually inserts.

Serving `vllm serve LiquidAI/LFM3-Audio-2B`:

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Transcriptions on `mary_had_lamb` and `winning_call` | correct transcripts |
| LibriSpeech dummy, 73 clips, `language=en`, temperature 0 | 0 failures, **WER 5.39%** |
| Offline `LLM.generate` on the same clips with the same prompt (reference) | WER 5.39% |
| 91.5 s audio (9 LibriSpeech clips joined), one request, single pass | WER 5.69% |
| Chat ASR, streaming, audio QA, 16 concurrent requests | all OK |

## Details

- The audio token count comes from the feature extractor (`num_frames` / `num_encoder_tokens`), so it can't drift from what the processor does.
- Language codes outside the model card's list but known to vLLM are passed through by name rather than rejected, since the prompt is just text.
- There are no timestamps or language detection, because the model doesn't produce them.
- I checked for duplicates: there is no open PR for LFM3 transcription. The open LFM3 PRs (#65829, #66323) don't touch these files.

items.body:
## Overview

Adds EAGLE-3 auxiliary hidden-state support to `Lfm3ForCausalLM`, so LFM3 can serve as the
target model for EAGLE-3 / DFlash / DSpark speculators and for `extract_hidden_states`.

Fixes #66311.

## Claims

- `Lfm3ForCausalLM` now implements `SupportsEagle3`; previously any aux-hidden-state method
  failed at load time with `RuntimeError: Model does not support EAGLE3 interface`.
- Aux hidden states are relayed across pipeline-parallel ranks
  (`supports_aux_hidden_states_over_pp = True`), mirroring `Qwen2Model`.

## Validation

Tested on 1× GPU (PP=1, TP=1) with `LiquidAI/LFM3-1.7B`, using Speculators' `launch_vllm.py`
(`extract_hidden_states`, layer ids `[3, 11, 19, 23, 24]`) to feed online DSpark training:

- Before: engine fails to start with the error above.
- After: server starts, hidden states are extracted, and training runs. With
  `--no-enable-prefix-caching --enforce-eager`, 0 non-finite hidden-state records in 1,000 steps.

Reproduce:
    vllm serve LiquidAI/LFM3-1.7B --no-enable-prefix-caching --enforce-eager \
      --speculative-config '{"method":"extract_hidden_states","num_speculative_tokens":1,
        "draft_model_config":{"hf_config":{"eagle_aux_hidden_state_layer_ids":[3,11,19,23,24]}}}' \
      --kv-transfer-config '<ExampleHiddenStatesConnector config>'

## Details

Follows the existing `LlamaModel` / `Qwen2Model` pattern: `Lfm3Model` inherits
`EagleModelMixin`, records hidden states before the first layer and after each layer via
`_maybe_add_hidden_state`, packs them into `IntermediateTensors` on non-last PP ranks, and
returns `(hidden_states, aux_hidden_states)` on the last rank. The output is unchanged when no
aux layers are configured.

**Known issue (help wanted): NaNs in extracted hidden states with CUDA graphs**

- **Symptom:** with CUDA graphs enabled, some extracted hidden states contain NaNs.
  It's intermittent: a retry of the same request usually comes back clean.
- **Workaround:** `--enforce-eager`.
- **Interaction with prefix caching:** with prefix caching also on, retrying a failed
  request appears to reuse the cached NaN hidden states, so the NaN repeats on every retry.
- **Evidence:** `--enforce-eager` with prefix caching on: 0 non-finite records over
  600 training steps. The prefix-cache hit rate in that run was 0% (no retries occurred),
  so prefix caching alone doesn't cause NaNs, but cache reuse wasn't exercised.
- **Possible cause:** how CUDA graphs capture aux hidden states for this hybrid
  conv/attention model, or this change itself. Not yet isolated.
  
**Limitations:** the PP relay path is untested (PP=1 only).

---

items.title: [ROCm][Model] Add Flint support on AMD GPUs
items.body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Adds ROCm support for [RecursiveSI/flint](https://huggingface.co/RecursiveSI/flint) on AMD Instinct gfx942 and gfx950 GPUs.

Flint is split into `common`, `nvidia` and `amd` directories. The NVIDIA implementation and kernels are unchanged under `nvidia`, GGUF loading moves to `common`, and the ROCm implementation lives under `amd`. On ROCm, Flint also uses `torch.compile` and the AITER fused QK-norm + RoPE + KV-cache kernel.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> Serving the NVFP4 GGUF checkpoint with `--kv-cache-dtype fp8` requires #67718. All other configurations work without it.

## Claims

| Checkpoint | GPU | TP | KV cache | Status |
|---|---|---:|---|---|
| `RecursiveSI/flint` (BF16) | MI355X | 1 | BF16, FP8 | Supported |
| `RecursiveSI/flint` (BF16) | MI300X | 1 | BF16, FP8 | Supported |
| `RecursiveSI/flint-nvfp4-gguf` → MXFP8 | MI355X | 1 | BF16 | Supported |
| `RecursiveSI/flint-nvfp4-gguf` → MXFP8 | MI355X | 1 | FP8 | Supported with #67718 |

- **Kernels:** `ROCM_AITER_FA` attention, `RocmDotScaledMxfp8LinearKernel` dense layers, `AITER_MXFP8` routed experts. BF16 uses AITER unquantized fused MoE.
- **Fusion:** the AITER QK-norm + RoPE + KV-cache fusion applies to all 35 sliding-window layers. BF16 output throughput on MI355X is 31–72% higher with no accuracy loss.
- **GGUF:** the GGUF checkpoint is converted once at load time to MXFP8, then runs on the existing ROCm MXFP8 kernels.
- **NVIDIA:** the implementation and kernels are unchanged, behind lazy platform dispatch.

## Validation

### Accuracy

Full GSM8K (1,319 questions) using `tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py`, with chat completions, 16K max tokens and the model's default sampling. These are the same settings as #62938. "Compile + fusion" is off on the baseline and on with this PR's defaults.

| Checkpoint | GPU | KV cache | Compile + fusion | Accuracy | Invalid responses |
|---|---|---|---|---:|---:|
| NVFP4 GGUF → MXFP8 | MI355X | BF16 | Off | 95.0% | 0.5% |
| NVFP4 GGUF → MXFP8 | MI355X | FP8 | Off | 94.8% | 0.2% |
| NVFP4 GGUF → MXFP8 | MI355X | FP8 | On¹ | 94.8% | 0.2% |
| BF16 | MI355X | FP8 | Off | 95.5% | 0.2% |
| BF16 | MI355X | FP8 | On | 95.8% | 0.2% |
| BF16 | MI300X | BF16 | Off | 95.1% | 0.4% |
| BF16 | MI300X | FP8 | Off | 95.5% | 0.1% |

¹ With #67718.

All results match the published accuracy of 95.0% for both BF16 and NVFP4. In the MI300X runs, the invalid responses hit the 16K-token limit. On MI300X, pass `--request-timeout-seconds 3600`: 35 BF16-KV and 22 FP8-KV requests took longer than the default 600 seconds.

### Fusion performance (BF16, MI355X)

TP1, `--kv-cache-dtype fp8`, `--no-enable-prefix-caching`. `vllm bench serve` with the random dataset and `--ignore-eos`. "Before" runs without `torch.compile`, so the gain includes both compilation and the fusion.

| ISL / OSL / Conc | Output tok/s (before → after) | Change | Median TPOT, ms (before → after) | Median TTFT, ms (before → after) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1K / 1K / 1 | 150 → 204 | +36% | 6.59 → 4.85 | 73.8 → 56.9 |
| 1K / 1K / 8 | 724 → 1,245 | +72% | 10.90 → 6.32 | 160.2 → 121.7 |
| 8K / 1K / 16 | 1,107 → 1,702 | +54% | 13.77 → 8.70 | 804.1 → 735.8 |


### Memory

| Checkpoint | GPU | Weights | KV cache capacity |
|---|---|---:|---|
| NVFP4 GGUF → MXFP8 | MI355X | 38.88 GiB | — |
| BF16 | MI300X | 75.17 GiB | 2.99M tokens (BF16), 5.97M tokens (FP8) |

Converting 243 layers from NVFP4 to MXFP8 takes 1.81 seconds.

### Backend cross-check (MI300X)

The prompts were up to 1,822 tokens, longer than the 513-token sliding window. Swapping `ROCM_AITER_FA` for `TRITON_ATTN`, and AITER MoE for Triton MoE, gave prompt-logprob differences of the same size for every pair. No backend is an outlier.

### NVIDIA compatibility (B200, BF16, TP1)

Prefix caching was off. Both builds served correctly, returned the same probe output and selected the same paths: FlashInfer attention, Flint CuTe GEMV and TRT-LLM BF16 MoE.

| Metric | Baseline | This PR |
|---|---:|---:|
| Request throughput | 41.10 req/s | 42.14 req/s |
| Output throughput | 1,315 tok/s | 1,348 tok/s |
| Median TTFT | 251.94 ms | 239.31 ms |
| Median TPOT | 4.24 ms | 4.21 ms |

NVIDIA NVFP4 could not be rerun. On the current CUDA nightly, the CUDA 13 PTXAS rejects the same Triton conversion instruction on both the baseline and this branch. Both builds loaded the checkpoint and selected the same NVIDIA NVFP4, FlashInfer and Flint CuTe paths before that failure.

### Tests

| Check | Coverage |
|---|---|
| AMD unit tests (MI355X, MI300X) | Tiny-model init, routed/shared MoE, logits, fusion enable/skip |
| GGUF tests | Constructor, source/target wiring, exclusions, logits scale |
| Numerical | Merged NVFP4 projections with distinct scales |
| CI | New `(MI355) Flint ROCm` step |
| NVIDIA tests | Updated for the `flint.nvidia` module path |
| Pre-commit | Ruff, format, mypy, SPDX, CI key, test tethering, docstring style |

## Details

### Layout

| Directory | Contents |
|---|---|
| `common` | Platform-neutral GGUF loader |
| `nvidia` | Existing model and Flint kernels, unchanged |
| `amd` | ROCm model on vLLM's standard attention, linear, norm and fused MoE layers |

The package entry point stays lazy and selects the implementation for the current platform.

### GGUF conversion

The NVFP4 GGUF stays packed during loading. Each layer is decoded once, quantized to MXFP8, and its source parameters are released. There is no full BF16 model copy and no NVFP4 dequantization during inference. The output head stays BF16, with its checkpoint scale applied to the logits.

### QK-norm + RoPE + KV-cache fusion

`FlintModel` is compiled with `@support_torch_compile`. Q/K are flattened before RoPE so the graph matches the AITER fusion pattern. `FlintForCausalLMConfig` enables the fusion only when it applies:

| Condition | Fusion |
|---|---|
| AITER enabled; attention backend auto or `ROCM_AITER_FA` | On |
| `custom_ops` includes `-rotary_embedding` | Off |
| Other attention backend, AITER disabled, or not ROCm | Off |

The 14 full-attention layers have no RoPE. They keep the standard path and share the KV-cache layout with the fused layers.

### Serving

BF16:

```bash
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 vllm serve RecursiveSI/flint \
  --tensor-parallel-size 1 \
  --reasoning-parser glm47 \
  --tool-call-parser glm47 \
  --enable-auto-tool-choice
```

NVFP4 GGUF. The ROCm OpenAI image includes `gguf>=0.19.0`; other installs need `pip install "gguf>=0.19.0"`.

```bash
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 vllm serve RecursiveSI/flint-nvfp4-gguf \
  --hf-config-path RecursiveSI/flint \
  --tokenizer RecursiveSI/flint \
  --quantization mxfp8 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 1 \
  --reasoning-parser glm47 \
  --tool-call-parser glm47 \
  --enable-auto-tool-choice
```

items.title: feat: CPU WNA16 MoE INT8 weight-only support for mixed INT4/INT8 models (issue #65070)
items.body:
## Summary

Adds CPU INT8 weight-only (W8A16) support to the MoE modular kernel for models with mixed INT4/INT8 quantization (e.g., poolside/Laguna-XS-2.1-INT4).

## Changes

### Python (vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/experts/cpu_moe.py)
- Extended CPUExpertsInt4 to support both INT4 (W4A16) and INT8 weight-only (W8A16) quantization
- Added weight type detection based on quant_config
- Added process_weights_after_loading() for VNNI prepacking (INT8) and AMX tile layout (INT4)
- Added property overrides for w1_scale, w2_scale, w1_zp, w2_zp
- Modified apply() to route to CPUQuantMethod.INT8_W8A16 or INT4_W4A8
- Added (kInt8StaticChannelSym, None) to supported quant schemes

### Enum (vllm/_custom_ops.py)
- Added INT8_W8A16 = 2 to CPUQuantMethod enum

### C++ Dispatch (csrc/cpu/sgl-kernels/moe.cpp)
- Added scale checks, buffer sizing, and runtime dispatch for INT8_W8A16

### C++ Kernels (csrc/cpu/sgl-kernels/moe_int8.cpp)
- tinygemm_kernel_bf16_int8_vnni: BF16 x INT8 VNNI GEMM for w13 (fused SiLU+Mul) using VPDPBSD
- tinygemm_kernel_bf16_int8_vnni2: BF16 x INT8 VNNI GEMM for w2 (float accumulation)
- fused_experts_int8_w8a16_kernel_impl: Main orchestration
- Uses AVX512_VNNI + AVX512_BF16 (_mm512_dpbsd_epi32 for BF16 x INT8 dot product)

## Testing
- All Python pre-commit checks pass (ruff, mypy, typos)
- C++ clang-format checks pass
- Python syntax verified

## Related Issue
Closes #65070

items.title: [Model] Support CrisperWhisper 2.0
items.body:
## Overview

Fixes #51619. Adds `WhisperForConditionalGenerationWithAttentionLoss`, the architecture of the CrisperWhisper 2.0 checkpoints (`nyralabs/CrisperWhisper2.0_{small,medium,turbo,large}`). They are Whisper fine-tunes, so this is a thin subclass of `WhisperForConditionalGeneration` in a new `crisper_whisper.py`, following the pattern of `granite_speech_plus.py`.

No duplicate: #51619 has no linked PRs or cross-references, and no open PR mentions CrisperWhisper. blazingbhavneek offered to open a PR on 2026-08-10, but none has appeared.

On main the checkpoints do not load, and `--hf-overrides` does not help:

- `LLM("nyralabs/CrisperWhisper2.0_small")` fails with `Model architectures ['WhisperForConditionalGenerationWithAttentionLoss'] are not supported for now.`
- `hf_overrides={"architectures": ["WhisperForConditionalGeneration"]}` fails with `There is no module or parameter named 'encoder_blank_head' in WhisperForConditionalGeneration`.
- The model's prompt puts five mode tags before `<|startoftranscript|>`. Whisper's prompt cannot produce that, and the engine would prepend a second start token.

## Claims

- The 2.0 checkpoints load and serve through `LLM` and `/v1/audio/transcriptions`.
- Output is the verbatim transcript by default, keeping fillers such as `[UH]` and `[UM]`. `vllm_xargs={"mode": "intended"}` gives the clean transcript.
- Language auto-detection works.
- Greedy output is token-identical to a Transformers greedy loop that uses the official prompt.

## Validation

All runs are on Apple M5 Pro, vLLM CPU backend, fp32, with `nyralabs/CrisperWhisper2.0_small`. The reference is the upstream `crisperwhisper` package at nyrahealth/CrisperWhisper@5e5ce64: `PromptBuilder` plus a single greedy `TransformersEngine` decode. A second reference is a plain argmax loop over the same Transformers model with no logits processors. The test set is 152 cases: 76 clips (`mary_had_lamb`, `winning_call`, the Italian `azacinto_foscolo`, and 73 `librispeech_asr_dummy` clips) in both modes, run with `LLM.generate` on the output of `get_generation_prompt`.

| check | result |
| --- | --- |
| decoder prompt ids == upstream `PromptBuilder` | 152/152 |
| token-exact vs Transformers argmax loop | 152/152 |
| text-exact vs upstream engine | 149/152 * |
| LibriSpeech dummy WER, verbatim (vLLM / upstream) | 5.90% / 5.90% |
| LibriSpeech dummy WER, intended (vLLM / upstream) | 6.67% / 6.67% |

\* The upstream engine applies the checkpoint's `generation_config.suppress_tokens`, which include `:` and `"`. vLLM does not apply them, as with Whisper. The 3 differences are only that punctuation.

`vllm serve ... --dtype float32`, `/v1/audio/transcriptions`:

- Text equals the Transformers loop in 20/20 cases: 5 clips × 2 modes × explicit or auto-detected language. Italian is auto-detected correctly.
- 134 s of audio (12 LibriSpeech clips concatenated) goes through the STT chunker. WER is 4.87% verbatim and 5.84% intended. For the same 12 clips sent one at a time, WER is 4.22% and 6.17%.
- An unknown mode, `verbose_json` and `/v1/audio/translations` each return 400.

Turbo and large initialize with dummy weights, and their decoder prompt ids match `PromptBuilder`. Their safetensors headers, and medium's, contain only Whisper keys plus `encoder_blank_head.*`.

**Not validated yet (why this is a draft):** turbo, medium or large with real weights, and anything on GPU (bf16, CUDA graphs).

<details>
<summary>Tests</summary>

```
pytest tests/models/multimodal/generation/test_whisper.py -k "crisper or parse_language or fake_bias"   # 5 passed
pytest tests/entrypoints/speech_to_text/transcription/test_transcription_validation.py -k "crisper or request_extensions"   # 4 passed
pytest tests/models/test_registry.py tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_common.py -k "CrisperWhisper or WithAttentionLoss or coverage"   # 8 passed
pytest tests/entrypoints/speech_to_text/test_speech_to_text_cancellation.py tests/entrypoints/speech_to_text/transcription/{test_chunk_timestamp_offset,test_transcription_inter_chunk_spacing,test_enable_force_include_usage}.py   # 25 passed
pre-commit run --files <changed files>   # passed
```

- Without the `serving.py` change, `test_crisper_whisper_modes` fails with `openai.InternalServerError: Error code: 500 - 'OpenAIServingTranscription' object has no attribute 'tokenizer'`.
- With `skip_decoder_start_token = False`, `test_crisper_whisper` fails its prompt check: `[50258, 51880, ..., 50258, 50259, 50359, 50363] != [51880, ..., 50258, 50259, 50359, 50363]`.
- `test_initialization.py -k WithAttentionLoss` segfaults in pytest's forked child on macOS. Whisper and Canary segfault the same way on this machine. The `can_initialize` body passes when run in-process.

</details>

## Details

- **Prompt:** `[{mode}_1]…[{mode}_5]<|startoftranscript|><|{lang}|><|transcribe|><|notimestamps|>`. This is upstream `PromptBuilder.verbatim()` / `.intended()` with no context and no hotwords. The processor sets `skip_decoder_start_token = True`, as Canary and Cohere ASR do.
- **Mode:** read from `vllm_xargs` (`stt_params.extra_args["mode"]`), as `docs/contributing/model/transcription.md` describes and as Ming-3.0-ASR does. The default is `verbatim`.
- **Weights:** `hf_to_vllm_mapper` drops `encoder_blank_head`, a 1-unit blank detector that upstream decoding does not use.
- **`serving.py`:** `self.tokenizer` was only created for models with segment timestamps, but `_detect_language` also uses it. CrisperWhisper is the first model that has language detection but no timestamps. The tokenizer is now also created when `supports_explicit_language_detection` is set. Whisper sets both flags, so nothing changes for it.
- **`test_initialization.py`:** Whisper's spawn override now also covers the new arch, which runs the same model and processor.
- **Not supported:**
  - `prompt` and hotwords are ignored with a warning. Upstream's `<ctx>` means "continue after these words", so in a probe mapping the prompt to it dropped those words from the output. Hotwords are limited to the Pro models.
  - Translation is rejected, and there are no timestamps (word timestamps need #47664).
  - Upstream's loop repair, fallback and long-form `<ctx>` carry-over. vLLM does one greedy pass per 30 s chunk, so hard clips and long audio can differ from `CrisperWhisperModel.transcribe()`.
- The weights are under the Nyra Health non-commercial research license. The repos are not gated.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used for the investigation, code and this description.

items.title: [Feature][Model] Add NCP-OLMo support for pure HF checkpoints
items.body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Add native support for pure-HF NCP-OLMo checkpoints, using existing vLLM attention
layers and the MRV2 request-state interface. Related to #56880; DFlash/speculative
decoding is outside this PR and the RFC remains open.

## Claims

- Load `NCPOlmo3ForCausalLM` checkpoints with fused QKV/SwiGLU parameters and
  paged token-tower KV caches.
- Maintain request-owned hierarchical model (HLM) state across batching,
  slot refill, chunked prefill and preemption/recompute.
- Keep the contribution model-specific: architecture implementation, model
  registration, the required dummy-initialization registry entry and usage docs.

## Validation

Both public checkpoints were validated on **one H200 each**, at
[`63f4a7f5`](https://github.com/LuckySJTU/vllm/tree/63f4a7f5d839c75d0eb03682e8f2e2b488b30475)
on base `405aaa3d51`, on 2026-11-06. Cleanup commit `d4609abdd2` leaves all runtime source and
the retained registry-test entry **byte-identical** to that snapshot. No new GPU
run is claimed for the cleanup, and these results do not validate later main.

| Check at the validated snapshot | Stage 1 | Stage 2 v1 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Registry initialization | 1 passed | 1 passed |
| Model/transport/contract/generation tests | 73 passed + 9 subtests | 73 passed + 9 subtests |
| Failures / errors / skips | 0 / 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 / 0 |
| Fresh HF/vLLM greedy tokens and per-offset top-5 | 48/48 exact; passed | 48/48 exact; passed |
| FI sampler same-prefix exact-maxima checks | 48/48; one exact tie | 48/48; one exact tie |
| Batching, preemption/refill and mixed-backend exact parity | passed | passed |
| Actual FI sampling / mixed-attention kernel calls | 32 / 272 | 33 / 272 |
| FI offline example | passed | passed |
| GSM8K diagnostic: first 64, 5-shot, greedy, max256 | 23/64 (35.9375%) | 47/64 (73.4375%) |

GSM8K invalid rate was zero for both; these are diagnostic subsets, not full
benchmark scores or speed comparisons. No speedup is claimed.

Runtime: Torch 2.14.0+cu130, main Transformers 5.22.0 / Hub 2.4.0, HF-only
reference Transformers 5.16.1 / Hub 1.33.0, FlashInfer 0.7.3 and FlashAttention 3.
MRV2 and `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error` were enabled. Batch invariance was enabled
except for the mixed-attention candidate (full attention=FI, sliding window=FA3).
HF references were generated live with identical input IDs, BF16/eager/cached
greedy decoding, 16 new tokens and the original top-5 checker at every offset.

Only FI sampling permits distinct tokens when both are exactly tied maxima in
both raw score maps, without an epsilon. Every actual FI prefix was rescored by
a fresh FA3 greedy reference; the original per-offset top-5 check still ran.
All other generation comparisons retained full-sequence exact tokens. An
independent audit checked the hash chains, inputs, versions, JUnit/journals and
actual GPU kernel traces. Native artifacts were reused from official wheel
`fce61a05a76ccf34e1af6511ff7071affc306424`, with source compatibility and all 13
native-file hashes verified; this was **not a full CUDA source build**.

Cleanup checks passed: changed-file pre-commit, mypy, test tethering, dependency
lock hooks, Python compilation and diff checks. The human contributor reviewed
the complete change and this cleanup. Hosted CI and the rendered docs preview
remain unverified; the initial hosted checks stopped at contributor authorization.

steps have been removed from the current PR diff. They are preserved at the

```bash

git diff --name-only --diff-filter=ACMRT 405aaa3d5171a7c9f88294b0e2b262b6d8b18141...HEAD -z \

```

</details>

and standalone example script. Usage examples remain in the
[model guide](https://github.com/LuckySJTU/vllm/blob/d4609abdd29ac4ff48377a4c4d302b5e07c66a97/docs/models/ncp_olmo.md).
There are no remaining changes to Buildkite configuration, global dependencies,
pre-commit configuration, shared scheduler, model runner, attention or sampler.

The HLM needs request-owned dense state in addition to paged token KV; its
lifecycle uses the existing MRV2 model-state interface. The initial implementation

quantized checkpoints and speculative decoding are unsupported. Public HF code
and weights, and the separate DFlash branch, are unchanged.

items.title: [Model] Add LoRA support for Reflection Beam
items.body:
## Overview

Adds LoRA support to Reflection Beam (`BeamForCausalLM`), on both the NVIDIA and ROCm implementations.

TLDR: `BeamForCausalLM` now declares `SupportsLoRA`, and on NVIDIA the SM100 low-latency `qkv_gate_proj` GEMM stays off when LoRA is enabled, because that GEMM reads the base weight directly and would skip the LoRA wrapper.

Not a duplicate: open and merged PRs matching `beam lora`, `BeamForCausalLM` and `beam` only turn up #62074 (model), #62057 (ROCm), #62540 (CI labeller), #62763 (MoE config) and unrelated Beam kernel/perf PRs. None of them touch LoRA.

## Claims

- `--enable-lora` is accepted for `BeamForCausalLM`. Adapters on attention (`q/k/v_proj`, the attention output gate, `o_proj`), the dense MLP and the routed experts load through the existing `packed_modules_mapping`, `hf_to_vllm_mapper` and FusedMoE LoRA paths.
- With LoRA enabled, the attention projection always runs through the LoRA-wrapped `qkv_gate_proj`. Without LoRA, behavior is unchanged.
- `docs/models/supported_models.md` lists LoRA support for Beam.

## Validation

**Local (macOS, CPU only, no CUDA).** I used a venv with `requirements/cpu.txt` and ran the checkout from `PYTHONPATH`. I also skipped the global cleanup fixture through a local pytest plugin that adds `skip_global_cleanup` to every test, because `torch.accelerator.empty_host_cache()` segfaults on macOS in `cleanup_dist_env_and_memory`. That crash is unrelated to this change.

```bash
pytest -p skip_cleanup_plugin tests/models/test_beam_construction.py tests/models/test_beam_weight_mapping.py -v
# this branch: 19 passed, 8 skipped (the 8 skips are CUDA/ROCm/checkpoint-gated)
```

New CPU tests on the base commit (`575cc1faf4`) compared with this branch:

| Test | base | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `test_beam_supports_lora` | FAILED | PASSED |
| `test_low_latency_projection_is_not_warmed_up_with_lora[lora_config1]` | FAILED | PASSED |
| `test_low_latency_projection_is_not_warmed_up_with_lora[None]` | PASSED | PASSED |

<details>
<summary>Base-commit failures</summary>

```
E       AssertionError: assert False
E        +  where False = supports_lora(<class 'vllm.models.beam.nvidia.model.BeamForCausalLM'>)

E       assert [BeamAttention()] == []
E         Left contains one more item: BeamAttention()
```
</details>

On this branch, `ModelRegistry._try_inspect_model_cls("BeamForCausalLM").supports_lora` is `True`, which is the value the config-time check reads. `supports_lora` is also `True` for the ROCm class (`vllm.models.beam.amd.model.BeamForCausalLM`).

`pre-commit run --files <changed files>` passes, including ruff and mypy.

**GPU, out of tree.** The same change ran end to end as a runtime patch on vLLM 0.33.0 in [SkyRL](https://github.com/NovaSky-AI/SkyRL/pull/2619) (commit `f854d6d9`). On L4 GPUs with a tiny random Beam, Megatron and vLLM logprobs matched for merged and unmerged LoRA adapters, with both disk and in-memory adapter loading. The Beam model files touched here are unchanged between v0.33.0 and `main`.

**Not run:**
- The new GPU row `test_beam_builds_and_generates[False-1-8-False-True]`, which builds the tiny Beam with `enable_lora=True` through `LLM` and generates. It needs CUDA or ROCm and is selected by the existing `models_basic` Buildkite step.
- The SM100 low-latency path itself. It only turns on for bf16 `qkv_gate_proj` weights of shape `(1792, 5120)` / `(3584, 5120)` on SM100, so neither the tiny test model nor the L4 validation reaches it. The CPU unit test covers the guard.
- ROCm with LoRA.

## Details

**Why LoRA was rejected.** `BeamForCausalLM` did not implement `SupportsLoRA`, so `LoRAConfig.verify_with_model_config` raised:

```
ValueError: LoRA is not supported for BeamForCausalLM (...). Supported models implement the `SupportsLoRA` interface. Run this model without `enable_lora`.
```

Everything else LoRA needs was already in place:
- `packed_modules_mapping` packs `q/k/v/output_gate_proj` into `qkv_gate_proj` when the KV heads cover the TP size. Otherwise it packs `q/k/v_proj` into `qkv_proj` next to a separate `output_gate_proj`.
- `hf_to_vllm_mapper` renames the attention `self_attn.gate_proj` to `output_gate_proj`, so it never matches the dense MLP's `gate_proj`.
- Routed experts use FusedMoE LoRA with per-expert adapter keys.

`embedding_modules` keeps the `SupportsLoRA` default `{}`. Beam has no LoRA on `embed_tokens` or `lm_head`.

**Why the low-latency GEMM bypasses LoRA.** `BeamForCausalLM.process_weights_after_loading` calls `BeamAttention.warmup_projection()`. On SM100 with unquantized bf16 weights, this sets `low_latency_projection = True`, and `BeamAttention.forward` then computes `packed_projection(hidden_states, self.qkv_gate_proj.weight, True)` instead of calling `self.qkv_gate_proj(...)`. The model runner wraps `qkv_gate_proj` with `MergedColumnParallelLinearVariableSliceWithLoRA` only after loading (`load_lora_model` runs after `model_loader.load_model`), so the direct weight read would silently drop every attention-projection adapter.

**Fix.** `BeamForCausalLM` stores `vllm_config.lora_config`. `process_weights_after_loading` returns before the warmup when it is set, so `low_latency_projection` keeps its `False` default and `forward` uses the module call.

Alternatives considered:
- *Gate inside `BeamAttention.warmup_projection`.* This would mean passing the LoRA config through `BeamDecoderLayer` into `BeamAttention`, for the same effect.
- *Check for a LoRA wrapper in `BeamAttention.forward`.* This adds a per-step branch on the hot path for a decision that is fixed at load time.
- *A LoRA-aware low-latency kernel.* Out of scope. Under LoRA the projection uses the standard wrapped GEMM.

**ROCm.** `vllm/models/beam/amd/model.py` also gets `SupportsLoRA`. It has the same module names and packing, and its `BeamAttention.forward` always calls `self.qkv_gate_proj(...)`, so it has no equivalent bypass. It is not validated on ROCm hardware.

**Existing test change.** `test_dense_only_pipeline_stage_initializes` builds `BeamForCausalLM` from a `SimpleNamespace` config. It now sets `lora_config=None`, because `__init__` reads that field.

items.title: [Model] Add Ricursive Ripple-65B support
items.body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Native support for Ricursive's [Ripple-65B Preview](https://huggingface.co/ricursiveAI/Ripple-65B-Preview) (`RicursiveForCausalLM`, BF16 and ModelOpt [NVFP4](https://huggingface.co/ricursiveAI/Ripple-65B-Preview-NVFP4)), its reasoning and tool-call format, and its [DFlash2 draft](https://huggingface.co/ricursiveAI/Ripple-65B-Preview-DFlash2). Before this PR the only serving path was the authors' out-of-tree SGLang plugin. No open vLLM PR or issue covers this model.

## Claims

- `RicursiveForCausalLM` runs natively with TP, PP, torch.compile and CUDA graphs, without `--trust-remote-code` (built-in `RicursiveConfig`).
- `--reasoning-parser ripple` / `--tool-call-parser ripple`: optional `<think>` plus Hermes-style JSON tool calls. Streaming matches non-streaming output.
- DFlash drafts can declare NoPE layers through `no_rope_layers`. On the Ripple draft this raises mean acceptance length on GSM8K from 4.98 to 7.34.
- Adds a `ricursiveAI/Ripple-65B-Preview` recipe (NVFP4 default on one B300, BF16 variant, parsers, opt-in DFlash2). It passes `validate-source.mjs` from vllm-project/recipes.
- Adds the missing ZAYA1 trace builder, without which `tests/parser/engine/test_replay.py` and `test_delegating_replay.py` fail at collection on main.

## Validation

All runs on B300.

**Parity against the authors' HF modeling code**

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Tiny random 10-layer checkpoint (every feature on, 16-token window), eager / compile / TP=2 / PP=2 | mean \|Δlogprob\| 0.009–0.014, equal to the HF bf16-vs-fp32 floor (0.013–0.015) |
| Ripple-65B BF16, 3 prompts of ~2.2K tokens (2× the sliding window), teacher-forced plus 48 greedy tokens | mean \|Δlogprob\| 0.0105, top-1 agreement 99.5%, greedy 48/48 on all three |

**Accuracy** (`tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py`, 1319 questions, NVFP4 at TP=1)

| Config | Accuracy | Invalid |
|---|---|---|
| Completions, 5-shot | 0.916 | 0.000 |
| Completions, 5-shot, with DFlash2 draft | 0.916 | 0.000 |
| Chat completions, `--reasoning-parser ripple` (content only scored), max 8192 tokens | 0.971 | 0.005 (all 5 hit max tokens while still reasoning) |

**DFlash2 per-position acceptance** (GSM8K 5-shot, `num_speculative_tokens=15`)

| | Mean acceptance length | p1 | p2 | p3 | p4 | p5 | p6 | p8 | p10 | p12 | p15 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Draft NoPE layer rotated (main) | 4.98 | .86 | .71 | .58 | .47 | .39 | .31 | .15 | .07 | .03 | .01 |
| `no_rope_layers` honored (this PR) | 7.34 | .91 | .82 | .73 | .65 | .58 | .52 | .38 | .26 | .17 | .09 |

**Tests**

- `tests/models/test_initialization.py -k Ricursive`, `tests/models/test_registry.py -k Ricursive`: pass.
- `tests/parser tests/tool_parsers tests/reasoning` (CPU): 9771 passed.
- `tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dflash2.py test_dflash_causality.py test_dflash_prepare_inputs.py tests/models/test_qwen3_dflash_mxfp8_context_kv.py tests/models/test_dspark_mla.py`: 160 passed.
- New: `tests/parser/engine/test_ripple.py` and the Ripple trace-builder samples; `test_ripple_draft_skips_context_rope_on_nope_layers` in `test_dflash2.py` (draft routing, and NoPE layers keep unrotated context keys).

<details>
<summary>Reproduce</summary>

```bash
vllm serve ricursiveAI/Ripple-65B-Preview-NVFP4 --max-model-len 32768
python tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --port 8000

vllm serve ricursiveAI/Ripple-65B-Preview-NVFP4 --max-model-len 32768 \
  --enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser ripple --reasoning-parser ripple \
  --speculative-config '{"method": "dflash", "model": "ricursiveAI/Ripple-65B-Preview-DFlash2", "num_speculative_tokens": 15}'
python tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --port 8000 --use-chat-completions --max-tokens 8192 --temperature 0
```
</details>

## Details

- **Model.** Dense 80 layers. Repeating pattern of 4 sliding-window (1024, RoPE) layers and 1 full-attention NoPE layer; PeriNorm (Gemma 3 style pre/post norms); per-head Q/K RMSNorm; fp32 sigmoid output gate; value residuals (`v_proj(lerp(x0, h, sigmoid(λ)))` with `x0` the scaled embeddings); clamped SwiGLU via the existing `SiluAndMulWithClamp`. Q/K/G share one `MergedColumnParallelLinear`; V stays separate because it reads the value-residual blend. The value-residual source is cloned, because the fused add+RMSNorm updates the layer-0 residual in place and would otherwise overwrite it. It travels through PP intermediate tensors, and the model exposes EAGLE-3 aux hidden states for the draft.
- **Parser.** A declarative `ParserEngine` grammar starting in CONTENT. The template's framing newlines (`<think>\n…\n</think>\n`, `\n<tool_call>\n…\n</tool_call>`) are folded into the marker spellings, so they reach neither reasoning nor content. Reasoning is optional, so structured outputs apply from the first token and constrained requests answer directly; this matches the authors' SGLang parser. The markers are multi-token plain text, so the parser is skipped in the single-token replay harness, as PLaMo3 already is.
- **DFlash NoPE.** Ripple's drafter lives in its own subclass (`ricursive_dflash2.py`): a `DFlash2DraftModel` draft that declares `no_rope_layers` is routed to `DFlash2RicursiveDraftModel` in `SpeculativeConfig.hf_config_override`. Its NoPE layers skip the query rotation and restore their unrotated context keys after the shared fused RoPE call. The only shared-code change is moving that fused call into an overridable `DFlashQwen3Model._apply_context_rope`, with no behavior change for other drafts.
- **Reasoning-only streaming.** Without a tool parser (no `--enable-auto-tool-choice`), `parse_delta` passed deltas through raw once the prompt closed reasoning. Ripple's grammar starts in content, so that is always the case. An engine whose grammar can open reasoning from content now parses the whole stream, matching the non-streaming path (`abstract_parser.py`, `adapters.py`). The full `tests/parser tests/tool_parsers tests/reasoning` suite still passes (9771).
- **CI coverage.** The full-size checkpoints are too large for CI, so the parity and GSM8K numbers above were measured locally. `test_ripple.py` joins the other `tests/parser` files on the tethering allowlist while that CI job is disabled.
- **Limitations.** Not tested: ROCm, LoRA, the BF16 checkpoint at TP>1.

items.title: [Model] Nemotron-3.5-Transcribe: support ReplaySSM

labels.name: mrv1-only
labels.description: Issues/PRs which apply only to Model Runner V1 (not applicable to Model Runner V2)

items.body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Follow-up to #64282. vLLM main refuses `--use-replayssm` for Nemotron-3.5-Transcribe, and every serve command in
the model card passes it. This PR declares ReplaySSM support for the model.

## Claims

- vLLM accepts `--use-replayssm` for `Nemotron3_5TranscribeForConditionalGeneration`. NemotronH already sizes the
  ReplaySSM buffers; the wrapper only declares `SupportsReplaySSM`.
- On Model Runner V2, every configuration in the card starts and serves with ReplaySSM (table below).
- CI now runs the model's tests that need the published checkpoint.

## Validation

On main before this PR, the card's serve command stops at startup: `ValueError: --use-replayssm is not supported for
architecture 'Nemotron3_5TranscribeForConditionalGeneration'`.

With this PR, on an RTX PRO 6000 (Blackwell) with the BF16 checkpoint and Model Runner V2, every configuration
starts, and 24 short clips get the same transcript from chat completions and from `/v1/audio/transcriptions`:

| Configuration | Endpoints agree | Mean acceptance length |
|---|---|---|
| MTP8 (the card's default) | 24/24 | 7.25 |
| MTP2 | 24/24 | 3.00 |
| No speculative decoding | 24/24 | – |
| DFlash2 K=7 | 24/24 | 5.46 |

From `tests/`, with Hub access, all pass: `models/test_registry.py -k Nemotron3_5Transcribe` (2),
`models/multimodal/processing/test_nemotron3_5_transcribe.py` (30),
`models/multimodal/processing/test_common.py -k Nemotron-3.5-Transcribe` (3),
`models/test_initialization.py -k Nemotron3_5Transcribe` (2),
`models/multimodal/processing/test_tensor_schema.py -k Nemotron-3.5-Transcribe` (1).

<details>
<summary>Serve command</summary>

```bash
vllm serve nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Transcribe-30B-A4B --dtype bfloat16 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.94 \
  --max-model-len 65536 --max-num-batched-tokens 4096 --max-num-seqs 192 \
  --enable-chunked-prefill --no-enable-prefix-caching \
  --use-replayssm --mamba-backend flashinfer --mamba-cache-mode none \
  --mm-processor-cache-gb 0 --no-async-scheduling \
  --limit-mm-per-prompt '{"audio":{"count":6,"length":120000000}}' \
  --reasoning-parser nemotron_v3 \
  --default-chat-template-kwargs '{"enable_thinking": false}' \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":8}'
```

MTP2 sets `"num_speculative_tokens":2`, no speculative decoding drops `--speculative-config`, and DFlash2 uses
`'{"method":"dflash","num_speculative_tokens":7,"model":"nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Transcribe-30B-A4B-DFlash2"}'`.
</details>

## Details

- **Root cause.** `VllmConfig` refuses `--use-replayssm` unless the architecture declares `SupportsReplaySSM`.
  NemotronH declares it, but the Transcribe wrapper contains a NemotronH decoder rather than subclassing it, so the
  flag was missing. The wrapper already passes the Mamba state shape, dtype and copy-function calls to NemotronH,
  which adds the ReplaySSM ring buffers, so the declaration is the whole fix.
- **Constraints.** With speculative decoding, vLLM's FlashInfer ReplaySSM needs `--mamba-backend flashinfer` and
  `--no-enable-prefix-caching`; the card sets both, and the docs note now says so.
- **Model Runner V1.** The card currently selects V1 for the NeMo vLLM plugin's word timestamps. Since Model Runner
  V1 is being removed, this PR is validated on V2 only.
- **CI coverage.** CI cannot serve the 30B checkpoint end to end, so the serving validation above ran locally. With
  the registry entries online, CI runs the model's registry, initialization, processing and tensor-schema tests.
- **Related PRs.** No open PR changes these lines. #65379 (native CTC word timestamps) also edits the model file.

items.title: [Model] Deprecate PaliGemma support.
items.body:
## Overview

- PaliGemma currently produces incorrect multimodal outputs in vLLM. vLLM applies causal attention to all tokens, while PaliGemma requires bidirectional attention for image tokens (PrefixLM).  #14565

items.title: [Model] Add ZAYA1 support
items.body:
## Overview

Adds native support for Zyphra's ZAYA1 models (`ZayaForCausalLM`: [ZAYA1-8B](https://huggingface.co/Zyphra/ZAYA1-8B), [ZAYA1-74B-preview](https://huggingface.co/Zyphra/ZAYA1-74B-preview)), with `zaya` tool and reasoning parsers. Closes #42286.

This builds on Zyphra's #41999 (thanks @yury-tokpanov and the Zyphra team), reimplemented against current `main`: it reuses the Transformers `ZayaConfig`, the existing Mamba state and `ShortConv` metadata for CCA, `FusedMoEFactory`, and the `Qwen3Parser` grammar, so it adds ~870 lines (≈600 for the model) instead of ~2.8k, and needs no changes to shared MoE/Mamba/config code.

## Claims

- `ZayaForCausalLM` matches Transformers in float32 (greedy-exact on 8B; logprobs on a 5.2k-token 74B prompt) and runs with chunked prefill, prefix caching, CUDA graphs, TP, EP and online FP8.
- CCA state handling has no host syncs and no per-request loop (`VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error` passes).
- `--tool-call-parser zaya --reasoning-parser zaya` parse ZAYA's `<zyphra_tool_call>` calls, including calls that end reasoning without `</think>`. `zaya_xml` is an alias matching the model cards.

## Validation

**Tests** (B300):

```bash
pytest tests/models/language/generation/test_hybrid.py -k zaya   # 1 passed
pytest tests/tool_parsers/test_zaya_tool_parser.py                 # 3 passed
pytest tests/models/test_initialization.py tests/models/test_registry.py -k Zaya  # 2 passed
```

`test_zaya_cca_state` builds a random tiny ZAYA1 (full and sliding-window layers) and compares vLLM against Transformers in fp32 with chunked prefill (`max_num_batched_tokens=32`) and prefix caching (cold pass, then cached pass). It fails if decode history, prefill/prefix-cache history, or the delayed value state is dropped (each mutation checked). The released tiny checkpoints (`tiny-random/zaya1`) predate the released config format, so the test builds its own.

**Correctness vs Transformers**

| Model | Setting | Result |
|---|---|---|
| ZAYA1-8B | fp32, 3 prompts × 60 greedy tokens, single and batched | 60/60 each |
| ZAYA1-74B-preview | fp32, TP=2, prompt logprobs over 5,200 tokens (past the 4,097 sliding window) | mean \|Δlogp\| 2.2e-4; 6 tokens > 0.05 (max 0.21); max after token 4097: 0.0009 |

Transformers' own one-shot vs chunked prefill differs by up to 0.77 logprob on 8B: the hard top-1 router flips experts on near-ties (203 of 104k routing decisions on a 2.6k-token prompt), so bf16 and long-prompt greedy outputs are not token-exact across implementations or batch shapes. vLLM's deviations land on the same positions.

**Eval** (GSM8K, chat, `--reasoning-parser zaya`, temperature 1.0 / top-p 0.95 per the model card, 16k max tokens):

| Model | GPUs | Accuracy | Invalid | Mean output tokens |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ZAYA1-8B | 1× B300 | 0.893 | 0.001 | 2,315 |
| ZAYA1-74B-preview | 1× B300 | 0.893 | 0.001 | 1,085 |

Full 1,319-question test set, single run with `--seed 0`. The model cards report no GSM8K score, so this checks end-to-end serving health rather than reproducing a published number.

```bash
vllm serve Zyphra/ZAYA1-8B --max-model-len 32768 --reasoning-parser zaya
python tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --use-chat-completions --max-tokens 16384 \
    --temperature 1.0 --top-p 0.95 --seed 0 --num-shots 0 --request-timeout-seconds 7200
```

**Other runs** (ZAYA1-8B): TP=2; EP (`--data-parallel-size 2 --enable-expert-parallel`) with a parsed tool call and a `json_schema` response after reasoning over `/v1/chat/completions`; `--quantization fp8`; default prefix caching (4,752 of 4,756 prompt tokens hit, cached output identical to cold).

## Details

- **CCA** (Compressed Convolutional Attention) mixes q/k with a two-stage causal conv over the current and two previous tokens, and takes half of v from the previous token's projection. Each layer keeps the last two raw q/k rows and the previous delayed value as Mamba state, reusing `ShortConvAttentionMetadata` (only per-request slots and query offsets are needed). Most tokens go through one conv over the flattened batch; only each request's first two tokens are recomputed against their saved history.
- **Router**: MLP router over `num_experts + 1` classes (the extra one skips the experts), with balancing biases and the previous layer's router state (EDA). Routing runs in the model and is passed to `FusedMoEFactory` through `custom_routing_function`. The weights slice is made contiguous: MoE kernels ignore the stride of a `[:, :topk]` view of the packed routing tensor and read token IDs as weights.
- Attention, CCA and router projections are replicated across TP ranks (2 KV heads); experts are TP/EP-sharded, as in #41999.
- Not supported: speculative decoding (raises), pipeline parallel, LoRA, EPLB.

items.title: [Test] Support hybrid GDN models in test_process_checkpoint
items.body:
## Purpose

`test_process_checkpoint` cannot run against hybrid GDN (mamba-family) models:
they reject `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` at startup
(`VLLM batch_invariant mode is not supported for GDN_ATTN`), and their batched
greedy generation is not run-to-run reproducible, so the test's batched
output comparison is unusable for that model family. The CUDA process
checkpoint feature therefore has no token-exact regression coverage for GDN
models (the test docstring previously just excluded them).

This PR makes the test handle hybrid models:

- When `ModelConfig.is_hybrid` is true for the selected model, the test no
  longer sets `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` and compares outputs per request
  (batch-size-1 generation, which is deterministic for this model family).
- Non-hybrid models keep the exact previous behavior (batched generation with
  batch invariance).

Closes #65112

## Test plan

Opt-in GPU test (requires `VLLM_TEST_CUDA_PROCESS_CHECKPOINT=1` and a
checkpoint-capable driver), not run in default CI.

Verified on 4×H20 96 GB, driver 580.126.09, torch 2.14.0+cu130, NCCL 2.30.7:

```bash
VLLM_TEST_CUDA_PROCESS_CHECKPOINT=1 VLLM_TEST_MODEL=Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B \
  VLLM_TEST_SLEEP_CYCLES=2 \
  pytest tests/basic_correctness/memory/sleep_mode/test_process_checkpoint.py -q
```

- Hybrid GDN (`Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B`): `[1-p2p]`, `[2-p2p]`, `[4-p2p]` all PASS —
  per-request outputs verbatim stable across cycles, graph handles identical,
  zero new captures. (shm cells not exercised for the GDN model.)
- Non-hybrid (`Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B`), full file (TP1/2/4 p2p + TP2/4 shm, 5/5):
  PASS via the unchanged batched batch-invariant path.

Additional scale data with the same protocol (5 cycles): TP2 and TP4 on the
27B hybrid GDN model all pass with graph identity preserved and zero
recaptures.

## Details

The per-request path loops `llm.generate([prompt], ...)` over the two fixed
prompts. Everything else in the test (graph identity assertions, replay/capture
counters, sleep/wake order rotation) is unchanged.

Note on the gate: `ModelConfig.is_hybrid` covers all hybrid model families
(not only GDN — e.g. lfm2, olmo_hybrid). Those families keep working in
per-request mode (the comparison stays token-exact, just slower), so the
wider gate is a safe simplification; happy to narrow it to mamba-family
backends explicitly if preferred.

items.title: [Mamba][MRV2] Plan Triton ReplaySSM decode on the GPU and support Model Runner V2

labels.name: ready
labels.description: ONLY add when PR is ready to merge/full CI is needed

items.body:
## Overview

Triton ReplaySSM (`--use-replayssm --mamba-backend triton`, #48018) was rejected on Model Runner V2: it planned each decode step on the CPU from a per-request ring origin that only the V1 input batch tracked. This PR moves that planning to the GPU using per-cache-slot ring counters (the same trackers the FlashInfer ReplaySSM backend from #52506 already uses), which enables MRV2 and deletes the runner-side plumbing.

## Claims

- Triton ReplaySSM now runs on MRV2, with logprob parity against the non-ReplaySSM baseline on both runners, with and without mamba `align` prefix caching.
- No runner changes are needed for V2; the V1-only `replayssm_decode_base_cpu` plumbing (in `CommonAttentionMetadata`, the V1 input batch, and the V1 runner) is removed.
- The per-step CPU planning in the Mamba metadata builder (about 70 lines, plus two `.tolist()` → H2D copies each step) is replaced by one small GPU kernel per KV-cache group per step.

## Validation

All runs were on GB200 (one GPU) with `nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Nano-4B-BF16`.

| Test | V1 | V2 |
|---|---|---|
| `test_replayssm_decode_matches_baseline` (Triton) | pass | pass |
| `test_replayssm_prefix_caching_matches_baseline` (Triton, align mode, asserts prefix-cache hits > 0) | pass | pass |
| Same two V2 tests with `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error` | n/a | pass |

```bash
pytest -v -s tests/v1/e2e/test_replayssm_decode.py \
  -k "(test_replayssm_decode_matches_baseline or test_replayssm_prefix_caching_matches_baseline) and not tp2"
```

Unit and kernel tests also pass: `tests/kernels/mamba/test_replayssm_plan.py` (new), `tests/kernels/mamba/test_replayssm_standard_decode_mamba2.py`, `tests/v1/attention/test_replayssm_metadata_builder.py`, `tests/model_executor/test_replayssm_warmup.py`, the tracker-sharing test in `tests/v1/worker/test_utils.py`, and the ReplaySSM config test in `tests/test_config.py` (168 tests).

The new kernel test drives the planner through whole decode runs and checks every step against the removed CPU formula. It covers none and align modes, buffer lengths 4, 6 and 16, align block sizes 16, 32 and 64, and prompts that end mid-block or on a block boundary. It also covers rows planned independently, padding rows, re-anchoring after a prefill reset (preemption-resume), and a stale slot counter at a prefix-cache block boundary.

Not run: the TP2 parity tests (V1 only, unchanged) and the FlashInfer ReplaySSM e2e tests (that path is unchanged apart from sharing tracker setup with Triton layers). CI's `replayssm-e2e` step (2×H100) covers both.

## Details

**Planning.** Each Mamba2 layer already gets per-slot `ring_start`/`prev_num_accepted`/`prev_query_len` tensors from `share_replayssm_ring_trackers`, shared within a KV-cache group; this PR extends that to Triton layers. For Triton, `ring_start[slot]` is the number of tokens buffered since the slot's last full-state write. The first ReplaySSM layer of each group calls `plan_replayssm_decode`, which writes that step's `write_pos`/`is_flush` into persistent builder buffers that every layer reads, then advances the counter (resetting it to 0 after a flush). Prefill resets the counters with the existing `reset_replayssm_ring_trackers`. The Triton SSU kernel is unchanged.

**Align mode.** The planner reads the GPU `seq_lens`, which both runners keep in persistent buffers. It restarts the ring on a block's first step and forces a flush on the step that completes a block, so the exact block-boundary state is materialized for prefix caching. That is what the CPU code did with `max(decode_base, block_start)`. Restarting at the block's first step also handles a prefix-cache hit on a reused slot whose counter is left over from a previous request, because such hits always land on a block boundary.

**CUDA graphs.** `write_pos`/`is_flush` were already persistent buffers for FULL graphs; they are now written on the GPU inside the graph instead of being copied in before replay. Padding rows have `NULL_BLOCK_ID` slots and are planned as no-ops.

**Behaviour change.** A one-token final prompt chunk that runs as a decode row (`prefill_to_decode`) now appends to the ring the previous chunk's prefill left empty, like any other decode step, instead of forcing a one-token flush. Both are mathematically equivalent, since the checkpoint is the state before that token. The planner unit test covers this case; the e2e tests don't deliberately trigger it.

**Limitations.** `mamba_cache_mode="all"` with Triton ReplaySSM is not rejected by config but was not handled correctly before this change either (the decode slot changes every block without a ring restart). This PR does not change that.
