items.body:
## Overview

Adds `torch.compile` support for the PaddleOCR-VL vision encoder. `SiglipEncoderLayer` gets the `@support_torch_compile` decorator behind `compile_mm_encoder`, following Qwen2.5-VL, Qwen3-VL and Pixtral ([#57168](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57168)). Nothing changes unless `compile_mm_encoder=True`.

## Claims

- `compile_mm_encoder=True` compiles PaddleOCR-VL's 27 SigLIP encoder layers. The first layer compiles in about 4 s, the other 26 reuse it, and restarts load from the cache.
- With `vllm bench serve` on H100, throughput rises by 1.8–7.3% and mean TTFT falls by 3.3–9.8% at concurrency 1–256. The gain exceeds the trial-to-trial range at concurrency 64–256.
- On the full OmniDocBench recognition set, throughput rises by 1.4% and accuracy is unchanged within BF16 noise.

## Validation

Setup: H100, PaddleOCR-VL-1.6 (`c5630ab`) in BF16, base `2631afd3f`. Both versions use `-cc.mode=3 -cc.cudagraph_mode=FULL_DECODE_ONLY` and differ only in `-cc.compile_mm_encoder`.

**OmniDocBench recognition.** 19,251 regions from all 1,651 public pages, concurrency 64, prefix caching off, 32 warmup crops, one measured pass per version. The harness is the same as in [#61458](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61458).

| Metric | Compile off | Compile on |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Throughput, crops/s | 76.58 | 77.65  |
| EngineCore CPU time, ms/crop | 13.64 | 13.43 |
| Text NED ↓ | 0.015787 | 0.015652 |
| Formula NED ↓ | 0.062234 | 0.062199 |
| Table TEDS ↑ | 0.952008 | 0.951610 |


**`vllm bench serve` (random-mm).** The serve flags, bench flags, image mix and seeds for c=32–256 match #61458. c=1 and c=8 were added with 128 and 256 prompts. Each configuration ran 3 trials, alternating off and on per trial. Throughput is the mean, with min–max in parentheses; TTFT is the mean of the per-trial means. All 11,520 requests succeeded.

| Concurrency | Off req/s | On req/s | Gain | Mean TTFT off → on |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 7.35 (7.22–7.53) | 7.66 (7.40–7.80) | +4.2% | 50.8 → 45.8 ms (−9.8%) |
| 8 | 29.24 (28.05–30.19) | 29.93 (29.35–30.27) | +2.3% | 139.5 → 128.5 ms (−7.9%) |
| 32 | 49.35 (46.45–51.90) | 50.24 (47.57–52.24) | +1.8% | 312.7 → 299.1 ms (−4.3%) |
| 64 | 52.68 (50.61–55.00) | 56.52 (54.67–58.78) | +7.3% | 598.5 → 565.6 ms (−5.5%) |
| 128 | 56.64 (54.72–57.66) | 59.21 (58.52–60.05) | +4.5% | 1,118 → 1,065 ms (−4.8%) |
| 256 | 55.31 (54.06–56.30) | 58.68 (56.43–61.11) | +6.1% | 2,163 → 2,091 ms (−3.3%) |

P99 TTFT improved at c=1, 8, 32 and 128, and was slightly worse at c=64 (+2.2%) and c=256 (+0.6%). This sweep ran on an H100 shared with other jobs; alternating the variants spreads that interference across both.

**Outputs, TP and sync checks.** 32 text-image prompts, including one with two images, at temperature 0 with `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error`. Off and on outputs were identical for 32 of 32 prompts at both TP=1 and TP=2, and no syncs were flagged. At TP=2, the all-gather inside the attention layer compiles and runs correctly.

**Tests.**

```bash
pytest tests/compile/fullgraph/test_multimodal_compile.py -k paddleocr -v   # new: 2 passed
VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error pytest tests/model_executor/test_paddleocr_vl_mrope.py \
  tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_tensor_schema.py -k "paddle or mrope"   # 5 passed
pre-commit run --files <changed files>                                          # passed
```

The new test checks the number of compiled modules: 2 for the language model when the flag is off, and 29 when it is on (one more per encoder layer). It runs in the `PyTorch Fullgraph` CI step.

## Details

**Scope.** Only `SiglipEncoderLayer` is compiled; the layers account for nearly all encoder time. The patch embedding and projector contain per-image Python loops (position-embedding interpolation and the 2×2 merge `rearrange`), which would cause graph breaks or recompiles. `hidden_states` is `[1, num_patches, hidden]`, so its dynamic dimension is 1.

**Encoder-only speedup.** Measured by timing eager and compiled encoders alternately on the same scheduled batches:

| Batch | Eager | Compiled | Speedup |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 image, 192 tokens | 15.1 ms | 10.8 ms | 1.40× |
| 1 image, 609 tokens | 15.0 ms | 12.1 ms | 1.24× |
| 1 image, 2,160 tokens | 68.6 ms | 65.2 ms | 1.05× |
| 8 images, 3,794–5,021 tokens | 81.6–119.1 ms | 75.8–112.5 ms | 1.06–1.08× |



**Relation to other PRs.** [#44394](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/44394) adds encoder CUDA graphs for PaddleOCR-VL. The two PRs are independent: this one does not touch the code paths #44394 changes, and it applies with or without encoder graphs. Running both together, where the encoder graphs would capture the compiled layers, is not covered here. No open or closed PR adds encoder compilation for PaddleOCR-VL.


<details>
<summary>Reproduction</summary>

Model: `PaddlePaddle/PaddleOCR-VL-1.6` @ `c5630abae1d940eafe0697512a0325494b02ab42`. Use the same commands for both variants, changing only `-cc.compile_mm_encoder`.

```bash
vllm serve "$MODEL_PATH" \
  --served-model-name paddleocr-vl --dtype bfloat16 \
  --host 127.0.0.1 --port 18356 \
  --max-model-len 16384 --max-num-seqs 512 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 4096 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.18 \
  --kv-cache-memory-bytes 8589934592 --no-enable-prefix-caching \
  --mm-processor-cache-gb 4 --seed 42 \
  -cc.mode=3 -cc.cudagraph_mode=FULL_DECODE_ONLY \
  -cc.compile_mm_encoder=true   # or false
```

Synthetic benchmark. Seeds: c=1 → 1042–1044, c=8 → 1142–1144, c=32 → 42–44, c=64 → 142–144, c=128 → 242–244, c=256 → 342–344. Prompts and warmups: c=1 → 128/8, c=8 → 256/16, others → 512/32.

```bash
vllm bench serve \
  --backend openai-chat --base-url http://127.0.0.1:18356 \
  --endpoint /v1/chat/completions --model paddleocr-vl \
  --tokenizer "$MODEL_PATH" --dataset-name random-mm \
  --random-input-len 64 --random-output-len 64 --random-range-ratio 0 \
  --random-mm-base-items-per-request 1 \
  --random-mm-num-mm-items-range-ratio 0 \
  --random-mm-limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image": 1, "video": 0}' \
  --random-mm-bucket-config \
  '{(224, 224, 1): 0.25, (448, 896, 1): 0.25, (896, 448, 1): 0.25, (896, 896, 1): 0.25}' \
  --temperature 0 --ignore-eos --request-rate inf \
  --num-prompts "$NUM_PROMPTS" --num-warmups "$NUM_WARMUPS" \
  --max-concurrency "$CONCURRENCY" --seed "$SEED"
```

OmniDocBench uses the same dataset, revisions, crop extraction, prompts, token limits and scoring as #61458.

</details>

items.body:
## Overview

ROCm support for [stepfun-ai/Step-5-Preview](https://huggingface.co/stepfun-ai/Step-5-Preview), complementing the NVIDIA support added in #61727. This PR adds a self-contained amd/ implementation under vllm/models/step5/ and moves the platform-independent Step-5 sparse-attention code from nvidia/ to common/.

The primary support and validation target is **MI300X/MI325X (gfx942)**. **MI355X (gfx950)** is also supported and has secondary validation from [@jamesETsmith](https://github.com/jamesETsmith).

## Claims

- Step-5-Preview FP8 weights serve at TP8 on ROCm with text and image input.
- Compressed sparse attention (CSA) runs on the 23 sparse layers for prefill, chunked prefill, decode, and MTP verification.
- The main paged K/V cache uses ROCm AITER unified attention. The sparse summary cache, speculative tail ring, region scoring, and split-K decode code are shared with the NVIDIA Step-5 path.
- Sparse layers support the default BF16 K/V cache and FP8 E4M3 K/V. FP8 K/V requires `--block-size 32`.
- Three-token MTP works through the Step-3.5 MTP proposer with comparable accuracy and about 2.3x speedup in the earlier GSM8K run.
- Prefix caching and P/D disaggregation are supported. NIXL and Mooncake keep compressed summary pages whole and reject unsupported page splitting.
- CSA uses the existing KV-cache lifecycle and does not require scheduler changes or GPU-to-CPU synchronization.

### Serving command (ROCm, MTP enabled)

<details>
<summary>Serve Step-5-Preview on 8x MI300X</summary>

```bash
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 vllm serve stepfun-ai/Step-5-Preview \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
  --max-model-len 32768 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 \
  --moe-backend triton \
  --mm-encoder-attn-backend ROCM_AITER_FA \
  --mm-encoder-tp-mode data \
  --mm-processor-cache-type shm \
  --limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image":1,"video":0}' \
  --reasoning-parser step5 \
  --tool-call-parser step5 \
  --enable-auto-tool-choice \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}'
```

| Flag | Why |
|---|---|
| `--moe-backend triton` | Required. Every MoE layer clamps SwiGLU at 7, and AITER's block-FP8 MoE does not apply that clamp yet. |
| `--mm-encoder-*`, `--limit-mm-per-prompt` | Image input through the perception-encoder tower. |
| Default K/V dtype | BF16 sparse K/V. |
| `--kv-cache-dtype fp8 --block-size 32` | Optional FP8 E4M3 sparse K/V. |

</details>

### How this fits with #61727

| | #61727 (NVIDIA) | This PR (ROCm) |
|---|---|---|
| Platforms | SM90, SM103 | gfx942 primary; gfx950 secondary |
| Main paged attention | NVIDIA backends | ROCm AITER unified attention |
| Sparse state | Summary cache + speculative tail ring | Same cache contracts |
| Region scoring / decode | Triton and FlashInfer adapters | Shared Triton scoring and split-K decode |
| Indexer Q/W | Sharded by provider group | Sharded by provider group |
| MTP | Yes | Yes, through the Step-3.5 MTP proposer |
| Parsers | `step5` | `step5` |

Like nvidia/, amd/ imports nothing from the other platform and does not use or change model_executor/models/step3p5*; nvidia/ changes are import paths only.

## Validation

### Primary: gfx942

**Model setup:** 8x MI300X, TP8, `max-model-len 32768`, vLLM ROCm nightly `3f1bcfd82` with this branch applied.

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| GSM8K, full 1319, 5-shot chat (earlier revision) | 97.2%; 97.4% with MTP |
| GSM8K, 200-question sample, MTP (final model revision) | 96.0% |
| Needle in a haystack, 4K / 16K / 30K, 3 depths, 3 trials | 27/27 |
| Image input: shapes, counting, reading text | 3/3 correct |
| Prefix caching, shared ~22K-token prefix | 66% of prompt tokens from cache; answers correct |
| MTP acceptance, 3 draft tokens (earlier revision) | Mean acceptance length 3.1 to 3.3 |
| `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error`, long chunked prefill + 15 concurrent decodes | No syncs |
| Prefill, 26K-token prompt | TTFT 2.7 s |
| `step5` parsers, stream and non-stream | Pass |
| `tests/models/test_initialization.py` | Pass |

The latest focused tests were also run on MI325X (gfx942). They cover gated four-token MTP verification, short-history decode, true nonzero-offset chunked prefill, equal-length prefill versus decode metadata, scored-prefill warmup discovery, and compressed-page checks through the real NIXL and Mooncake connector constructors.

### Secondary: gfx950

Validation by [@jamesETsmith](https://github.com/jamesETsmith):

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| GSM8K, 5-shot, 1319 | 96.97% strict / 97.27% flexible; 96.59% / 97.04% with MTP |
| GPQA-Diamond, 198-question, zero-shot CoT | 85.86% (170/198); 85.35% (169/198) with MTP, raw lower bounds with a 16K generation budget |
| RULER-style single-key and multikey-2/3 NIAH | 100% at 32K / 128K / 256K, with and without MTP |

The focused CSA and connector tests also passed on MI355X (gfx950). Full validation details are in [James's comment](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61837#issuecomment-6206831125).

About 8% of GSM8K items timed out in lm-eval's client at concurrency 64 because of long reasoning traces. They were re-asked with the same settings and scored with lm-eval's strict regex. Raw lm-eval scores were 89.2% for CSA and 88.7% for CSA + MTP.

#### In-tree reorganization (latest commit)

Same session, 8x MI300X, TP8, median TPOT (ms) over 3 runs, before vs after the reorganization:

| K/V | 1K in, 1 req | 8K in, 1 req | 1K in, 16 conc |
|---|---|---|---|
| BF16 | 38.97 / 39.42 | 86.67 / 87.01 | 45.10 / 44.80 |
| FP8 E4M3, `--block-size 32` | 39.41 / 39.32 | 91.96 / 91.90 | 44.85 / 45.66 |

Raw lm-eval GSM8K is unchanged (89.4% before; 89.4% BF16 K/V and 89.2% FP8 K/V after), and the real checkpoint loads the same tensors and values. The scored-prefill warmup cuts the first cold 9K-token prompt from 3.46 s to 1.14 s.

The same comparison on 8x MI350X (gfx950), BF16 K/V:

| | 1K in, 1 req | 8K in, 1 req | 1K in, 16 conc | GSM8K raw (flexible / strict) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Before | 24.83 | 79.10 | 32.18 | 89.9% / 89.7% |
| After | 24.83 | 79.17 | 32.32 | 89.1% / 88.6% |

The GSM8K gap is within one standard error (±0.86) and matches the extra client timeouts on long reasoning traces (101 before, 110 after).

The 600B checkpoint does not fit in CI, so model-level results come from real hardware. The focused kernel, metadata, configuration, warmup, and connector tests are CI-sized.

## Details

- **Layout:** `vllm/models/step5/{common,nvidia,amd}` with platform dispatch from `vllm/models/step5/__init__.py`. ROCm code lives only in `amd/`
- **Main K/V:** written by `unified_kv_cache_update` and consumed directly from the AITER unified paged layout.
- **Sparse state:** an FP8 summary cache plus a tail ring for incomplete and speculative regions, both attached to the existing KV-cache lifecycle.
- **Decode and MTP:** summary scoring, per-row top-k, and split-K paged attention support ordinary decode and four-row MTP verification, including the head-wise attention gate.
- **Scored prefill:** histories longer than `topk * region_size` use packed summary scoring. Startup warmup now covers this path  on ROCm it dispatches to `amd/warmup.py`
- **Indexer sharding:** Q and W are `ColumnParallelLinear` sharded by provider group; K and Z stay replicated.
- **P/D:** NIXL and Mooncake preserve compressed pages for compatible layouts and fail early if a layer-outer transfer would split one compressed state page. This check applies to every compressed-cache model.
- **MoE:** the shared expert runs inside FusedMoE, and the combined output is all-reduced once in the model dtype.
- **Graphs:** the CSA op is a graph-splitting op and uses real per-step metadata. Piecewise CUDA graphs are supported.

### Limitations

| Limitation | Follow-up |
|---|---|
| Piecewise CUDA graphs only | Make CSA metadata safe for full graphs |
| `--moe-backend triton` required | Add the post-SiLU clamp to AITER block-FP8 MoE |
| Sparse top-k still has unfused work | Fuse and optimize region selection |

---

<details>
<summary> Pull Request Checklist </summary>

- [x] I used vLLM's PR checklist.
- [x] AI assistance was used during the creation and review of this PR.
- [x] This is the ROCm counterpart to #61727, not a duplicate implementation for the same platform.
- [x] **Design Fit:** Reuses the existing KV-cache lifecycle and shared Step-5 sparse components without scheduler changes.
- [x] **Testing and Validation:** Covers BF16/FP8 K/V, prefill, chunked prefill, decode, MTP, the head-wise gate, warmup, and connector page geometry, with model validation on real gfx942 and gfx950 hardware.
- [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Keeps the platform-specific model code under `amd/` and shares platform-independent code through `common/`
- [x] **Pull Request Contents:** Documents the current implementation, commands, limitations, and validation results.

</details>

items.title: [Model] Add LoRA support for PaddleOCR-VL
items.body:
## Purpose

Enable LoRA and multi-LoRA serving for PaddleOCR-VL
(`vllm/model_executor/models/paddleocr_vl.py`). Related to #48019.

Currently `
vllm serve PaddlePaddle/PaddleOCR-VL --enable-lora` accepts
PEFT adapters but they silently never affect inference: the model class
does not implement `SupportsLoRA`, and its `hf_to_vllm_mapper` lacks the
prefix rule for adapters trained against the native transformers class
(`PaddleOCRVLModel.language_model`). Such adapters carry keys like
`model.language_model.layers.N.*`, which the existing rule
`"model." -> "language_model.model."` rewrites to the nonexistent
`language_model.model.language_model.*`, so no module is matched and the
request is served by the base model.

Scope: text-LoRA only (the adapter targets the ERNIE-4.5 language model).
Tower/connector LoRA (`--enable-tower-connector-lora`) is out of scope;
the SigLIP vision tower receives no LoRA injection.

## Changes

1. `PaddleOCRVLForConditionalGeneration` now inherits `SupportsLoRA`.
2. Add mapper rule `"model.language_model." -> "language_model.model."`,
   placed before the generic `"model."` rule (prefix rules are applied
   sequentially; the specific rule must win).
3. Add `packed_modules_mapping` for the fused `qkv_proj` / `gate_up_proj`
   modules (Ernie4.5 follows the Llama layout).
4. Add `embedding_modules` (`embed_tokens` / `lm_head`).
5. Mark LoRA support in `docs/models/supported_models.md`.

## Test Plan

```
vllm serve PaddlePaddle/PaddleOCR-VL \
--enable-lora --max-loras 3 --max-lora-rank 32 \
--lora-modules adapter1=<adapter1-path> adapter2=<adapter2-path> adapter3=<adapter3-path>
```

- `/v1/models` lists base + all 3 adapters; routing via the `model` field.
- base / adapter1 / adapter2 / adapter3 requests on the same image,
  interleaved in one batch: base output byte-identical to no-LoRA
  serving; adapter outputs differ from base and match offline HF+PEFT
  inference on sampled cases.
- Server logs show non-null `lora_id` on adapter requests.

## Test Result

Environment: vLLM v0.31.0 (patched with this PR) + torch 2.13.0+cu130,
serving PaddleOCR-VL with 3 LoRA adapters (rank 32) via
`--enable-lora --max-loras 3 --max-lora-rank 32`.

1. **Adapter loading**: startup logs show `Loaded new LoRA adapter` for
   all 3 adapters; the LoRA compute kernels (`_lora_shrink_kernel`,
   `_lora_expand_kernel`) are JIT-compiled and exercised during
   inference, confirming the LoRA path is taken.
2. **Routing**: `GET /v1/models` lists the base model and all 3 adapters;
   requests are routed by the OpenAI-compatible `model` field.
3. **Base non-regression**: with the same image/prompt, the base route of
   the multi-LoRA server produces byte-identical output to a vanilla
   base-only server (no `--enable-lora`).
4. **LoRA effect**: the same image sent to base vs. each LoRA route yields
   distinct outputs — base returns raw OCR text while each adapter
   returns its task-specific structured JSON.
5. **Offline parity**: 15 images per adapter, compared field-by-field
   against offline HF+PEFT inference baselines:
   - adapter1: 15/15 identical (10 fields)
   - adapter2: 14/15 identical; the single mismatch is a one-character OCR
     ambiguity that also varies across runs of the offline baseline
     itself (unrelated to LoRA adapter loading)
   - adapter3: 15/15 identical

Note: This PR was prepared with AI assistance.

items.title: [Model] Support every Decision 3.0 size (d3-flash, d3-mini, d3-nano, d3-lite, d3-edge)

labels.name: ready
labels.description: ONLY add when PR is ready to merge/full CI is needed

items.body:
## Overview

Make every Decision 3.0 model work in vLLM: `vllm serve vllm-sr/d3-nano` stopped while loading weights, and d3-flash, d3-lite, d3-mini and d3-edge had no published validation on current vLLM. Follow-up to #61565, which added Decision 3.0 and validated d3, d3-mini and d3-edge; its "Follow-ups" section promised this PR.

## Claims

- **d3-nano loads.** Its checkpoint has one `model.safetensors` and no weight index, so the default loader also read `readout.safetensors` as a backbone file and stopped with `ValueError: There is no module or parameter named 'weight' in D3ForSequenceClassification`. `D3ForSequenceClassification` now names the readout's only tensor in `is_unused_checkpoint_weight`, so the backbone pass skips that file; the readout still loads as the FP32 `score` head through `secondary_weights`.
- **All five sizes give the checkpoint runtime's decisions** with `vllm serve vllm-sr/<model>` and no flags, on one AMD Instinct MI300X: 0 to 2 of 416 decisions changed per model, all near-ties (the reference's two most likely answers within 0.015 of each other), with a median probability difference of 0.003 (table below).
- **Throughput.** At 8 and 64 closed-loop clients vLLM serves 2.0x to 3.6x the requests per second of the checkpoint's own server on the mixed text / image / video load; one request at a time it is 7 % to 32 % slower (each question is its own engine request).
- The docs list all six models, the GPU test runs d3-nano next to d3-edge, and the test registry lists every size.

## Validation

**Setup**: one AMD Instinct MI300X (ROCm 7.2), a new `rocm/dev-ubuntu-24.04:7.2.3-complete` container with empty caches. vLLM is the ROCm nightly wheel `0.32.0rc1.dev190+g3f1bcfd82` (it contains #61565, and every file on the Decision 3.0 path is identical to `main`) with this PR's `d3.py` copied over the installed one; no kernels were built. The reference is the checkpoint's own runtime, `AutoModel.from_pretrained(..., trust_remote_code=True)`, with the versions its `requirements.txt` pins (torch 2.13.0+rocm7.1, transformers 5.17.0, flash-linear-attention 0.5.2), in its own venv on the same GPU. Checkpoints at their current `main`: `vllm-sr/d3-edge` @ cab71e6a, `vllm-sr/d3-lite` @ 9c107031, `vllm-sr/d3-nano` @ aeb70d4d, `vllm-sr/d3-mini` @ 97dd054d, `vllm-sr/d3-flash` @ 8b35c853.

**Reproducer**: in the same container, the unchanged nightly fails on d3-nano and this PR loads it:

```bash
vllm serve vllm-sr/d3-nano
# nightly 0.32.0rc1.dev190+g3f1bcfd82:
#   ValueError: There is no module or parameter named 'weight' in D3ForSequenceClassification
# with this PR: ready, and the agreement set below
```

**Answers vs the reference**: the same 416 questions as #61565 (3 states x 128 typed questions, 1-, 4- and 16-question text, a 4-question JSON state, a 40-option choice, an image with 1 and 4 questions, and a 10 s 1080p video). The decision is the top choice, `noul >= 0.5`, or a score's most likely level; |dp| is the largest absolute probability difference over a question's options.

| Model | Decisions changed | Median abs dp | p90 | Max | Image / video questions, max abs dp |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| d3-edge (0.59B) | 0 / 416 | 0.0030 | 0.0122 | 0.034 | 0.0071 |
| d3-lite (0.85B) | 1 / 416 (reference margin 0.0149) | 0.0031 | 0.0097 | 0.022 | 0.0182 |
| d3-nano (2.21B) | 1 / 416 (reference margin 0.0028) | 0.0028 | 0.0094 | 0.030 | 0.0300 |
| d3-mini (4.54B) | 1 / 416 (reference margin 0.0042) | 0.0028 | 0.0076 | 0.042 | 0.0192 |
| d3-flash (8.39B) | 2 / 416 (reference margins 0.0128, 0.0077) | 0.0027 | 0.0077 | 0.020 | 0.0104 |

**Throughput**: closed loop, 20 s per level after an 8 s warm-up, over the mix of #61565 (40 % one-question text, 20 % four-question text, 10 % four-question JSON, 10 % 40-option choice, 15 % new 1.6 MP image, 5 % new 10 s 1080p video; every image and video carries new bytes). The checkpoint server is the package's `d3_server.py` (AutoModel behind HTTP). Each cell gives req/s and p50 / p90 latency in ms:

| Model | Side | 1 client | 8 clients | 64 clients |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| d3-edge | checkpoint server | 18.7 (12 / 89) | 36.5 (187 / 341) | 26.9 (2,108 / 2,569) |
| d3-edge | vLLM | 16.1 (17 / 85) | 72.0 (34 / 302) | 61.5 (36 / 4,233) |
| d3-lite | checkpoint server | 15.9 (25 / 102) | 24.6 (285 / 457) | 19.2 (2,863 / 3,104) |
| d3-lite | vLLM | 10.8 (36 / 107) | 59.7 (81 / 229) | 59.5 (94 / 4,213) |
| d3-nano | checkpoint server | 14.2 (26 / 125) | 20.7 (358 / 521) | 16.5 (3,192 / 3,677) |
| d3-nano | vLLM | 11.1 (32 / 113) | 52.8 (94 / 254) | 59.8 (235 / 3,699) |
| d3-mini | checkpoint server | 11.4 (33 / 147) | 16.2 (449 / 671) | 12.7 (3,953 / 4,276) |
| d3-mini | vLLM | 10.4 (32 / 135) | 37.1 (167 / 360) | 35.7 (1,585 / 2,031) |
| d3-flash | checkpoint server | 10.7 (34 / 203) | 11.2 (698 / 934) | 9.3 (5,126 / 5,480) |
| d3-flash | vLLM | 9.9 (32 / 169) | 24.6 (297 / 485) | 20.8 (2,706 / 3,130) |

**Start-up**: vLLM's launch to the first answer from empty caches, the model download included: 132 to 172 s (d3-edge 140 s, d3-lite 136 s, d3-nano 132 s, d3-mini 163 s, d3-flash 172 s).

**Tests**

- `pytest tests/models/multimodal/pooling/test_d3.py` (MI300X, this PR): `[vllm-sr/d3-edge]` PASSED, `[vllm-sr/d3-nano]` PASSED (2 passed in 270 s). Without this PR, d3-nano fails at load as in the reproducer.
- `pytest tests/config/test_model_arch_config.py tests/models/test_registry.py tests/entrypoints/generate/structured_decisions/test_strategies.py -k "decision_config or joint_head or D3 or d3 or strategy_selection"` (MI300X, this PR): 13 passed.
- CPU check of `DefaultModelLoader.get_all_weights` on a d3-nano-like layout (`model.safetensors` with backbone tensors plus `readout.safetensors`, no index): on main the backbone pass yields the readout's root `weight`; with this PR it yields only the backbone tensors, and `score.weight` still comes from `secondary_weights`.
- vLLM CI on NVIDIA, Buildkite #95083 (H200, MIG 18 GB, the multimodal pooling step): `test_d3.py` `[vllm-sr/d3-edge]` and `[vllm-sr/d3-nano]` PASSED; the d3-nano run logs `Skipped 1/2 safetensors shard(s) holding no weights the model loads`.
- `pre-commit run --from-ref origin/main --to-ref HEAD`: all hooks pass (actionlint skipped locally; no workflow files changed).

## Details

- **Root cause**: without `model.safetensors.index.json`, `DefaultModelLoader._prepare_weights` keeps every `*.safetensors` file of the repo (`filter_duplicate_safetensors_files` returns them all when the index is missing), so `readout.safetensors` ({`weight`: [255, hidden]}) joins the backbone pass. Its root key `weight` matches no module, and `AutoWeightsLoader` raises. The other five checkpoints ship an index that lists only the backbone shards, so the index filter already drops the readout there. d3-nano is the only Decision 3.0 repo without an index.
- **Fix**: `is_unused_checkpoint_weight` is the existing hook the default loader passes to `filter_safetensors_files_by_weight_name` for the primary weights only; it drops a safetensors file when every tensor in it is unused. The readout file holds a single tensor named `weight`, which no backbone checkpoint has at the root. Its own `secondary_weights` source sets no such rule and keeps loading it under the `score.` prefix. For indexed checkpoints nothing changes beyond reading the shard headers, which the loader already does for pooling models (their protocol default returns False).
- **Alternatives considered**: `allow_patterns_overrides=["model*.safetensors"]` would also skip the index filter and depend on file names; adding an index to the Hub repo fixes only that copy of the checkpoint.
- **CI**: `test_d3.py` runs in the optional "Multimodal Models (Extended Pooling)" step; d3-nano adds a 4.5 GB checkpoint there. d3-lite, d3-mini and d3-flash take the same code path as d3-edge and d3-nano and are covered by the measurements above rather than CI, to keep the step's downloads and run time small.
- **Not measured**: agreement and throughput on NVIDIA GPUs (only the CI test above ran there; no NVIDIA GPU was available to me), tensor parallelism, LoRA.
- **Not a duplicate**: no open or closed PR or issue covers d3-nano or the other sizes (searched for Decision 3.0, `vllm-sr/d3`, d3-nano, `D3ForSequenceClassification`, `decision_config`); #61565 is merged.
- **AI assistance** was used for the code, tests, measurements and this description.

items.body:
## Overview

Adds native serving for Nemotron Parse 3.5's causal visual-prefix architecture and a one-token auxiliary MTP proposer. This extends the Parse model implementation; related earlier-model speculative work is [#51168](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/51168).

## Claims

- Register RadioMBartPrefixForCausalLM and process variable-resolution packed RADIO images with content-normalized positional embeddings and visual-prefix placeholder expansion.
- Add ParseAuxMTPModel, loading the checkpoint's integrated auxiliary projections and routing causal-prefix configurations to one speculative token on Model Runner V2.
- Extend HF/vLLM generation coverage to Parse 3.5 and add five MTP configuration/loading/sharing contract tests to Basic Models CI. End-to-end MTP correctness and speedup remain unvalidated.
- Older generations of Nemotron-Parse are still supported.

## Validation

Tests ran locally. The nemotron-3.5-parse (with and without mtp) and nemotron-parse-2.0 accuracy verified on internal benchmarks. Parse 3.5 mtp acceptance rate is verified at various concurrencies. Tested on A100, H100. 

## Details

New nemotron-3.5-parse model uses an updated architecture which the current vllm implementation does not support. To simplify the change, created a new nemotron_parse3_5.py implementation while leaving code for previous versions unchanged. Major differences compared to previous implementation and approaches taken for implementations: 
1. New model uses visual prefix and removes cross-attention. 
add_cross_attention field controls whether to add cross-attention in decoder layer. Parse 3.5 implementation in vllm only supports checkpoints that has it set to False (as official checkpoint). Added a hard fail check that nemotron-3.5-parse models have it set to False. 
2. New model uses GQA vs old model using MHA.
Since WhisperAttention does not support GQA, created a local attention implementation that copies Whisper but adds GQA support. Can instead add GQA support to Whisper, but this increases common-code change. 
3. New model uses dynamic-size vision encoder with packed batching (NaVit-style) vs old model using static resolution. 
New RadioMBartPrefixForCausalLM and pre-processing. Parse 3.5 is not using device-side preprocessing for parse 3.5 for simplicity (d1d8e6c). 
4. New model uses a different version of RADIO encoder.
Added RADIOv4-SO400M parameters to RADIO file. Model: https://huggingface.co/nvidia/C-RADIOv4-SO400M

## Known limitations and future work

1. Only V2 runner is supported for mtp-enabled parse 3.5. V1 runner fails because it expects kv-cache in the speculator and parse mtp does not have attention. 
2. RADIO dynamic packing causes a sync on . This code is reused between models, so leaving it as-is for this PR. The torch.tensor constructor should be replaced with async copy in the future. Will submit separate PR. 
3. Nemotron-3.5-Parse is currently not public, so the 3.5-specific tests are disabled. Those tests and additional validation for parse 3.5 was ran locally.

items.title: [XPU] Add Qwen4Exp (Qwen3.8-Flash-Next) model architecture support
items.body:
# [XPU] Add Qwen4Exp (Qwen3.8-Flash-Next) model architecture support

  Adds the `xpu/` sibling to the existing `amd/` and `nvidia/` implementations under
  `vllm/models/qwen4_exp/`, routed through the existing platform dispatch. It reuses
  `Qwen3NextAttention`, `QwenGatedDeltaNetAttention` and `Qwen3NextSparseMoeBlock`, so
  it is much smaller than the other two backends.

  **Changes outside the model package**

  - `speculator.py` / `llm_base_proposer.py` - the MTP hidden buffer was widened via
    `hc_mult` (the DeepSeek-V4 spelling). Qwen4Exp calls it `hc_count`, so the `getattr`
    fell back to 1 and the MTP head got an un-widened buffer. Both names now accepted.
  - `inc_wna16_linear.py` - guard the `qzeros` copy, which can be empty or mismatched
    under symmetric group quantization and crashed weight load on the 512 routed experts.

  **`layer_types`** - Transformers v5.18 renames `full_attention` to `indexed_attention`;
  all three spellings map to the dense GQA block here. This does not branch on
  `indexer_n_heads` like `amd/`/`nvidia/` do: on `Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-W4A16` that field is
  set (`4`) but the checkpoint ships no indexer tensors, so keying off it would pick a QSA
  path the weights cannot feed.

  **Known limitations** - no QSA/indexer path on XPU (such checkpoints fail at weight load
  rather than silently running dense attention); TP=4 needs `--enable-expert-parallel`
  (`moe_intermediate_size=640 / 4 = 160` is not divisible by `group_size=128` - checkpoint
  arithmetic, not an XPU limit); requires `transformers >= 5.16.1`, same as the other
  backends; TP=4 validated with `--enforce-eager` only.
  
**model** - https://huggingface.co/devan-carlin/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-W4A16

items.body:
## Overview Fixes the NIXL KV-transfer crash when a P/D disaggregated deployment uses **heterogeneous TP** (e.g. prefill TP16 + decode TP8) with a **mixed MLA** model — a model that combines a replicated MLA latent cache with head-sharded attention regions (GLM-5.3 `GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM` with `sparse_mla_force_mqa`, i.e. MLA + DSA sparse-attention indexer). Extends the per-region classification introduced in #44583 to heterogeneous-TP page geometry. ## Claims - Heterogeneous P/D TP works for mixed MLA models: prefill TP16 + decode TP8 and prefill TP8 + decode TP16 both complete full benchmarks with correct output quality. - Pure-MLA (DeepSeek-class), pure-GQA, and symmetric-TP deployments keep their existing behavior — every change is gated on conditions only hybrid + mixed-TP produce. - Measured on GLM-5.3 785B fp8 (8xH200): `1P×TP16 + 2D×TP8` = 0.81 req/s vs 0.48 req/s for the best symmetric split (**+68%**) — prefill is compute-bound (wider TP wins) while decode is latency-bound (smaller TP group wins); heterogeneous TP lets each role sit at its optimum. ## Validation Live on an 8xH200 cluster, GLM-5.3 785B fp8, full request-load benchmarks per config: - D>P (prefill TP8 + decode TP16): EPP registration 3s, full benchmark, quality ok - D

Failure signature (before the fix) ``` ValueError: Replicated region i=99 local_len=8192 remote_len=16384 (NIXL handshake validation, decode engine, first request) ``` followed, after each layer was fixed in sequence, by descriptor-size mismatches and finally a multi-source read assertion in `pull_worker`. Performance evidence and the full 11-iteration investigation: internal benchmarking on ServeIt Studio (GLM-5.3 asymmetric TP analysis).

items.body:
## Overview

Serve the Decision 3.0 decision models ([`vllm-sr/d3`](https://huggingface.co/vllm-sr/d3) and its smaller variants such as `vllm-sr/d3-mini` and `vllm-sr/d3-edge`) from their Hub checkpoints as they are: `vllm serve vllm-sr/d3`, then ask typed questions on `/v1/systemone`. Today these checkpoints do not load in vLLM (`Qwen3_5Model` is not a registered architecture and the readout is a separate file). This builds on vLLM's Qwen3.5 implementation, the structured decisions API (#60465 and its predecessors) and the Clef-Flash detection pattern (#61308).

## Claims

- **The published checkpoints load unchanged** (measured here: d3, d3-mini and d3-edge; see Follow-ups). A bare `Qwen3_5Model` checkpoint that ships a `decision_config.json` is detected and served as `D3ForSequenceClassification`. The 255-row answer-code readout (`readout.safetensors`) becomes the FP32 `score` head. The declared `noncausal_full_attention` makes the full attention layers bidirectional, while the Gated DeltaNet layers stay causal. Tied embeddings need nothing, and per-model `layer_types` are honoured (d3-edge: `llFllFllFFFF`).
- **`/v1/systemone` gives the checkpoint runtime's answers.** For each question, `D3Strategy` writes the prompt the checkpoint's own `d3_format.py` writes (byte-identical on 416 prompts), reads the question's codes from the classify head, and applies the option mask and the checkpoint temperature. It supports choice (up to 255 options), yes / no and score questions, text and JSON states, and images and videos read with the runtime's budgets (1.6 MP images; 2 fps, at most 32 frames of 0.2 MP).
- **Same decisions as the reference runtime on AMD Instinct MI325X.** Against `AutoModel.from_pretrained(..., trust_remote_code=True)`: 0 of 416 decisions changed on d3, 1 on d3-mini and 2 on d3-edge, all ties or near-ties. The median probability difference is 0.0024 to 0.0029.
- **Throughput.** On a mixed text / JSON / image / video load at 8 and 64 closed-loop clients, vLLM sustains 1.4x to 2.6x the rate of the checkpoint's own server (AutoModel behind HTTP, one request at a time).

## Validation

Hardware and software: one AMD Instinct MI325X per side. vLLM used the official ROCm nightly image `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-5555a2d8f7116b2b4877f66516f4128176cf722a` (PyTorch 2.13, ROCm 7.2), with this branch's Python tree (main `f4b8d43a6` plus this PR) overlaid; no kernels were built. The reference used the same image with the versions the checkpoint pins (transformers 5.17.0, flash-linear-attention 0.5.2). vLLM ran with no flags: `vllm serve vllm-sr/<model>`. Models: `vllm-sr/d3` @ fc2d74bd, `vllm-sr/d3-mini` @ 6d8971f4, `vllm-sr/d3-edge` @ fe71f8e1.

**Answers vs the reference** (`model.system_one(...)` in process): 416 questions per model, namely 3 states (a support ticket, release notes, a JSON account) x 128 typed questions (48 choice, 40 yes / no, 40 score), plus 1-, 4- and 16-question text, a 4-question JSON state, a 40-option choice, an image with 1 and 4 questions, and a 10 s 1080p video. The decision is the top choice, `noul >= 0.5`, or a score's most likely level; |dp| is the largest absolute probability difference over a question's options.

| Model | Decisions changed | Median abs dp | p90 | Max | Image / video questions, max abs dp |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| d3 (27B) | 0 / 416 | 0.0024 | 0.0078 | 0.027 | 0.0049 / 0.021 |
| d3-mini (4B) | 1 / 416 (0.5003 vs 0.4996) | 0.0026 | 0.0078 | 0.032 | 0.018 / 0.032 |
| d3-edge (0.6B) | 2 / 416 (margins 0.0019, 0.0012) | 0.0029 | 0.012 | 0.043 | 0.0050 / 0.0055 |

For scale, two vLLM configurations of d3 (defaults vs `--max-model-len 32768`, so different batch shapes) differ from each other by up to 0.011 and change 2 decisions.

**Throughput and latency**: closed loop, 30 s per level after an 8 s warm-up, over a mix of 40 % one-question text, 20 % four-question text, 10 % four-question JSON state, 10 % 40-option choice, 15 % new 1.6 MP image and 5 % new 10 s 1080p video. Every image and video carries new bytes. Each cell gives req/s and p50 / p90 latency in ms:

| Model | Side | 1 client | 8 clients | 64 clients |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| d3 | checkpoint server | 6.9 (69 / 290) | 6.1 (1,210 / 1,653) | 4.6 (9,300 / 9,817) |
| d3 | vLLM | 6.7 (74 / 265) | 8.6 (903 / 1,228) | 8.5 (5,907 / 6,552) |
| d3-mini | checkpoint server | 17.0 (23 / 123) | 23.3 (339 / 499) | 18.3 (3,157 / 3,427) |
| d3-mini | vLLM | 15.8 (30 / 103) | 43.0 (166 / 273) | 45.0 (1,357 / 1,606) |
| d3-edge | checkpoint server | 31.6 (7.4 / 66) | 47.3 (141 / 306) | 41.7 (1,463 / 1,724) |
| d3-edge | vLLM | 28.6 (10 / 56) | 102 (23 / 211) | 110 (36 / 2,679) |

One request at a time (p50 ms, AutoModel in process / vLLM):

| Model | 1 text question | 16 text questions | new image, 1 question | new image, 4 questions | new 10 s video |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| d3 | 55.9 / 54.9 | 583 / 547 | 293 / 216 | 1,020 / 700 | 519 / 443 |
| d3-mini | 18.1 / 19.4 | 114 / 116 | 111 / 64 | 341 / 158 | 319 / 261 |
| d3-edge | 6.4 / 7.0 | 21.2 / 29.0 | 56 / 33 | 140 / 48 | 266 / 234 |

**Start-up and memory** (launch to the first answer; cold = empty compile caches, model files on local disk):

| Model | AutoModel cold / warm | vLLM cold / warm | GPU memory above idle, steady: AutoModel / vLLM |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| d3 | 39.9 / 22.0 s | 214.5 / 130.0 s (`--max-model-len 32768`: 139.0 / 67.8 s, same throughput) | 52 / 199 GiB |
| d3-mini | 28.6 / 10.5 s | 136.2 / 61.7 s | 11 / 216 GiB |
| d3-edge | 27.0 / 8.2 s | 129.2 / 37.1 s | 3.5 / 227 GiB |

**Tests**

- `pytest tests/models/multimodal/pooling/test_d3.py`: d3-edge vs the checkpoint runtime, with text prompts as token ids (including a 40-option choice) and one image prompt processed by vLLM. PASSED on MI325X (134 s).
- `pytest tests/config/test_model_arch_config.py -k "decision_config or joint_head"`: 8 passed.
- `pytest tests/entrypoints/generate/structured_decisions/`: 115 passed, including the new d3 strategy tests.
- `pytest tests/models/test_registry.py tests/models/test_initialization.py -k D3`: 2 passed.
- `pre-commit run` on the diff: all hooks pass. actionlint was skipped locally because no workflow files changed.

## Details

- **Detection** follows Clef-Flash: `Qwen3_5ModelArchConfigConvertor` maps `architectures: ["Qwen3_5Model"]` plus `decision_config.json` to `D3ForSequenceClassification` and keeps the decision config on `hf_config`. Bare `Qwen3_5Model` checkpoints without that file are unaffected (they stay unsupported, as today).
- **Config hook** `D3ForSequenceClassificationConfig` validates `format_version` 1, `pooling: last` and the attention mode. It sets `is_causal=False` for `noncausal_full_attention`, so chunked prefill and prefix caching turn off by themselves, sets `id2label` to the 255 codes, and makes the classify head return raw code logits by default. Probabilities only exist over a question's own options, so `/classify` and `/pooling` callers mask and normalize themselves.
- **Model** (`d3.py`): `as_seq_cls_model(Qwen3_5ForConditionalGeneration)`, so no LM head is allocated and the `score` head is FP32. It adds a mapper for the bare-backbone keys, `readout.safetensors` as `score.weight` via `secondary_weights`, and a processing info that applies the runtime's media budgets. The checkpoint's processor config allows 16.7 MP images, while the runtime reads at most 1.6 MP; video frames use transformers' `cap_pixels_per_frame` with the runtime's 200,704-pixel cap.
- **Strategy**: one classify read per question. The media come first, so they are processed once per request and shared by its questions, and the encoder cache deduplicates the vision tower. Videos go through the existing `qwen3_vl` loader, whose sampling rule already matches the runtime's, with `max_frames=32`. A small change to the question builder, `DecisionLimits.labeled`, lets label-free strategies accept more options than the A to Z label set; the defaults of other strategies are unchanged.
- **Why not an example client**: the System One API already has question types on main, so the option mask and temperature belong in the strategy rather than in client code.
- **Tradeoffs and limits**
  - Start-up: with chunked prefill off, the profiling pass runs one `max_model_len`-token sequence. At the config's 262,144 tokens this dominates start-up (71 s of d3's 130 s warm start). `--max-model-len 32768` halves it, with no throughput change on this mix.
  - Memory: vLLM reserves `--gpu-memory-utilization` (0.92) of HBM. The Gated DeltaNet layers still keep per-request state, and the attention layers keep no KV.
  - Media under load: at 64 clients, text stays fast (d3-edge text p90 about 80 ms) while image and video requests queue (image p50 2.65 s), because decoding a new 300-frame 1080p video per request is CPU-bound. `--renderer-num-workers 4` did not change this.
  - Small-model latency: one request at a time, multi-question requests on the small models are slower than in process (d3-edge, 16 questions: 29.0 vs 21.2 ms), since each question is its own engine request.
  - API differences from the runtime: a request with an invalid or too-long question returns 400 instead of per-question errors; at most 64 questions per request (the API's limit); `confidence` and `usage` follow `/v1/systemone`'s definitions; option descriptions, instructions and score levels are rendered as text (non-string values go through `str`, where the runtime writes JSON); the runtime's optional `permutation_average` is not available.
  - Not measured: d3-flash, d3-nano and d3-lite (same layout and code path), CUDA GPUs, tensor parallelism, LoRA.
- **Not a duplicate**: no open or closed PR or issue covers these checkpoints, `decision_config.json` readout checkpoints, or bare `Qwen3_5Model` loading (searched for d3, Decision 3.0, `Qwen3_5Model`, `decision_config.json`, decider, readout). The Laya PR (#58429) adds an unrelated ModernBERT-based model.
- **AI assistance** was used for the code, tests, measurements and this description. The PR stays a draft until the submitter has reviewed every line.

## Follow-ups

- **The other five Decision 3.0 models** (`vllm-sr/d3-flash`, `vllm-sr/d3-mini`, `vllm-sr/d3-nano`, `vllm-sr/d3-lite`, `vllm-sr/d3-edge`) share d3's architecture and take the same code path: each Hub checkpoint is a bare `Qwen3_5Model` with a `d3-code-readout-v1` `decision_config.json` (`noncausal_full_attention`, 255 codes) and a `readout.safetensors`. The variations between them, tied embeddings and d3-edge's layer layout, are exercised by d3-mini and d3-edge.
- **d3-mini and d3-edge** already match the reference in this PR's measurements (1 and 2 of 416 decisions changed, all ties or near-ties; see the agreement and throughput tables under Validation).
- **A follow-up PR** will validate d3-flash, d3-nano and d3-lite, publish agreement and throughput for all five, and add them explicitly to the docs examples and tests where it makes sense.

items.title: [Spec Decode][MRV2] Support heterogeneous-vocab draft models (TLI)
items.body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

This PR brings back draft models with a different tokenizer than the target, `use_heterogeneous_vocab=True` from #38174, and implements them on Model Runner V2. #63373 removed V1 and dropped this option with it, because only V1 supported it, and asked whether to land before porting the dropped features. This PR is that port for TLI, the item still marked TBD in #47172.

## Claims

- `method="draft_model"` with `use_heterogeneous_vocab=True` is accepted again and handled by the MRV2 standalone drafter. The config option, its checks, `VocabMapping` and its unit tests come back as they were before #63373, apart from docstring formatting.
- The id mapping lives in `StandaloneARSpeculator` and is written for the draft CUDA graphs from #60989. It has not run on a GPU since the rebase, see Validation.
- Before the rebase, while V1 still existed, acceptance length on V2 matched V1 for both directions of vocab mismatch, and GSM8K accuracy stayed within noise of the target alone.

## Validation

Since the rebase I have only run the CPU checks. The GPU numbers further down are from the first version of this PR and have not been rerun on this commit.

On this commit, on CPU, with vLLM installed with `VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=empty`:

```bash
pre-commit run --files $(git diff --name-only origin/main)
# every hook passed, including mypy, the docstring check and the Buildkite test wiring check
pytest tests/test_config.py -k heterogeneous_vocab -v
# test_heterogeneous_vocab_draft_model_config PASSED
pytest tests/v1/spec_decode/test_vocab_mapping.py -q
# 11 passed, 6 skipped
```

The 6 skipped cases need CUDA. With the code files reverted to main and the tests kept, the config test fails with `unexpected_keyword_argument`, and `test_vocab_mapping.py` fails with `No module named 'vllm.v1.spec_decode.vocab_mapping'`.

The e2e test now runs with `enforce_eager` set to both True and False, so CI also runs it with the draft CUDA graphs enabled, in the Spec Decode Draft Model step. `test_vocab_mapping.py`, including its CUDA no-sync checks, runs in the V1 Spec Decode step.

<details>
<summary>GPU results from the first version (main 624a5dd, 1x L4)</summary>

The MRV2 drafter had no CUDA graphs yet, and V1 still existed.

```bash
pytest tests/v1/spec_decode/test_vocab_mapping.py -q
# 17 passed
pytest tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/draft_model/test_draft_model.py -k heterogeneous_vocab -v -s
# acceptance_len=1.920
# exact text matches=96/100 (required=61)
# 1 passed
pytest tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/draft_model/test_draft_model.py -k "correctness or realistic" -v
# 5 passed
```

GSM8K, 500 questions, greedy, k=3, all prompts submitted at once. AL is the mean acceptance length from the spec decode metrics.

| Target | Draft | Runner | GSM8K | AL | tok/s |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct | none | V1 | 0.532 | | 3666 |
| Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct | none | V2 | 0.532 | | 3724 |
| Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct | SmolLM2-360M-Instruct | V1 | 0.542 | 2.11 | 1771 |
| Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct | SmolLM2-360M-Instruct | V2 | 0.524 | 2.11 | 1832 |
| SmolLM2-1.7B-Instruct | none | V1 | 0.458 | | 1859 |
| SmolLM2-1.7B-Instruct | none | V2 | 0.458 | | 1816 |
| SmolLM2-1.7B-Instruct | Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct | V1 | 0.448 | 3.13 | 2281 |
| SmolLM2-1.7B-Instruct | Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct | V2 | 0.454 | 3.12 | 2311 |

The first pair has a larger target vocab than the draft, 151,936 vs 49,152, and the second pair is the reverse. The SmolLM2 target ends right away on raw few-shot prompts, so its rows use chat prompts. The standard error at 500 questions is about 2 points.

Greedy outputs with drafting do not match the target alone token for token, with or without TLI, because verify computes k+1 rows at once while plain decode computes one, see #54506. With a same-vocab draft as a control, 242/500 and 296/500 outputs matched the target alone, and with TLI 247/500 and 289/500. Most first divergences fell where the target's top-2 logits were tied or one bf16 step apart: 80% and 96% for the control, 85% and 95% for TLI.

</details>

## Details

Ids cross between the two vocabularies at three points in `StandaloneARSpeculator.propose()`:

1. Target ids become draft ids in the expanded step-0 input buffer, in place, right after `prepare_prefill_inputs` and before the prefill runs or its CUDA graph replays. Every slot the kernel writes is mapped right away, so the padded tail never holds unmapped target ids. The dummy-run path that skips attention reads the target's own input ids, so it maps into a new tensor instead.
2. `compute_draft_logits` masks the logits outside the shared vocab, so the drafter only proposes tokens the target also has. In FULL CUDA graph mode this is captured with the rest of the draft step.
3. The proposals become target ids, in a preallocated buffer, right before `propose()` returns. Between draft steps the drafter keeps its own ids. Ids in the shared vocab map one to one, so the drafter sees the same inputs as with V1's per-step round trip.

`VocabMapping` and `test_vocab_mapping.py` are back at their old paths. The only edits are three docstring lines, for the backtick rule of the docstring hook. The config checks are the same as before #63373: `method="draft_model"` only, greedy draft sampling only, no `use_local_argmax_reduction`, and no equal vocab size check for TLI.

The target tokenizer is loaded with the target's tokenizer path, mode and revision. The draft tokenizer is loaded with the draft model's path and revision and mode `auto`, because the draft model config inherits the target's tokenizer mode and revision. #54780 fixes the same thing for the V1 proposer, which #63373 deleted.

The docs section and the `--use-heterogeneous-vocab` flag of `spec_decode_offline.py` are back too. The docs example now uses the model pair from the e2e test.

Not tested: TP > 1, PP, DP, dynamic speculative decoding, adaptive verification, prompt embeds, the path under `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error`, and the docs example and the example script on a GPU.

Duplicate check: #47172 still lists TLI as TBD, and no open PR ports TLI to MRV2. #54780 and #59012 fix the V1 proposer and `VocabMapping`. #61152 keeps target-only tokens with narrower draft vocabularies, and #67222 shares the d2t mapping of pruned EAGLE3, DFlash and DSpark heads. None of them adds TLI to MRV2.

This PR was written with AI assistance from Claude Code. I reviewed every changed line of the first version and ran its GPU tests myself. The rebase onto the MRV1 removal was done with Claude Code and checked with the CPU tests above.

items.title: [Model][DSV4.1] Support MXFP4-packed Engram embedding tables

labels.name: ready
labels.description: ONLY add when PR is ready to merge/full CI is needed

items.body:
## Overview

Support DeepSeek-V4.1 checkpoints with MXFP4 Engram tables: two E2M1 values per byte with UE8M0 block-32 scales. Checkpoint metadata selects the layout; existing FP8 checkpoints retain their default format.

## Claims

- Packed Engram tables load through GPU, peer-HBM, pinned host, huge-page, and DP-shared storage paths. Allocation and host-memory eligibility use the actual packed row width.
- MXFP4 reduces table storage from 264 to 136 bytes per 256-element row, including scales (48.5% less).
- Unsupported checkpoint block sizes, scale formats, and partial layer lists fail before table allocation. Packed-table FP8 output fails before kernel launch; DP exchange uses BF16.
- The DSpark TP4 GSM8K CI configuration exercises the published checkpoint without an old FP8 revision pin.

## Validation

Rebased onto `cb95d994f4ec066b75672035ca3ae7e1c9745e84`. OCI JHB, four NVIDIA GB300 GPUs, torch 2.14.0+cu130, editable Python source with the exact base commit's precompiled vLLM wheel.

- All pre-commit hooks passed.
- `python -m pytest -v tests/kernels/test_engram.py --timeout=180 --durations=10`: 139 passed, four existing platform skips.
- `python -m pytest -v tests/distributed/test_engram_dp_shard.py --timeout=1200 --durations=10`: 29 passed. Existing workers now cover both formats, including peer and non-peer GPU reads, host offload, cuMem success/fallback, sharding, loading, and graph replay.
- Targeted reversions demonstrate failures without metadata validation, packed meta allocation, the packed-output guard, and packed shared-memory sizing.
- Matched GSM8K: FP8 95.91%, MXFP4 96.74% (+0.83 percentage points), 1,319 unique responses each, 5-shot chat, temperature 0, seed 42, thinking disabled, max_tokens 4096. No empty or unparseable responses. FP8/MXFP4 hit the output cap 1/2 times; these remain scored by the native parser, so this is a measured comparison with an output-limit caveat.
- Unpinned DSpark TP4 CI entry: passed on all 1,319 questions, score 0.8984 (configured expectation 0.88 ± 0.03), invalid rate 0, mean acceptance length 3.527 (minimum 2.5). This uses the CI protocol and is separate from the matched 4,096-token chat comparison.
- Full MMLU: FP8 12,831/14,042 (91.38%), MXFP4 12,806/14,042 (91.20%), delta −0.18 percentage points. [OpenAI simple-evals](https://github.com/openai/simple-evals/tree/652c89d0ca9df547706735883097e9537d40dc47), full English set, zero-shot CoT prompt, temperature 0, seed 42, thinking disabled, max_tokens 8192, concurrency 32. Raw prompts and dataset hashes match; each arm made exactly 14,042 successful requests with no retries. FP8/MXFP4 had 5/7 unparseable answers, including 1/2 limit stops; all were retained and scored incorrect.
- Lookup microbenchmark: 96M rows × 256 values, 24 heads, CUPTI with cold L2 and CUDA graphs. At 8192 tokens, GPU-resident FP8/MXFP4 lookup measured 118.75/168.96 µs (42.3% slower packed); no additional GPU temporary memory from MXFP4. This is an isolated FP8-versus-MXFP4 lookup comparison, not a 42.3% end-to-end serving slowdown or a measured regression from the review fixes. The matched accuracy runs used default CPU-offloaded tables. Host-offload timing was cache-sensitive and is not used for a general speed claim.

The matched comparison uses `nvidia/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-NVFP4` revisions `3431dde3247c13b5957f682b1e3c6fcae2566079` (FP8 Engram) and `c48dca0146b56d64c8116dbb6fcace8b7cc835f8` (MXFP4 Engram). All 48 weight files per revision passed SHA256 verification against Hugging Face LFS metadata; only Engram shards 47/48 differ. Both retain NVFP4 expert weights. Tokenizer, encoding, and prompt-template files are identical. These are single-run measurements; no directly comparable external reference or acceptance threshold is claimed.

## Details

`EngramLayout` resolves and validates the format once. The lookup kernel reads packed bytes, decodes E2M1 nibbles, and applies the unchanged UE8M0 scales. Peer-buffer scale offsets and every allocation path use the packed row width. DP-shared storage uses the existing cuMem and shared-memory fallback mechanisms.

Enable the format in checkpoint metadata:

```json
{
  "quantization_config": {
    "engram_embed_quant": "mxfp4",
    "engram_embed_block_size": 32,
    "engram_embed_scale_dtype": "ue8m0",
    "engram_embed_layers": [1, 14]
  }
}
```

The layer list must match the checkpoint's `engram_layer_ids`. Mixed per-layer table formats and packed-table FP8 batched exchange are unsupported. ROCm test eligibility is enabled, but this validation used NVIDIA hardware; ROCm performance is unmeasured. Quark export mapping is separate follow-up work.

---

- [x] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill.
- [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR.
- [x] Design Fit: extends the existing layout, allocation, and lookup mechanisms.
- [x] Testing and Validation: focused GPU/distributed tests, matched accuracy, and DSpark CI completed.
- [x] Code Quality and Style: pre-commit passes; Engram documentation updated.
- [x] Pull Request Contents: includes verified checkpoint identity, protocol, results, and limitations.

items.title: [Model] Enable LoRA support for tower and connector in MiDashengLM
items.body:
## Overview

Enable LoRA on the Dasheng audio tower and `AudioProjectorSubsample` connector of MiDashengLM, built on the `get_mm_lora_token_counts` interface from #42662. Part of #31479; sibling audio-model PRs: #45697 (Voxtral), #45944 (Qwen2-Audio).

## Claims

- `MiDashengLMModel` now declares `SupportsLoRA` and `supports_tower_connector_lora`, with `get_mm_mapping` (`decoder` / `audio_encoder` / `audio_projector`). Adapters can target the Qwen2 decoder, the Dasheng tower (`qkv`, `proj`, `fc1`, `fc2`), and the projector (`net.0`, `net.2`); no encoder rewrite was needed since the tower already uses vLLM-native linears and the HF checkpoint's fused `qkv` maps to `QKVParallelLinearWithLoRA` without packing.
- With `--enable-tower-connector-lora`, every audio item is padded to a fixed 160000 samples, so the tower always runs 250 patches and the projector 50 rows per item for the 7B config, making the tower/connector punica token mappings exact under encoder batching.
- Covered by a processor-driven unit test (real `mispeech/midashenglm-7b` processor, awkward audio lengths whose patch counts are not multiples of the projector's subsample factor), plus end-to-end GPU validation with a tower+connector adapter on a variable-length multi-audio batch.

## Validation

On an A100 80GB (nightly `vllm==0.31.1rc1.dev376+g5555a2d8f.cu129`, torch 2.13.0+cu129, torchaudio 2.11.0+cu129, transformers 5.19.0, Python 3.12.3; the changed model file overlaid onto site-packages, tests tree shipped alongside):

**Unit test** (real `mispeech/midashenglm-7b` processor, no model weights):

```
tests/models/multimodal/test_midashenglm.py::test_mm_lora_token_counts_match_padded_tower_input[mispeech/midashenglm-7b] PASSED [100%]
======================= 1 passed, 14 warnings in 18.28s ========================
```

**End-to-end smoke** — randomly-initialized small-magnitude PEFT adapter targeting `qkv`/`fc1`/`fc2` (tower blocks 0/15/31), `net.0`/`net.2` (connector), and `q/k/v_proj` (decoder layer 0); batch of 3 prompts mixing audio lengths 0.37s / 3.3s+7.77s (two audios in one prompt) / 10.0s (patch counts 9, 82, 194, 250 — three of them not multiples of 5), `enforce_eager`, `gpu_memory_utilization=0.199` (16.7 GiB free on a shared box):

```
(EngineCore) WARNING [model_manager.py:273] LoRA for the tower and connector of multimodal models is experimental and may contain bugs. ...
=== generate WITH tower/connector LoRA ===
[lora 0..2] completed, 16 tokens each
=== generate WITHOUT LoRA (same engine, padded path) ===
[base 0..2] completed, identical ids to the LoRA pass (greedy argmax unchanged by the small random adapter)
=== SMOKE TEST PASSED ===
```

The adapter loads with every target wrapped (no `unexpected modules` error, no unwrapped-module or `does not support` warnings in the full log), and prefill through the LoRA-mapped tower/connector plus 16 decode steps complete without any punica shape/mapping assertion across the variable-length multi-audio batch — the property this PR is responsible for.

**Caveat (pre-existing, unrelated to this PR):** base MiDashengLM on current main emits only the untrained token id 151872 (text-only prompts included, top-1 logprob 0.0 vs −619 for rank 2). Verified pre-existing by rerunning with the pristine nightly `midashenglm.py` (same output), with no LoRA flags at all (byte-identical output, which also confirms the pad path changes nothing for non-LoRA use), and with `Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct` in the same environment (correct output, ruling out the env). Tracked in #61469; adapter-quality validation on this model is blocked on that fix, mapping/plumbing validation above is not.

<details>
<summary>Smoke-test script</summary>

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Functional smoke-test for MiDashengLM tower/connector LoRA (A100).

Validates the plumbing the PR touches, not adapter quality: with
`enable_tower_connector_lora` every audio is padded to 160000 samples, so the
tower/connector punica mappings built from `get_mm_lora_token_counts` must
match the rows the Dasheng/projector linears actually receive. A
randomly-initialized small-magnitude adapter targeting tower (qkv/fc1/fc2),
connector (net.0/net.2), and LM (q/k/v_proj) modules is enough: if the counts
or the wrapping were wrong, generation would throw a punica shape/mapping
error or the adapter load would report unexpected modules.

The batch mixes audio lengths whose patch counts are not multiples of the
projector's subsample factor (9, 82, 194 patches) with a full-length audio
(250 patches) across single- and multi-audio prompts.
"""

import faulthandler
import json

faulthandler.dump_traceback_later(2400, exit=True)

import numpy as np
import torch
from safetensors.torch import save_file

import vllm
from vllm.lora.request import LoRARequest

MODEL = "mispeech/midashenglm-7b"
SR = 16000
ADAPTER_DIR = "/tmp/mdsl_lora_val/rand_adapter"

# (in_features, out_features) per targeted module, from the 7B config:
# tower embed_dim=1280, mlp_ratio=4, subsample_factor=5, text hidden 3584,
# 28 heads / 4 kv heads, head_dim 128.
_TOWER_BLOCKS = [0, 15, 31]
_SHAPES: dict[str, tuple[int, int]] = {
    "audio_projector.net.0": (6400, 3584),
    "audio_projector.net.2": (3584, 3584),
    "decoder.model.layers.0.self_attn.q_proj": (3584, 3584),
    "decoder.model.layers.0.self_attn.k_proj": (3584, 512),
    "decoder.model.layers.0.self_attn.v_proj": (3584, 512),
}
for _i in _TOWER_BLOCKS:
    _SHAPES[f"audio_encoder.blocks.{_i}.attn.qkv"] = (1280, 3840)
    _SHAPES[f"audio_encoder.blocks.{_i}.mlp.fc1"] = (1280, 5120)
    _SHAPES[f"audio_encoder.blocks.{_i}.mlp.fc2"] = (5120, 1280)


def make_random_lora(out_dir: str) -> str:
    """Write a PEFT-format adapter with small random A/B matrices directly
    (no HF model load needed on the shared box)."""
    import os

    os.makedirs(out_dir, exist_ok=True)
    rank = 8
    rng = np.random.RandomState(0)
    tensors = {}
    for name, (fan_in, fan_out) in _SHAPES.items():
        tensors[f"base_model.model.{name}.lora_A.weight"] = torch.from_numpy(
            (rng.standard_normal((rank, fan_in)) * 0.01).astype(np.float16)
        )
        tensors[f"base_model.model.{name}.lora_B.weight"] = torch.from_numpy(
            (rng.standard_normal((fan_out, rank)) * 0.01).astype(np.float16)
        )
    save_file(tensors, f"{out_dir}/adapter_model.safetensors")
    config = {
        "peft_type": "LORA",
        "base_model_name_or_path": MODEL,
        "r": rank,
        "lora_alpha": 16,
        "lora_dropout": 0.0,
        "bias": "none",
        "task_type": "CAUSAL_LM",
        "target_modules": [
            "qkv", "fc1", "fc2", "net.0", "net.2",
            "q_proj", "k_proj", "v_proj",
        ],
    }
    with open(f"{out_dir}/adapter_config.json", "w") as f:
        json.dump(config, f, indent=2)
    return out_dir


def _audio(seconds: float, rng: np.random.RandomState):
    return ((rng.rand(int(seconds * SR)).astype(np.float32) - 0.5) * 0.1, SR)


def main() -> None:
    lora_path = make_random_lora(ADAPTER_DIR)

    free, total = torch.cuda.mem_get_info()
    free_gib = free / 1024**3
    print(f"GPU free: {free_gib:.1f} GiB / total {total / 1024**3:.1f} GiB")
    if free_gib < 15.0:
        raise SystemExit(f"ABORT: only {free_gib:.1f} GiB free (<15 GiB)")
    # Leave ~1 GiB headroom for the resident prod workload. The fp32
    # checkpoint runs as bf16 (~15.4 GiB weights), so this is tight on a
    # busy box; keep batching budgets small.
    gpu_util = round((free - 1.0 * 1024**3) / total, 3)
    print(f"gpu_memory_utilization={gpu_util}")

    llm = vllm.LLM(
        model=MODEL,
        dtype="bfloat16",
        trust_remote_code=True,
        enable_lora=True,
        max_loras=1,
        max_lora_rank=8,
        enable_tower_connector_lora=True,
        mm_processor_cache_gb=0,
        max_model_len=2048,
        max_num_batched_tokens=2048,
        max_num_seqs=4,
        limit_mm_per_prompt={"audio": 2},
        gpu_memory_utilization=gpu_util,
        enforce_eager=True,
    )

    rng = np.random.RandomState(0)
    span = "<|audio_bos|><|AUDIO|><|audio_eos|>"
    inputs = [
        {
            "prompt": f"{span}What do you hear?",
            "multi_modal_data": {"audio": [_audio(0.37, rng)]},
        },
        {
            "prompt": f"{span}{span}Compare the two clips.",
            "multi_modal_data": {"audio": [_audio(3.3, rng), _audio(7.77, rng)]},
        },
        {
            "prompt": f"{span}Describe this.",
            "multi_modal_data": {"audio": [_audio(10.0, rng)]},
        },
    ]
    # ignore_eos: the base model may emit EOS immediately on raw (non-chat)
    # prompts; force 8 decode steps so the LoRA-mapped decode path runs too.
    sp = vllm.SamplingParams(
        temperature=0, max_tokens=8, min_tokens=8, ignore_eos=True
    )

    print("=== generate WITH tower/connector LoRA ===")
    out = llm.generate(
        inputs, sp, lora_request=LoRARequest("rand_tower_conn", 1, lora_path)
    )
    assert len(out) == len(inputs)
    for i, o in enumerate(out):
        text = o.outputs[0].text
        assert len(o.outputs[0].token_ids) == 8
        print(f"[lora {i}] {text!r}")

    print("=== generate WITHOUT LoRA (same engine, padded path) ===")
    out = llm.generate(inputs, sp)
    assert len(out) == len(inputs)
    for i, o in enumerate(out):
        print(f"[base {i}] {o.outputs[0].text!r}")

    print("\n=== SMOKE TEST PASSED ===")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

</details>

## Details

- **Why fixed padding:** scheduled audio items are grouped and batched (`group_and_batch_mm_kwargs`) and `_parse_and_validate_audio_input` pads them to the batch max, so a per-item token count derived from the item's own length can never match the rows the tower linears actually process in a mixed-length batch. Padding every item to `_MAX_AUDIO_LENGTH` (the model's existing `get_max_audio_len`) mirrors Ultravox's `pad_audio_to_max_context` and is gated on `enable_tower_connector_lora` — zero impact when the flag is off.
- **Why this needed #42662:** the pre-#42662 hook (`get_num_mm_encoder_tokens(num_embeds)`) served runtime items and punica wrapper sizing through one formula. For MiDashengLM those must differ: runtime needs the per-item constant, while sizing needs a budget-scaled bound. The `mm_kwargs` parameter disambiguates the two calls.
- **Sizing bound:** placeholder counts are derived from each audio's true length (projector rows are `patches // 5`, floored), so unlike Voxtral's chunk-padded placeholders they cannot bound the number of items within the encoder budget — a batch of many short audios would overflow a full-item-scaled buffer. The sizing path therefore assumes worst-case one-embed items (`num_mm_embeds` items). Cost: tower punica index buffers sized at ~250x the encoder budget in int64 entries (tens of MB at default budgets), only when the flag is on. A follow-up could shrink this by passing the scheduler's max item count through the interface.
- **Limitation:** with the flag on, audio longer than 160000 samples (10s, the profiled max item) is rejected with a clear `ValueError`; without the flag, longer audio behaves as before. The rejection uses the standard `_parse_and_validate_audio_input` error path (like the Ultravox tower's over-long raise); rejecting at input-processing time instead would require LoRA-config visibility in `InputProcessingContext`, which could be a follow-up.
- **Not a duplicate:** as of 2026-10-13, `midashenglm.py` on main has no LoRA support, no open PR touches it for LoRA (searched `midashenglm lora`, `MiDashengLM`, PRs referencing #31479), and MiDashengLM is unclaimed on #31479.
- AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to draft this change; the submitter reviewed every line and ran the validation above.

items.body:
## Overview

Add native support for [Cloudflare/clef-flash](https://huggingface.co/Cloudflare/clef-flash) through `/v1/systemone`, reusing the Qwen3.5 backbone and the joint schema head introduced for Clef-Omni in #61064.

## Claims

- Automatically detect and load the separate joint schema head, scoring `choice`, `noul`, and `score` questions in one pooling request.
- Support text/JSON, images, and videos sampled at 2 fps. Match the release's fixed prompt, media separators, schema spans, and 16K truncation.
- Share the head/pooler between Clef-Flash and Clef-Omni. Flash rejects audio inputs and ignores video soundtracks.

## Validation

Compared the full checkpoint at revision `8b2e5fd17c09fd49bc2880b805d5323ec7ff4ff3` against the release's `joint_schema_model.py` in BF16. Ten model inputs covered invoice decisions, Unicode/empty instructions, a state truncated to 16K, one/two images, video, and image+video. Prompt token IDs and question/option spans matched the reference exactly in all ten cases.

Each mode ran the ten inputs once sequentially and twice at concurrency 4:

| Mode | Requests | Highest-probability option matches | Max absolute probability difference |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Eager | 30 | 57/57 | 0.001508 |
| Default compile | 30 | 57/57 | 0.000863 |

The four invoice threshold labels were correct in every repetition (12/12 per mode). These are synthetic model correctness checks. Probability normalization and input-token counts also matched; output-token counts were zero.

The reference evaluation used `encode_record`, `collate_records`, and `load_release_model(..., attn_implementation="sdpa")`, comparing each question's softmax probabilities against `/v1/systemone` responses. Serve the model with:

```bash
vllm serve Cloudflare/clef-flash \
  --served-model-name clef-flash --dtype bfloat16 \
  --max-model-len 16384 --max-num-batched-tokens 512 --max-num-seqs 8
# Add --enforce-eager for the eager comparison.
```

## Details

The checkpoint advertises `Qwen3_5ForConditionalGeneration` and supplies `joint_head_config.json` plus `joint_head.safetensors`. Architecture conversion detects that head, and the Flash wrapper uses the output embedding table for lexical option features, matching the reference implementation.

The existing Clef head/pooler is moved unchanged into `clef_joint_schema.py`. Flash shares the joint schema strategy's typed answers and span/truncation logic, with its own media rendering for adjacent placeholders and a single trailing newline.

Duplicate checks found no open Clef-Flash support PR. #61064 supports Clef-Omni; the other open Clef-related PRs concern API/frontend behavior.

Model comparisons cover BF16 with TP=1. Multi-GPU configurations, quantization, and the full Clef checkpoint were not evaluated.

AI assistance (Codex) was used to implement and validate this model support.

items.body:
## Overview

Enable LoRA for `BertForSequenceClassification` cross-encoders, e.g. `cross-encoder/ms-marco-MiniLM-L6-v2`. That includes PEFT `SEQ_CLS` adapters that save a trained classification head. Follow-up to #61033 (BERT/RoBERTa embedding models); same pattern as #58884.

## Claims

- `--enable-lora` works instead of failing with `... does not support LoRA yet.`
- PEFT adapters with a saved head (`modules_to_save=["classifier"]`) load and match transformers + PEFT. Backbone-only adapters match too.
- Without LoRA, outputs are unchanged.

## Validation

Tesla T4, main @ e0317b28c. Random PEFT adapters (r=8, `init_lora_weights=False`); saved heads are perturbed so they differ from the base head. Each pair is scored with `LLM.score`, vLLM fp16 vs transformers + PEFT (merged) fp32 on CPU, 4 query/document pairs.

| Model | Adapter | Max abs diff, base | Max abs diff, LoRA vs HF+PEFT | LoRA effect (HF) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ms-marco-MiniLM-L6-v2 (raw logits) | encoder q/k/v/dense + saved head | 0.0022 | 0.0027 | 13.53 |
| ms-marco-MiniLM-L6-v2 (raw logits) | encoder q/k/v/dense only | 0.0022 | 0.0110 | 7.25 |

- **On main:** the model fails at startup with `... does not support LoRA yet.`
- **With only `SupportsLoRA` added (no classifier change):** the saved-head adapter fails with `ValueError: Cannot load full module 'classifier': the model does not expose a unique ClassificationHeadWithLoRA.`
- **Existing tests,** each passing both before and after the change:
  - `tests/models/language/pooling/test_classification.py::test_bert_model_runner_v2`
  - `tests/models/test_registry.py`
  - `tests/models/test_initialization.py -k BertForSequenceClassification`
  - `tests/lora/test_sequence_classification.py`
  - `tests/models/language/pooling_mteb_test/test_cross_encoder.py`

The comparison script (adapter generation + vLLM vs HF+PEFT check) is ~150 lines; happy to share it or turn it into a `tests/lora` case if useful.

## Details

- **`classifier`: `nn.Linear` → `ReplicatedLinear(..., return_bias=False)`.** With the default `target_modules`, `LoRAModelManager` only wraps `LinearBase` modules (`is_supported_lora_module`). A plain `nn.Linear` classifier therefore never becomes a `ClassificationHeadWithLoRA`, and `_validate_modules_to_save` rejects saved heads. This matches how `as_seq_cls_model` builds `score`, and #60211 makes the same change for RoBERTa's head. BERT's head is a single linear, so this stays within the existing single-layer `modules_to_save` contract. Same weights, bias and `head_dtype`, so non-LoRA outputs are identical. The weight names are unchanged.
- **`packed_modules_mapping`:** `qkv_proj ← query/key/value`. BERT's vLLM module names already match HF, so no `hf_to_vllm_mapper` is needed.
- **`self.config`** is needed by the LoRA manager.
- **Limitation: `bert.pooler.dense` is not LoRA-wrapped,** because `BertPooler.dense` is a plain `nn.Linear`. An adapter that targets it loads and the pooler LoRA is dropped: max abs diff 0.42 vs HF on the pooler-targeting adapter. This is the same class of issue as RoBERTa's `classifier.dense` in #60211. Making it a `ReplicatedLinear` would apply token-indexed LoRA in a per-sequence stage, so I left it. Happy to follow the reviewers' preference: reject such adapters, or let BERT opt `bert.pooler.dense` in if `lora_classifier_modules` from #60211 lands.
- **ModernBERT left out on purpose:** #59206 moves `ModernBertForSequenceClassification` to the Transformers modeling backend and removes the native class, so I didn't touch it. The same change does work there (gte-reranker-modernbert-base on the same T4 setup: max abs diff 0.0002 with a saved head, 0.0014 encoder-only), and I'm happy to send it separately if that's useful before #59206 lands.
- **Scope and fallback:** this does not change `modules_to_save` or any shared LoRA code. It only makes this single-linear classifier eligible for the existing saved-head path. If maintainers prefer not to widen saved-head support for now (see the scope discussion on #60211), the `ReplicatedLinear` change can be dropped. That leaves backbone-only LoRA, as in #58884, which the "encoder only" rows above already validate.
- **No file overlap with #60211** (`vllm/lora/*`, `roberta.py`).
- **CI gap:** no new test. LoRA correctness needs a GPU and adapter checkpoints. Happy to add a `tests/lora` case if wanted.

items.title: [Model] Support MTP drafts in the Transformers modeling backend
items.body:
## Overview

Serve the MTP layers of any model that opts into the Transformers MTP standard (huggingface/transformers#46229) as a speculative decoding draft in the Transformers modeling backend.

Draft: depends on huggingface/transformers#49544, which adds the `MtpModel` helpers this uses (`forward_layer`, `get_mtp_weights_regex`, `get_weight_conversions`) so vLLM shares the per-layer logic and weight loading with Transformers instead of duplicating them. The minimum version is set to 5.20.0, assuming that PR lands in it.

## Claims

- `--speculative-config '{"method": "mtp", ...}'` works for targets on the Transformers backend whose config sets `num_mtp_layers` (`TransformersForMTP` / `TransformersMoEForMTP`)
- MTP weights are found and renamed by the same `MtpModel` helpers as `MtpModel.from_pretrained`, so new checkpoint layouts only need the Transformers-side mapping
- Multi-module MTP: `spec_step_idx` selects the MTP layer, so `num_speculative_tokens > 1` uses every checkpoint layer
- Covers DeepSeek-V3/R1 and GLM-4.5/4.6/4.7 today, and Mellum with huggingface/transformers#49531

## Validation

GLM-4.5-Air, B200, TP=4, gsm8k (before the `speculative.py` refactor and the switch to the `MtpModel` helpers; to re-run):

| Config | Native MTP | Transformers MTP |
| --- | --- | --- |
| n=1 acceptance | 95.9% | 95.8% |
| n=3 mean acceptance length | 3.13 | 3.15 |
| n=3 per-position acceptance | 95.3 / 76.1 / 41.6% | 95.3 / 76.6 / 42.7% |

Mellum (huggingface/transformers#49531 + #49468, before the switch to the helpers): on a tiny checkpoint in Mellum's `mtp.*` layout, the draft's MTP weights equal those loaded by `MtpModel.from_pretrained` (CPU).

Tiny Llama checkpoint with an appended MTP layer (CPU, against huggingface/transformers#49544): the draft builds as `TransformersForMTP` and its MTP weights load correctly.

```bash
pytest tests/models/transformers/test_backend.py -k mtp  # passed on B200
pytest tests/config/test_speculative_draft_hf_overrides.py tests/test_config.py -k "speculative or mtp or draft or hf_override"
# 98 passed, 1 failed (test_draft_model_enables_async_scheduling_by_default, also fails on main)
```
